But Tom does not like the pill. It is big and bitter. He spits it out when Mom is not looking. He hides it under his pillow. He thinks Mom will not know.

Mom comes back to check on Tom. She sees his pillow is wet. She lifts it up and finds the pill. She is angry and sad. She says to Tom, "Why did you spit out the pill? It is good for you. Do you want to be sick forever?"

Tom is scared. He says, "I'm sorry, Mom. I don't like the pill. It is yucky. Can I have something else?"

Mom sighs. She says, "No, Tom. You have to take the pill. It is the only thing that can help you. If you don't take it, you might get worse. You might lose your voice or your hearing. Do you want to be deaf?"

Tom shakes his head. He does not want to be deaf. He likes to hear Mom's voice and the birds and the music. He says, "OK, Mom. I will take the pill. But can you stay with me and read me a story?"

Mom smiles. She says, "Of course, Tom. I love you. I want you to be well. Come on, let's try again. Swallow the pill and I will read you your favorite story."

Tom nods. He takes the pill and drinks some water. He makes a face, but he does not spit it out. He lies down and cuddles with Mom. Mom reads him a story about a brave knight and a friendly dragon. Tom feels a little better. He closes his eyes and listens to Mom's voice. He falls asleep.

John and mum were walking around in the park. They saw a skull on the ground. John asked his mum what it was and she told him it was a skull. John wanted to take it home and keep it for himself. 

Mum was thoughtful about it and said it was okay to take it but they must take care of it. John was very happy he now owned the skull. 

They went home and John put the skull on a shelf. Every day John would wash and brush it, until it was nice and clean. 

John and mum talked every day about the skull, they thought of funny stories to tell it and asked it questions. 

John said he was the proud owner of the skull and he would take good care of it. He promised the skull it would have a long and happy life with him.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat. The cat wanted to climb up a tall tree. But it was too tough for the cat. So the cat had a plan. The cat found a hook on the ground and hoped it would help her climb the tree. 

The cat grabbed the hook in her mouth and started to climb the tree. She hooked the hook on different places and steadily went up, higher and higher. Finally, the cat made it to the top. She was so excited, she started to purr. 

The cat looked around, and saw that she was now at the tallest tree in the forest. She could see the sun, birds and other animals. She felt happy of her success. 

The moral of the story is if you work hard and never give up, you can reach the top.

Tom and Anna like to go to the park with Mom. They put on their hats and shoes and walk to the park. It is not far. They see many things on the way. They see a big dog, a red car, a yellow flower and a blue bird.

At the park, they play on the swings and the slide. They have fun. They see other kids and say hello. They share their toys and make new friends. The park is green and pretty. There are many trees and grass and flowers.

Mom calls them for a snack. They run to her and sit on a bench. She gives them juice and cookies. They say thank you and eat. They are happy. They love the park. They love Mom. They smile and hug. They are a good family.

Timmy was walking in the garden when he found a ball of yarn. He was excited and tried to take it away with him. His mom saw him and said, â€œNo, Timmy, thatâ€™s not yours. Give it back.â€ Timmy was naughty and didnâ€™t want to do it, so he started to run away with the yarn in his hand.

His mom called to him, â€œTimmy, remember your manners. Give that yarn back.â€ But Timmy wanted to keep it. So, he started to run even faster.

Suddenly, a bird flew by and grabbed the yarn from Timmyâ€™s hand. Timmy was surprised and did not know what to do. His mom came to him and hugged him. She said, â€œTimmy, remember why itâ€™s important to share.â€

Timmy felt bad and hugged his mom. He said he was sorry and promised to remember to share next time. His mom smiled and said, â€œGood job remembering, Timmy!â€

Once upon a time, there was a barn. Inside the barn was a secret, it was hidden. It was a room full of special things.

 Josie and her brother, Jack, went to see what was inside. It was full of toys! Toys of all shapes, sizes and colors!

They ran around picking up toys and playing with each other loud. After a while, Josie and Jack had to put the toys back into the hidden room. They put them away in boxes, shelves and drawers. When they were finished, the room was almost as neat as before!

Josie and Jack ran outside to tell everyone what they found. They said the barn had a secret room filled with toys. Everyone was excited and wanted to go! 

Now, every weekend, Josie, Jack and their friends go to the barn to store their toys in the hidden room and have lots of fun!

Amy and her mom were walking in the park. Amy saw a chicken and pointed to it. She said, "Mommy, look! A chicken!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, a chicken."

Suddenly Amy's face frowned. "What's wrong?" her mom asked. Amy said, "The chicken is hungry." Her mom looked around and said, "That's a great idea! Let's get some food for the chicken."

They walked over to a nearby store and picked up some chicken feed. Then they went back to feed the chicken. When the chicken heard Amy and her mom coming, it ran over and started eating the food. Amy smiled.

"The chicken looks very happy now, doesn't it?" her mom asked. Amy nodded in agreement.

"Yes, it is great!" she said. Amy and her mom smiled and shared a hug.

Once upon a time, a jolly daughter was playing in her backyard. She saw a big ball and wanted to play with it. She tried to kick the ball, but she fell down. She stood up and tried again, but she fell down again. She needed to balance better to play with the ball. So, she held her arms out to balance and kicked the ball. She was so happy that she could play with the ball without falling down.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to succeed. Every day she tried her best, but she just couldn't seem to get it right. She started to feel very sad.

One day, she got a special present. It was a lovely high vest. She put it on and felt so proud. The vest made her feel so brave and strong.

She decided that now was her chance and gave it her all. She put her head down and worked hard. Then, finally she did it! She had succeeded.

The little girl celebrated so much. She was so happy that she had succeeded. She wore her high vest every day for a long time afterwards, to remind her of her success.

Bobthe elephant was walking in the jungle, looking for something to eat. He was very hungry. He was so hungry he could feel it in his trunk. Suddenly he spotted a banana tree. Bob blinked in surprise. He walked towards the banana tree and began to eat the ripe, yellow bananas. He munched on the sweet fruit until his appetite was satisfied. He was feeling very fine now and he was ready to continue walking through the jungle.

He walked through the tall grass, looking around and blinking at the trees and animals. Suddenly he heard a loud thump! Bob blinked in surprise and peered around. He spotted a trunk lying in the grass and wondered what it could be. He cautiously walked towards it, sniffing as he went. It smelled like a trunk, but it was too small for an elephant. Bob bent down to look closer and saw that it belonged to a baby elephant!

Bob wrinkled his trunk in surprise and carefully picked up the trunk. He saw that the little elephant was just fine. He placed the trunk around the baby's body and held it there while the baby happily wiggled her trunk. As he walked away with the baby elephant in tow, Bob smiled and blinked in relief.

Once there was a boy who liked to play outside. One cold winter day, the boy's mom was giving him his jacket so he could go and play. As the boy put his jacket on, he noticed something outside the window. It was snowing! He was so excited that he ran outside and looked around. The ground was covered in a thick, icy layer of snow.

The boy started to scatter the snow around with his feet. He had so much fun! He noticed a rubber ball in the snow, so he picked it up and started running around with it.

The boy found it fun to throw the rubber ball against the icy walls of his house. The ball bounced off it and landed in the snow again. The boy ran to grab the ball, and started to scatter the snow around again with his feet. The boy had so much fun that he wanted to keep playing until dinnertime.

Mommy and Daddy wanted to buy a mattress. It was silly how many mattresses were in the store! Mommy and Daddy looked at all the mattresses. They wanted to find the best one. 

Finally, Mommy and Daddy chose a soft, warm mattress. It was so perfect! They bought the mattress and stowed it in the car. 

But when they got home, they realized the mattress was too big to fit in the bedroom! So they stowed it in the living room and used it to sleep on. 

Mommy and Daddy had lots of fun while they slept on the silly mattress. In the mornings, they made funny shapes out of the mattress and pretended the living room was a jungle. 

Mommy and Daddy always enjoy silly mattress days!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a mop that she loved to play with. One day, Lily's mom gifted her a big box of chocolates. Lily was so happy and excited to eat them all.

But then, she had to decide whether to eat them all by herself or share them with her friends. Lily decided to eat them all by herself, because she wanted to keep them all for herself.

However, Lily ate too much chocolate and got very sick. She had to go to the hospital and couldn't play with her mop anymore. From then on, Lily learned that sharing is important and that being gifted with something special also means being responsible with it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys in the bathtub. One day, she accidentally dropped her favorite toy boat in the sink and it broke.

Lily was sad and went to her mommy. "Mommy, my boat is broken. Can you repair it please?" she asked.

Her mommy said, "Of course, I can fix it for you. Let's go to the charming toy store and find a new boat for you to play with while I repair your old one."

Lily was so happy and hugged her mommy. They went to the toy store and found a new boat that was even better than the old one. When they got home, her mommy repaired the old boat and Lily had two boats to play with in the bathtub. She was very happy and thanked her mommy for being so kind.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Penny. Penny was three years old and she was always very curious. Today, she decided to explore in her mum's room. 

Penny found a piece of paper and it looked very fascinating to her. She carefully picked it up and wanted to fit it in her tiny pocket. But it was too big and it wouldn't fit.

Penny started to get sad and she said "I want to keep it! Its very tasty!" Her Mum heard her and came into the room. She said "Its alright, Penny. You can keep it!"

Penny was so excited and she thanked her Mum. With the help of her Mum, she managed to fold the paper and it fit nicely into her pocket. She happily skipped out of the room, still holding her piece of tasty paper.

Once upon a time there was a lady called Maria who needed a stove. She searched and searched, but she couldn't find one. Everywhere she looked, none of the stoves were perfect.

One day, Maria came across a strange shop with an old stove in the window. She looked and looked, and it seemed perfect. She went inside and asked the shopkeeper if she could buy it. "Yes," the shopkeeper said. "It's perfect for you!"

So, Maria bought the stove and she took it home. She put it in the kitchen and it looked just like she wanted. From that day on, she always cooked perfect meals with her perfect stove.

Maria was so happy she had found the perfect stove. She never had to search again. She had everything she needed.

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toys and wear their vests. Their vests are blue and have a big star on the front. They are the same, but Ben and Mia are different. Ben likes to run and jump and make noise. Mia likes to draw and sing and be quiet.

One day, Ben and Mia are playing in the yard. Ben sees a big rock and kicks it hard. The rock flies and hits Mia's vest. Mia's vest rips and the star falls off. Mia is sad and cries.

"Look what you did!" Mia says to Ben. "You broke my vest! It was my favorite!"

"I'm sorry, Mia," Ben says. "I didn't mean to. It was an accident."

Ben feels bad and wants to make Mia happy. He thinks of a way to repair her vest. He runs inside and gets some glue and some paper. He cuts out a new star from the paper and glues it on Mia's vest. He also draws some flowers and hearts around the star. He brings the vest to Mia and shows her.

"Here, Mia," Ben says. "I fixed your vest. I made it different, but I hope you like it."

Mia looks at her vest and smiles. She sees the new star and the flowers and the hearts. She thinks it is pretty and special. She hugs Ben and thanks him.

"Thank you, Ben," Mia says. "You are a good brother. I like my vest. It is different, but I love it."

Ben and Mia are happy and play together. They wear their vests and show them to their mom and dad. Their mom and dad are proud of them and tell them they are both wonderful. Ben and Mia are twins. They are the same, but they are different. And they love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, while they were playing, Lily saw a bird sitting on a tree. The bird was singing a beautiful song. Lily wanted to get closer to the bird without scaring it away. So, she whispered to her friends to be quiet and not make any noise. 

Lily was very alert and careful as she slowly walked towards the bird. When she got close enough, she smiled at the bird and the bird smiled back at her. Lily was so happy that she had made a new friend. From that day on, Lily would visit the park every day to see her bird friend. They would sing and play together, and Lily would always remember to whisper and be very alert so as not to scare away her feathered friend.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jake who wanted to go on an adventure. He was very cheerful and couldn't wait to explore. So, he grabbed his bags, gave his Mum a big hug and ran out the door. He was ready to go!

Jake hurried down the street, past the park and across a bridge. He was getting very tired so he decided to take a break. Up ahead he saw a big, tall building - it was a hotel! Jake was so excited he ran as fast as he could. 

When he arrived at the hotel, he was surprised to find that the lobby was very crowded. Everyone was smiling and laughing - they were very cheerful. Jake made lots of new friends and had lots of fun.

Finally it was time to go home. Jake said goodbye to his new friends and hurried off back where he came from. He had had a wonderful adventure and couldn't wait for his next one!

One day, a lazy gorilla decided to make a new friend. He looked around and saw a little boy sitting near the zoo. The gorilla walked over to him.

"Hi, who are you?" said the gorilla.

"My name is Mike," said the little boy, smiling.

"Do you want to be friends?" asked the gorilla.

"Yes!" said Mike.

So the lazy gorilla and Mike played together every day. They would climb trees and swing from vines. Mike even fed the gorilla bananas every once in a while.

After a few months, the gorilla and Mike became the best of friends. Whenever Mike was feeling lazy, the gorilla would give him a big hug and it always made him feel better. 

From that day on, the lazy gorilla and the little boy were always happy to be together.

Joe was excited. He was going to the park to borrow his friend's kite. When he got to the park, he saw his friend. He was giving a lively lecture about the birds and bees. Joe was fascinated. After the lecture, Joe and his friend grabbed the kite and flew it in the air. It whirred happily and cheerfully. They flew the kite for what felt like forever before putting it away. Joe waved goodbye and as he walked away, he knew he had learned something special that day. He was happy he was able to borrow his friend's kite and listen to a lively lecture.

Tim and Kim are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun.

One day, they see a big hole in the ground. It is a pit. They are curious. They want to look inside.

"Be careful," Tim says. "The pit is deep and dark. We might fall in."

"Don't worry," Kim says. "I have a flashlight. I can see what is in the pit."

Kim turns on the flashlight and shines it into the pit. She sees something shiny and wet. It is water.

"Look, Tim," Kim says. "There is water in the pit. Maybe we can drink it. I am thirsty."

"I don't know," Tim says. "The water might be dirty or bad. It is not regular water. It is pit water."

Kim does not listen. She leans over the pit and reaches for the water. She slips and falls in. She screams.

"Help, Tim, help!" Kim cries. "The water is cold and yucky. It tastes like mud. Get me out!"

Tim is scared. He grabs a rope from the slide and throws it to Kim. He pulls her out of the pit. She is wet and dirty.

"I am sorry, Tim," Kim says. "You were right. The pit water is not good to drink. It is gross. I should have listened to you."

"It's okay, Kim," Tim says. "I am glad you are safe. Come on, let's go home. We can drink some regular water there. And maybe some juice."

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a big post in the ground. It was a rare post, with a funny face on it. Tim wanted to act like the face on the post.

Tim made a face like the post and said, "Hi, I am a funny post!" A girl named Sue saw Tim and laughed. She said, "You look funny, Tim!" Tim felt happy that Sue liked his act.

But then, a mean boy named Tom came over. He did not like Tim's act. Tom said, "You look silly, Tim!" Tim felt sad. Sue said, "Don't be mean, Tom!" Tom left, and Tim and Sue played together, acting like the rare post and having fun.

Once upon a time, there was a small child. The child loved to play with toys and run around. One day, the child went outside to play and saw a small bird. The child wanted to play with the bird, so the child called out to the bird. 

The bird came and played with the child. They had so much fun together. But the child didn't know that the bird had a family. The bird's family was looking for the bird and couldn't find it. 

When the bird's family finally found the bird playing with the child, they were so happy. But they were also angry that the child had taken the bird away from them. The bird's family took the bird back and flew away. The child was sad and missed the bird.

Once there was a beautiful blueberry bush. Every day different kinds of animals would come to visit the bush.

One day, a rabbit hopped over to the bush. The rabbit was feeling very thirsty. He spotted a big, juicy blueberry and quickly ate it.
 
Suddenly, the blueberry started to shrink! The rabbit was very confused.

The rabbit hopped over to a nearby fox. "What can you tell me about this blueberry?" the rabbit asked. 

The fox replied, "That blueberry is very different, it shrinks when you eat it!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane loved to explore the world around her. One day, she went for a walk in the woods. As she walked, she felt something soft and wet under her thumb. She picked it up and saw that it was a slug! It was crawling very slow and Jane watched it go.

Jane held the slug in her hands, feeling its slimy skin. She was so curious! She held the slug closer to her and looked at it up close. She noticed the slug had two big eyes, which looked a bit scary but also kind of cute.

The slug slowly moved away and went back on the ground. Jane smiled as she watched it move away slowly. She put her thumb on her nose and waved goodbye to the slug. Jane waved as the slug went away slowly.

She watched the slug until it was gone and she felt happy. Jane smiled and went home, feeling excited to share her adventure with her family.

Anna loves to read books. She likes to look at the pictures and the words on the pages. She has many books in her room, but her favorite one is about a princess and a dragon.

One day, Anna wants to read her favorite book to her little brother, Ben. She finds the book on her shelf and sits on the floor with Ben. She opens the book and starts to read.

"Once upon a time, there was a princess who lived in a castle. She was very kind and brave, but she was also very stubborn. She always wanted to do things her way."

Ben listens to Anna for a while, but he gets bored. He does not like the princess. He likes the dragon. He wants to see the dragon. He grabs the book from Anna and flips the pages.

"Stop it, Ben!" Anna says. "You are ruining the book! You have to read it from the beginning!"

"No, I don't!" Ben says. "I want to see the dragon! The dragon is cool! The princess is boring!"

Anna and Ben start to fight over the book. They pull and tug and shout. The book rips in half. The pages fly everywhere. Anna and Ben stop fighting. They look at the book. They feel sad.

"I'm sorry, Anna," Ben says. "I didn't mean to rip your book."

"I'm sorry, too, Ben," Anna says. "I should have let you see the dragon."

They hug each other. They pick up the pages and try to put them back together. They decide to share the book and take turns reading. They learn that the princess and the dragon become friends at the end. They smile and say, "We love this book!"

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious hat. A small bunny wanted to find out what it was. He was brave, so he hopped up and touched it with his paw. But suddenly, the hat started to rot! The bunny was so surprised, he hopped away. He couldn't believe what happened.

The bunny went to get his friend, a fox. The fox wanted to figure out why the hat was rotting. He sniffed it and said, "Maybe it was too old?" The bunny was confused. He had never seen anything like it before. 

The two friends decided to find the owner of the mysterious hat. So, they set off on an adventure. Along the way, they met a friendly bear. The bear said he knew the owner of the hat. The fox and the bunny were excited! 

Eventually, they came to a large cave. The bear told them to wait outside while he went inside. A few minutes later, the bear came out with an old man. The old man was the owner of the mysterious, rotting hat! 

The bunny and the fox were so relieved. They thanked the bear for his help, and promised to visit him again soon. Then the bunny and the fox said goodbye to the old man and continued on their journey.

Once upon a time, there was a big palace. It seemed very pretty and shiny. A little girl named Lily wanted to go inside and see what was in there. She walked closer and closer to the palace.

Suddenly, a scary dragon appeared! The dragon seemed angry and Lily got very scared. She tried to run away, but the dragon chased her. Lily tripped and fell, hurting her leg. The dragon came closer and closer until Lily was too scared to move.

The dragon took Lily to his cave and she never saw her family again. The big palace seemed like a good idea, but it was too dangerous.

One day, a girl named Lily and a boy named Tom were playing in their room. They liked to watch videos on their big TV. Their favorite video was about a big, impressive dog that could do many tricks.

Lily began to tease Tom, saying, "I bet you can't do tricks like the big dog in the video!" Tom laughed and said, "I can try!"

Tom tried to do a trick like the big dog. He jumped and spun in the air. Lily clapped and laughed. "That was fun!" she said. Tom smiled and said, "I want to try another trick!"

They spent the whole day trying to do tricks like the big, impressive dog in the video. They laughed and had a lot of fun together. And even though they couldn't do all the tricks, they were happy to play and tease each other.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy cloud. He liked to stay alone in the sky and had never been very friendly. Every day he would look down at the world with a grumpy face; nothing seemed to excite him.

One day the grumpy cloud noticed something happening in the meadow below. There was a family of rabbits playing and having fun. It made the grumpy cloud excited. He had never seen anything like it before.

The grumpy cloud watched the family of rabbits playing in the meadow. He was so excited that he started to smile. He was still grumpy but now he was happy too!

The grumpy cloud was so excited that he decided to join the family of rabbits and show them his smile. Everyone was so surprised but so very happy! From then on, the grumpy cloud was never grumpy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She liked to take things from the house. One day, when no one was looking, she took a knife from the kitchen drawer. It was a nice knife and it was very shiny. The little girl wanted to play with it. She ran outside, into the dark and far away woods. Suddenly, she felt scared. It was too dark and she couldn't find her way home. 

Just then, she heard an old wise voice coming from the trees. It said "Don't take things that don't belong to you, it will get you into trouble". The voice was right - the little girl was lost and she didn't know how to get home. 

The little girl was very sad and she put away the knife. Suddenly, a beam of light came down from the sky and it showed the little girl the way home. She was happy to find her way back and she never took things that didn't belong to her ever again. 

The moral of the story is that you should never take things that don't belong to you. You never know where it could lead you.

Once there was a beautiful princess named Daisy. Daisy loved her family and had a very strong urge to marry. One day, Daisy's mother told her she ought to marry very soon. She was excited, but worried.

Daisy went outside to her favourite spot. While she was thinking, a rude man came to her. He began asking her to marry him. Daisy was scared; she knew he was not a nice person. She didn't like how he talked and quickly ran away.

The next day, Daisy's mother realised that the rude man had been a prince. He had come to her spot because he had heard Daisy wanted to marry. Daisy was very sad. She had wanted to marry, but not to someone so rude.

The day of Daisy's wedding came. When the doors opened, Daisy's heart skipped a beat. Standing in the doorway was the same prince from the day before. He had come to propose with all of his respect, and Daisy was finally able to marry the prince she had always wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a small taxi. The taxi was not very big, but it was very modest. One day, the man went for a ride in his taxi. He drove around the town and saw many things. He saw a big park, a tall building and many people walking on the street.

After some time, the man decided to release a bird that he had in a cage. The bird was very happy to be free and flew away. The man felt happy too because he knew the bird was now free to fly wherever it wanted. The man then drove his taxi back home and went to sleep. The end.

Timmy was an active three year old. He enjoyed playing outside in the sun. One day, he went out and found something dull in his hand. It looked like a funny rock. He enjoyed feeling its rough surface. He twirled it around and around in his hands. 

The rock had a funny smell and Timmy thought it was special. He enjoyed picking it up and moving it close to his face. He looked at it for a long time, imagining all kinds of shapes and colours. 

Finally, he put it in his pocket and ran to tell his mum. She said the rock was an old fossil. Timmy smiled and said that he would always enjoy keeping it with him.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very intelligent. One day her mom asked her if she'd like to go to a picnic. The little girl thought it would be fun, so she said yes.

On the way to the picnic, the little girl asked her mom lots of questions. She wanted to know all about the picnic, like where it was, who was coming, and what they were going to do. Her mom answered all of the little girl's questions.

When they arrived, there were lots of people at the picnic. Everyone had fun playing games, eating food and talking. The little girl was very happy. She talked and laughed with the other kids and asked lots of questions about the picnic.

At the end of the day, the little girl was tired but very satisfied. It had been a great day and she couldn't wait to go to another picnic again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. One day, she started to wonder what was under her bed. She tip-toed over to the bed and peaked underneath. Suddenly, she saw something long and scary!

Jane jumped back and shouted, "It's a monster!" Jane was so scared that she ran to the other side of the room and hid behind the chair.

The monster crept out from under the bed. He was very gentle and said, "Don't be scared. I'm just looking for my lost ball." Jane looked at the monster and asked, "Where did you lose your ball?" The monster replied, "I'm not sure. I think it might have rolled under your bed."

So, Jane and the monster searched under the bed together. Soon, they found the ball and the monster said, "Thank you for helping me find my ball." 

As Jane watched the monster's big tail wiggle away, she began to wonder what else was under her bed.

Once upon a time there was an otter. He was so fast that he could run faster than any of the other animals in the forest. 

One day, he was running in the forest and he noticed a very long log. It was so big he could hardly believe it! So he decided he wanted to race the log. 

The otter said to the log, "I'm going to race you, let's see who can get to the end first!" 

The log replied, "I'm a log so I can't really run. But I can roll. So if I roll, can I still race you?" 

The otter thought about it for a moment and said, "Yes, if you roll on the ground we can both race and see who gets to the end first!" 

So the otter and the log started their race. The otter ran as fast as he could and the log rolled as fast as it could. In the end, the otter won the race and the log was very proud of its long race.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the woods behind their house. They liked to climb trees, make forts and look for animals. One day, they found a big pile of lumber near a path. It was wood that someone had cut from the trees.

"Wow, look at all this lumber!" Tim said. "We can use it to make a bigger fort!"

"Or a boat!" Sam said. "Or a bridge!"

They ran to the pile and started to pick up some pieces. But then they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you kids! Get away from my lumber!" It was a man who came out of a small hut. He looked angry and had a big saw in his hand.

"Who are you?" Tim asked. "Why do you have so much lumber?"

"None of your business!" the man said. "This is my lumber and you can't touch it! Go away or I'll call the police!"

Tim and Sam were scared. They dropped the lumber and ran back to the path. They wondered who the man was and why he was so mean. He was a mysterious man who did not like to share.

They decided to go home and tell their mom what they saw. Maybe she would know more about the man and his lumber. They hoped he would not come after them. They also hoped he would yield some of his lumber to other people who needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a birdie. The birdie loved to fly high up in the sky. One day, the birdie saw a flashlight on the ground. It was broken and didn't work. The birdie picked up the flashlight in its beak and flew away.

As the birdie continued to soar in the sky, it saw a little boy who was sad. The birdie knew just what to do. It flew down to the boy and gave him the broken flashlight. The boy was happy to have the flashlight, even though it didn't work.

The birdie continued to soar in the sky, feeling happy that it could help the little boy. From that day on, the birdie always looked out for things that might make someone happy, like a broken flashlight that could still bring a smile to someone's face.

Lily liked to look at photos of her family. She had a big book with many photos. Some photos were old and some were new. The old photos were black and white. The new photos were colorful. Lily liked the colorful photos more. They looked modern and happy.

One day, Lily wanted to show her photos to her friend Tom. She took the big book and went to Tom's house. Tom was happy to see Lily and the book. They sat on the floor and opened the book. They saw photos of Lily's mom and dad, her brother and sister, her grandparents and cousins. They saw photos of birthdays, holidays, trips and fun times.

But when they turned the page, they saw something bad. The photos were wet and sticky. Lily was sad and angry. She remembered that yesterday she left the book on the table. She also remembered that her brother spilled his juice on the table. He did not tell anyone. He did not dry the table. He did not dry the book. He ruined the photos.

Lily cried and Tom tried to comfort her. He said they could try to dry the photos with a hairdryer. He said they could try to make new photos with his camera. He said they could try to make the book look modern and happy again. Lily liked Tom's ideas. She stopped crying and smiled. She thanked Tom for being a good friend. They went to find a hairdryer and a camera. They hoped the photos would be okay.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a unique room with pink walls and a big bed. Lily loved to play with her dolls and read books in her room. 

One day, Lily's mom told her they were moving to a new house. Lily was sad because she hoped she could keep her unique room forever. But when they arrived at the new house, Lily was surprised to see that her new room was even better than her old one! 

It had a big window with a view of the garden and a cozy bed with fluffy pillows. Lily was so happy and felt grateful for her new room. She hugged her mom and said, "I hope we can live here forever!"

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks. They want to build a big tower. They take turns to put blocks on top of each other. They are careful not to make the tower fall.

"Look, Anna, I have a blue block. It is very pretty. Where can I put it?" Ben asks.

"Let me see, Ben. Maybe you can put it here, next to the yellow block. It will fit well," Anna says.

Ben tries to put the blue block next to the yellow block. But the blue block is too big. It does not fit. It pushes the yellow block and makes the tower wobble.

"Oh no, Ben, the tower is going to fall!" Anna cries.

They both try to catch the tower, but it is too late. The tower falls down with a loud noise. The blocks scatter all over the floor. Anna and Ben are sad. They worked hard to build the tower.

"Sorry, Anna, it is my fault. I should have found a smaller block," Ben says.

"It is okay, Ben. It was an accident. We can build the tower again. But first, we have to clean up the mess," Anna says.

They start to pick up the blocks and put them back in the box. But they cannot find the blue block. It is hidden somewhere.

"Where is the blue block, Anna? I cannot see it," Ben says.

"Me neither, Ben. Maybe it rolled under the sofa. Let us look there," Anna says.

They go to the sofa and lift the cushion. They find the blue block, but they also find something else. It is a mark on the wall. A big, red mark. It looks like someone drew on the wall with a crayon.

"Uh-oh, Anna, look at that. Who made that mark?" Ben says.

"I do not know, Ben. Maybe it was Max, the cat. He likes to play with crayons," Anna says.

"Or maybe it was you, Anna. You like to draw, too," Ben says.

"Or maybe it was you, Ben. You like to make funny shapes," Anna says.

They look at each other and start to giggle. They do not want to tell the truth. They both made the mark. They did it when Mom was not looking. They thought it was fun. But now they are in trouble.

"Maybe we can hide the mark, Anna. Maybe we can put the sofa in front of it," Ben says.

"Good idea, Ben. Let us try that," Anna says.

They push the sofa to cover the mark. But the sofa is too heavy. It does not move. They try harder, but they only make more noise.

"What are you doing, kids?" Mom says. She comes into the room and sees the mess. She sees the fallen tower, the blocks on the floor, and the mark on the wall. She is not happy.

"Anna, Ben, what is this? Who made this mark?" Mom says.

Anna and Ben look at each other. They do not know what to say. They are sorry. They do not want to lie. They do not want to blame each other. They do not want to make Mom angry.

They decide to tell the truth.

"We did, Mom. We are sorry. We were playing with blocks and crayons. We wanted to make a big tower and a big picture. But we made a big mess. We did not mean to. We tried to fix it. We tried to fit the blue block and hide the mark. But we could not. We are sorry, Mom. Please do not be mad at us," Anna and Ben say.

Mom sighs. She is not happy, but she is not mad either. She loves Anna and Ben. She knows they are good kids. They made a mistake, but they told the truth. They are sorry, and they want to help.

"It is okay, kids. I am not mad at you. I am glad you told me the truth. But you have to be more careful. You cannot draw on the wall. It is not nice. It is hard to clean. And you have to pick up your toys. They can hurt someone. They can make a mess. Do you understand?" Mom says.

"Yes, Mom. We understand. We are sorry. We will help you clean. We will not draw on the wall again. We will pick up our toys. We will be good," Anna and Ben say.

Mom smiles. She hugs Anna and Ben. She is proud of them. They are good kids. They learned a lesson. They will do better next time.

"Thank you, kids. I love you. Now, let us clean up this mess. And then, we can have a snack. And maybe, we can build a tower together. A

Once upon a time there was a little pig who was very excited for sunrise. He was outside his house looking for something to mark. He saw a big rock and decided it was perfect for marking. He picked up a big stick and marked a smiley face on the rock. The pig was so proud of his work.

Just then a bird came flying by and noticed the rock with the smiley face. "That is such an amazing thing to mark. Where did you learn to do it?" asked the bird.

The little pig was so excited to explain. "I learned it all by myself! I just wanted to make something special for the upcoming sunrise," he said.

The bird was very impressed and flew away. The little pig smiled and knew that the smiley face would cheer up the sunrise.

One day, Tom was feeling very lonely. He had no one to play with and he was sad. So he decided to have a picnic all by himself. He got a big piece of cake from the kitchen and went to the nearby park.

When Tom arrived he saw a big blanket on the grass. He sat down and started to rub the blanket. It felt so soft! Then he took out his cake and it smelled so good! He was so excited that he started to rub the cake with his hands.

Suddenly, a very rare bird flew down and landed on the blanket. It was beautiful! It had colorful feathers and a big beak. Tom was so happy and he started to rub the bird gently. The bird stayed still and let Tom rub it. Then the bird flew away, but Tom was still so happy that he had met such a rare bird. 

Tom finished his picnic and he was no longer lonely. He realized that sometimes all you need is a little adventure and a delicious cake!

Once upon a time there was a humble old lady who lived alone. She called out to her cat every day and the cat always replied back with her meow. 

One day the old lady was hungry and decided to make herself a special treat. She made a warm cake with a sweet, delicious taste. She called out to her cat, "Come try it with me!"

The cat came running right away, eager to try the cake. The old lady gave the cat a small piece and the cat licked it with delight! 

"It's so yummy!" said the cat. The old lady smiled and said "I'm glad you like it! Please tell all your friends so that they can taste it too!" 

The cat was so happy and ran off to tell her friends. Everyone loved the old lady's cake and thanked her for her humble kindness.  Ever since then, the old lady and her cat could always be seen enjoying their cake together.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they always wanted more. They did not like to share or say thank you to anyone. One day, their mom told them they were going to visit their grandma for Thanksgiving. Tom and Lily were not happy. They did not want to leave their toys or see their grandma.

When they got to grandma's house, they saw a big turkey on the table. It smelled good, but Tom and Lily did not care. They ran to the living room and looked for toys. They found some old books and puzzles, but they did not like them. They threw them on the floor and made a lot of noise. Grandma heard them and came to see what was wrong. She was sad to see the mess and the rude twins.

She said, "Tom and Lily, why are you so noisy and mean? Don't you know that Thanksgiving is a time to be thankful and kind? You should be happy to see me and enjoy the food I made for you. You should also respect the toys I have, even if they are not new. They are special to me, because they remind me of your mom and dad when they were little. They used to play with them and say thank you to me. They were good and sweet children. You should learn from them."

Tom and Lily felt ashamed. They realized they had been selfish and ungrateful. They said sorry to grandma and helped her clean up the mess. They hugged her and said thank you for the turkey and the toys. They also said thank you to their mom and dad for bringing them to grandma's house. They decided to be more thankful and kind from then on. They ate the turkey with grandma and enjoyed the books and puzzles. They had a happy Thanksgiving after all.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They wanted to go on an adventure and explore something new. With a blanket, lunch, and water bottles, they set out on a trail.

The path was long and bumpy, but the friends were having fun. Suddenly, the trail got very dark, and the friends felt very scared.

They kept walking and soon arrived at the entrance of a cave. At the entrance was a big sign that said, "Warning: Do Not Enter. It's very dangerous in here." But the friends were brave and decided to enter anyway.

Inside, the cave was terrible. There were dangerous animals and creepy caves. The friends started to get very scared, and they quickly decided it was time to go back home. They ran as fast as they could until they were back at the cave entrance.

The friends stopped, panted and caught their breath. Then they slowly closed the entrance of the cave. They were glad to be out of the terrible place, and together, the two friends made their way home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, beautiful firework. It was so pretty that one day, a child decided to design it. The child took special care to make the firework look special. But then, one careless moment changed everything! The child got too close to the firework and there was a big BANG! The firework exploded and the child was very scared. Thankfully, no one was hurt and the child learned an important lesson - never be careless around firework. The end.

One day, Sammy was walking down the street and saw something green. He ran over to it and discovered it was a classroom! He peeked inside and saw a kind teacher inside.

"Hi there!" said the teacher.

"Hi!" said Sammy.

"Would you like to come inside?" asked the teacher.

"Yes!" said Sammy and jumped inside. He looked around and the classroom was filled with fun toys and books.

The teacher smiled. "Would you like me to bring you a snack?"

"Yes please!" said Sammy, and the teacher went to the kitchen and brought back a yummy snack.

Sammy was so happy and ate his snack with a big smile on his face. He had a wonderful time in the green classroom.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy. His name was James. He was three years old.

One day, he said to his mom, "Mommy, I remembered something!" His mom asked, "What do you remember?" 

James replied, "I remember a black rhinoceros!" His mom was surprised. She asked, "Where did you see one?"

James said, "I saw it today when I was playing in the park. It was very big! I was scared." 

His mom smiled and said, "That's amazing that you remember it, James. Rhinos are special animals." 

Then James smiled and said, "I will always remember the big, black rhinoceros."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big birthday party coming up and his mom had an important job for him. She asked him to cut the cake and put candles on it. Timmy was so excited to help his mom. 

He got a big knife and started to cut the cake. It was a big cake, but Timmy was strong. He cut it into many pieces. After that, he put candles on the cake. There were ten candles, one for each year of his age. 

When the party started, Timmy's mom brought out the cake. Everyone sang "Happy Birthday" and Timmy blew out the candles. He was so happy that he could help his mom. From that day on, Timmy knew that he was an important part of his family.

Lily was a very independent girl. She liked to do things by herself, without asking for help. She had a big box of toys in her room, and she loved to play with them. She had dolls, cars, blocks, and a shiny gold key.

One day, she decided to lock her door with the gold key. She thought it would be fun to have her own secret place, where no one could bother her. She turned the key in the lock and heard a click. Then she smiled and went to play with her toys.

But after a while, she got bored. She wanted to go outside and see her friends. She wanted to have a snack and a drink. She wanted to hug her mom and dad. She tried to open the door, but it was locked. She tried to turn the key, but it was stuck. She started to cry.

She heard a knock on the door. It was her mom. "Lily, are you okay? Why did you lock the door?" she asked.

"I wanted to be independent," Lily sobbed. "But now I can't get out. I'm sorry, mom. Please help me."

Her mom called her dad, and they got a tool to open the door. They hugged Lily and told her they loved her. They also told her that being independent is good, but sometimes you need to ask for help and share with others. Lily learned her lesson. She never locked her door again. She played with her toys, but also with her friends and family. She was happy and independent, but not alone.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toy truck. They pretended to be mailmen and deliver letters and packages to their friends. One day, they found a shiny copper coin on the road. They thought it was very pretty and wanted to keep it.

"Let's deliver this coin to someone who will like it," Tom said.

"Who will like it?" Lily asked.

"Maybe Mr. Fox. He is smart and knows many things. He lives in the big house at the end of the street," Tom said.

"OK, let's go," Lily said.

They put the coin in their truck and drove to Mr. Fox's house. They knocked on the door and waited. Mr. Fox opened the door and saw the twins.

"Hello, Tom and Lily. What do you have for me?" he asked.

"We have a copper coin for you. We found it on the road. We think you will like it," Tom said.

"Thank you, that is very kind of you. Come in, I have something for you too," Mr. Fox said.

He smiled and invited them inside. Tom and Lily followed him, happy to see what he had for them. They did not know that Mr. Fox was not a nice mailman, but a greedy and hungry fox. He locked the door behind them and grabbed them with his sharp teeth. He ate them up and took their coin. He was very pleased with his meal and his treasure. He did not care that Tom and Lily were gone. He was a bad fox.

Once upon a time, there was a generous rabbit named Bobo. He lived in a small house in the woods. One day, he saw a little bird named Lulu who could not fly.

Bobo asked Lulu, "Why can't you fly?" Lulu said, "I suffer from a hurt wing. I can't find the exit from the woods."

Bobo wanted to help Lulu. He said, "Come with me. I will show you the exit." Lulu was happy and said, "Thank you, Bobo."

Bobo and Lulu walked together through the woods. They found the exit and Lulu could go home. Lulu thanked Bobo for his help. They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around. One day, she was playing with her friends when she fell and hurt her knee. She cried and cried because it hurt so much.

Her mom came over and said, "Oh no, what happened? Let's get you inside and rest your knee." Lily's mom picked her up and carried her inside. She put a treat on the table and said, "Here, have a cookie. It will make you feel better."

Lily took a bite of the cookie and felt a little better, but her knee still hurt. She said to her mom, "I'm not comfortable. My knee still hurts." Her mom said, "I understand. Let's put some ice on it and then you can rest on the couch." Lily nodded and her mom put some ice on her knee. She felt better and soon fell asleep on the couch.

Sara and Ben are hungry. They want to eat pasta for lunch. Mom is cooking pasta in a big pot. She says, "Pasta will be ready soon. You can help me set the table."

Sara and Ben run to the kitchen. They get plates, forks, spoons, and napkins. They put them on the table. They are happy. They love pasta.

Mom says, "Pasta is done. Be careful, it is hot. Let me serve you some." She puts pasta on their plates. She adds cheese and sauce. She says, "Enjoy your lunch."

Sara and Ben start to eat. They say, "Mmm, this is yummy. Thank you, Mom." They eat fast. They are very hungry.

Mom eats slow. She says, "I'm glad you like it. But don't eat too fast. You might get a tummy ache."

Sara and Ben say, "OK, Mom. We will eat slow." But they don't. They eat fast. They want to end their lunch. They want to play outside. They finish their pasta. They say, "We are done. Can we go outside now?"

Mom says, "Yes, you can. But first, clear your plates and wash your hands." She smiles. She says, "You are good helpers. I love you."

Sara and Ben say, "We love you too, Mom." They clear their plates and wash their hands. They run outside. They play with their ball. They are happy. They had a good lunch.

Once there was a duck who always wanted to find the perfect place to lay her eggs. She looked far and wide, but nothing seemed quite right. Everywhere she went there was too much noise, or the ground was too hard and uncomfortable. Until one day she came upon a field of grass. It was so quiet; all she could hear was the sound of silence. She thought it would be the perfect place for her eggs.

The grass was green and lush, so she happily lay her eggs there. For days she stayed by the side of the eggs, until one day a huge storm came. It brought with it dirty rain and filthy mud. The mud and water covered the eggs, and when the storm was over all the eggs were ruined.

The duck was heartbroken. All she wanted was for her babies to hatch safely, but the storm had taken away her dream. Now all she could do was mourn in the silence of the grass.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to watch TV all day long. One day, his mom said, "Timmy, you need to go outside and play. It's a beautiful day!"

Timmy didn't want to go outside. He said, "But Mom, it's too harsh outside. I want to stay inside and watch TV."

His mom replied, "No, Timmy. You need to get some fresh air. Why don't you go to the pool and dive in?"

Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, Mom. I'll go to the pool and dive in. But can I watch TV when I come back inside?"

His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Timmy. But remember, it's important to have fun outside too!"

Once there was a rabbit who was hungry. He knew he would have to find food, so he started to look. He saw a carrot and thought it looked tasty. 

He hopped over to the carrot and asked, "Can I have a bite?"

The carrot answered, "Yes, of course you can!" 

The rabbit was so happy and thanked the carrot for being so kind. He took a big bite and was very satisfied. 

But then he realised he had been too eager. He hadn't asked the carrot's owner for permission. The rabbit felt ashamed for not asking and ran away quickly. 

The end!

The big man went to work every day. He picked up his iron and was ready to go.

One day Mommy asked the big man why he always brought the iron to work.

"It's an important job that takes a lot of care," he said.

The big man liked to iron all the clothes so that it looked neat and tidy. He knew that it was an important job; so he worked hard to make sure everything was perfect.

When the big man was done with all the work, he took the iron back home. He was happy and proud of what he had done. He knew it was important work.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emma. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day she saw a net lying in the grass. She thought it looked like fun so she grabbed it.

Then she decided to act like a butterfly. She waved the net around in circles, pretending to fly around the garden. Her friends watched, amused by her funny game.

When Emma finished playing, she saw that the net had caught something different inside. Emma opened up the net and found a little frog inside! At first she was a bit scared of the frog but she soon realised that he was really friendly. She introduced him to her friends and they all had a great time playing together.

The next day Emma came out with her net and her frog to play again.

The end.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play with toys. They had many toys in their room upstairs, but they always wanted more. One day, they saw a big store with many new toys in the window. They asked their mom if they could go inside and look.

Mom said yes, but they had to be careful and stay close to her. She also said they could not buy any toys, because they already had enough. Tim and Kim nodded, but they did not listen. They ran into the store and looked at all the toys. They saw cars, dolls, balls, puzzles, and books. They wanted them all.

They each grabbed a toy and tried to hide it in their pockets. They thought they were lucky and smart. They did not see the store man watching them. He saw them take the toys and he was angry. He called mom and told her what they did. Mom was very sad and mad. She made them give back the toys and say sorry. She also made them go home without any treats.

Tim and Kim felt bad. They knew they did a wrong thing. They learned that stealing is not good and that they should be happy with what they have. They also learned that they should listen to mom and be careful in the store. They hugged mom and said sorry again. They went to their room upstairs and played with their old toys. They realized they had many toys and they did not need more. They were not lucky and smart, they were silly and naughty. They decided to be good and share their toys from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the grass. One day, she found a big hole in the ground. It was very deep and she had to be careful not to fall in. 

Lily saw a sharp stick on the ground and she picked it up. She wanted to use it to see how deep the hole was. But her mommy said, "No, Lily, that stick is too sharp. You could hurt yourself. Let's find something else to use." 

So, they found a long stick that was not sharp. Lily carefully put the stick down into the hole. It was very deep! She was happy she didn't fall in. From that day on, Lily was always careful when playing near holes and never picked up sharp sticks again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily decided to go on a walk with her mommy. They walked and walked until they reached a big park. 

While they were walking, Lily felt something on her shoulder. It was a disgusting bug! She didn't like bugs, so she asked her mommy to take it off. Her mommy brushed it away and they kept walking. 

After a while, they saw a big slide in the park. Lily wanted to go on it, but she was scared. Her mommy told her she should try it and that she would be there to catch her. So, Lily went up the ladder and slid down. She had so much fun! 

Finally, it was time to go home. Lily was tired from all the walking and sliding, so her mommy carried her on her shoulder. Lily felt safe and happy. They went home and had a yummy dinner together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play in the pool. She liked to splash and make big waves. One day, Lily's mommy put lotion on her skin to protect her from the sun. Lily thought the lotion felt funny and slimy. 

Lily went back to playing in the pool, but then a boy came and splashed her. Lily got mad and thought the boy was rude. She wanted to splash him back, but her mommy told her not to be rude. So, Lily just kept playing and having fun in the pool. 

After a while, Lily got out of the pool and her mommy put more lotion on her skin. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you mommy, I love you." Then, Lily went to eat some yummy snacks with her mommy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a troubled little girl. Her name was Janie. She lived with her mom and dad in a small house. 

One day, Janie was looking for her mom's wallet. She searched all over the house, but she could not find it. She was getting more and more sad and troubled.

Just then, Janie's mom appeared. She had a big smile on her face. In her hand was the missing wallet! Janie was happy to see her mom and the wallet. 

Her mom hugged her and said, "I found your wallet in a special place where I keep it safe." Janie was relieved and they hugged each other. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved the color yellow and had a lot of yellow things. One day, she saw her friend, Max, who looked sad. 

"What's wrong, Max?" asked Lily. 

"I want to have a big party, but I don't know how to prepare for it," said Max. 

Lily had an idea. "I can help you prepare for the party! I have a lot of yellow decorations that we can use." 

Max was happy and said, "You are so wealthy in yellow things! Thank you for helping me." 

Together, they prepared for the party and it was the best party ever with lots of yellow balloons, yellow cake, and yellow presents. Max was very grateful to his friend, Lily.

One day, a little girl called Mandy was playing in her garden. It was a sunny day and she was having lots of fun. Suddenly, she saw something strange on the grass. It was a thing. It was very shiny and sparkly.

Mandy got closer. She reached out to touch it and wipe it. But the thing wouldn't move!

Mandy asked, "What are you?"

A voice said, "I'm a successful gold coin. If you wipe me three times, you can make a wish. Then your wish will come true!"

Mandy's eyes opened wide. She quickly wiped the coin three times and wished for new toys.

Soon enough, Mandy's mommy came outside with a big bundle of toys.

Mandy was so excited! She thanked the coin and gave it a big hug.

"I'm glad my wish came true," said Mandy.

The coin smiled. "I'm glad I was able to help," it said.

Once upon a time, there was a kind princess who lived in a big castle. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite one was a little scale. She used it to weigh all her toys and see which one was the heaviest.

One day, the princess decided to make some yummy cookies. She cut some butter and sugar with a knife and put them in a big bowl. Then she added some flour and mixed it all together. She used her scale to make sure she had the right amount of ingredients.

After baking the cookies, the princess shared them with her friends. They all said they were the most delicious cookies they had ever tasted! The princess was very happy that she could share her yummy treats with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs all day long. One day, Lily's mommy took her to a big store where there were lots of toys and things to buy. 

As they walked around, Lily saw a luxury toy that she really wanted. She asked her mommy if she could have it, but her mommy said they couldn't afford it. Lily was sad, but then she saw a sign that said they could win the toy if they entered a contest.

Lily's mommy signed them up for the contest and they waited anxiously. Finally, they got a call that they had won the luxury toy! Lily was so happy and felt very clever for finding the sign that led to the contest. She played with her new toy all day long and sang songs about her good luck. The end.

Lily was very happy. She had an invitation to go to Ben's birthday party. She liked Ben. He was kind and funny. He always shared his toys and snacks with her. He was generous.

But Sam was not happy. He did not have an invitation to go to Ben's birthday party. He was jealous of Lily. He wanted to go too. He did not like Ben. He thought Ben was boring and silly. He never played with him. He was mean.

Sam decided to tease Lily. He waited for her outside the classroom. When he saw her, he said, "Lily, Lily, you are so silly. You think Ben likes you, but he does not. He only invited you because he felt sorry for you. He does not want you at his party. He wants you to go away."

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not believe Sam. She knew Ben was her friend. She said, "Sam, Sam, you are so mean. You are lying. Ben does like me. He invited me because he wanted me to have fun. He does not feel sorry for me. He does not want me to go away. He wants you to stop teasing me."

Sam laughed. He did not care. He said, "Lily, Lily, you are so dumb. You do not know anything. Ben is lying. He does not like you. He does not want you to have fun. He does not want you to stop teasing me. He wants you to cry."

Lily felt hurt and scared. She did not know what to do. She wanted to go to Ben's party. She wanted to be happy. She did not want to cry. She did not want to listen to Sam. She ran away.

She ran to Ben. He was waiting for her at the gate. He saw her and smiled. He said, "Lily, Lily, you are so sweet. I am glad you are here. I like you. I invited you because I wanted you to have fun. I do not feel sorry for you. I do not want you to go away. I want you to come with me."

Lily felt happy and safe. She believed Ben. She knew he was her friend. She said, "Ben, Ben, you are so kind. I am glad I am here. I like you. I want to have fun. I do not want to go away. I want to come with you."

Ben hugged her. He said, "Lily, Lily, you are so brave. You did not let Sam tease you. You did not cry. You did not listen to him. You ran to me."

Lily hugged him back. She said, "Ben, Ben, you are so generous. You did not let Sam ruin your party. You did not get angry. You did not fight with him. You waited for me."

They walked to the car. They went to Ben's party. They had fun. They ate cake and played games. They laughed and smiled. They were happy. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to serve her family and friends by making them yummy food. One day, she was making cookies for her rude neighbor, who always yelled at her. 

As she was taking a step towards her neighbor's house, she accidentally dropped the cookies on the ground. Her neighbor saw this and started yelling at her, calling her names. Lily felt sad and scared. 

Later that day, Lily's family found out what had happened and they all went to talk to the neighbor. But the neighbor was still rude and didn't want to listen. The conflict between Lily and her neighbor continued and they never became friends. 

In the end, Lily learned that sometimes, no matter how kind you are, some people will still be rude. She decided to focus on serving those who appreciated her kindness and love.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends saw a big pile of hay. They wanted to play on it, but it was too high. 

Lily's friend, Emily, said, "I wish we could slide down the hay like a slide." 

Lily had an idea. She ran to her house and came back with a helpful tool - a big piece of cardboard. They put the cardboard on the hay and slid down. It was so much fun! 

After playing for a while, they heard a loud noise. It was the farmer who owned the hay. He said, "What are you doing on my hay?" 

Lily said, "We're sorry. We just wanted to play." 

The farmer smiled and said, "I remember when I was your age. I used to play on hay too. But next time, ask me first." From that day on, they always asked the farmer before playing on his hay.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and feel the soft ground under her feet. One day, she was playing with her toys when she accidentally stepped on a sharp rock. It hurt her foot and made her uncomfortable.

Lily's mom saw her crying and asked what happened. Lily showed her the rock in her foot. Her mom gently removed the rock and cleaned the wound. Lily felt much better and was able to play outside again.

From then on, Lily made sure to watch where she was walking so she wouldn't step on any more rocks. She loved feeling the ground under her feet, but she didn't want to be uncomfortable again.

Once upon a time, there was a deep forest. In the deep forest there lived a deer. The deer loved to explore the forest and play around the trees.

One day the deer was so tired it decided to quit running. It went to the deepest part of the forest and lay down. While it was lying there, the deer saw something. It was a beautiful pond with many little fish swimming around in it. The deer was so mesmerized that it forgot all about wanting to quit running.

The deer hopped and ran around the pond. It jumped over the logs and played with all of the animals in the forest. Soon, the deer wasn't so tired anymore. It hadn't quit running - it had just taken a break!

The deer had lots of fun for the rest of the day, and when it was time to go home the deer was sad to leave the beautiful deep forest. It was so excited to come back and explore another day.

Once upon a time, there was a fancy penguin. He seemed so happy and he liked to play all day. One day, he went for a walk and he saw something special. It seemed like a party - there were lots of balloons and people dressed up fancy. He felt so excited. Suddenly, he saw a huge cake! He got very close to have a better look. He noticed that the cake was so big, he could fit inside it - so he did! Everyone cheered loudly when he got inside the cake. So the fancy penguin enjoyed the party and it seemed like he had lots of fun. The End.

Once there was a lady. She was walking in the park and it was a very nice day. Suddenly, she paused. High in the air, she saw a kite. It was bright and colourful and it had long ribbons. The lady smiled and watched it for a long time. The kite moved high in the sky and danced around. Suddenly, the lady had an idea. She got some string from her pocket and tied it to a tree. Then, with a few running steps, she threw the string high into the air. The string flew higher than anything else and the kite came down to the lady. She was very happy and laughed. She grabbed the kites long ribbons and tied them to the string. Then, she paused for a moment, watching the kite move magically high in the sky. The lady smiled and started to walk home, feeling very pleased.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mia. Today was Mia's first day at school and she was very excited. Mia's Mum knew she was nervous and wanted to make sure she would be safe. To do this she made Mia a special bag with a pocket on the outside. 

Mum said "This pocket will support you and keep you safe. It has a leak-proof lining to keep your things dry. You can put things in it that make you feel safe and comfortable."

Mia was so happy and she thanked her Mum. She put in things that made her feel safe, like her favourite teddy bear. Then she put the pocket over her shoulder, made sure the zipper was closed properly and confidently went off to school.

One day, a little gray bird was flying in the sky. The gray bird saw a big tree and thought it would be a good place to make a nest. So, the gray bird flew down to the tree and started to make a nest with sticks and leaves.

While the gray bird was making the nest, a friendly squirrel came by. The squirrel said, "Hi, bird! What are you doing?" The gray bird replied, "I am making a nest for my family." The squirrel smiled and said, "That's nice! I live in this tree too."

The gray bird and the squirrel became good friends. They played together every day and helped each other find food. The gray bird was happy to have a new friend and a cozy nest for its family.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. Jack and Jill were very polite to each other. They were always laughing and playing together.

One day, Jack and Jill noticed a table outside with a special game on it. It was a game called chess. They had never seen it before, so they looked at the pieces carefully.

The game looked fun. So, Jill asked Jack to learn how to play the game with her.

Jack said yes, and he quickly signed up for tutorial lessons. Jack and Jill practiced each day and soon they knew how all the pieces moved.

After a few weeks, Jack and Jill were very good at playing chess. They were very polite while they played, always saying 'good move' or 'well done'.

They would play the game together all the time. They had so much fun!

Once upon a time, there was a kind duck. The duck lived by a river. Every day, the duck would go for a swim in the river. One day, the duck met a fish. The fish said hello to the duck and the duck nodded back. They became friends and swam together every day. 

One day, the river became very fast and the fish could not swim well. The duck saw the fish struggling and knew he had to help. The duck used his beak to carry the fish to safety. The fish was very grateful and thanked the duck. The duck just nodded and they continued to be friends. 

From that day on, the duck and the fish always looked out for each other. They swam in the river together and had many adventures. They were the best of friends and nothing could ever break their bond. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went outside to play in the rain. She loved to jump in puddles and feel the wet raindrops on her face. Her mom told her to wear her raincoat, but Lily didn't listen. She thought it was more fun to get wet.

As Lily played, she saw a frog hopping in the grass. Lily believed that if she caught the frog, it would bring her good luck. She chased after the frog, but slipped on the wet grass and fell down. Her mom came outside and scolded her for being foolish and not wearing her raincoat. Lily felt silly and wished she had listened to her mom.

From that day on, Lily always wore her raincoat when she played in the rain. She still believed in good luck, but now she knew it was important to be safe and not do foolish things.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a unique talking corn. The corn could speak to all the animals and people. Everyone loved the corn, and they liked to listen to its stories.

One day, a little boy named Tom came to the corn. He said, "Hello, corn! Can you speak to me?" The corn smiled and said, "Yes, Tom! I can speak to you, and I have a fun story to tell." Tom sat down, and the corn began to tell a story about a big, friendly bear.

In the story, the bear lived in a forest with many friends. The bear would dance and play with the other animals all day. Everyone in the forest loved the bear, just like how the village loved the talking corn. Tom listened to the story and laughed with joy.

When the story was over, Tom thanked the corn for the fun story. He went back to his home and told his mom about the unique talking corn. From that day on, Tom and the corn became good friends, and they shared many more stories with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy car. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to clean up his toys. Timmy didn't want to clean up, so he hid his toy car under his bed.

As time passed, Timmy's toy car started to shrink. Timmy was sad when he saw that his toy car was now too small to play with. His mom asked him why he didn't clean up his toys, and Timmy told her he was sorry.

Timmy's mom told him that it's important to be responsible and take care of our things. She said that if we don't take care of our things, they might shrink or even end up in jail (like when we lose them). Timmy learned his lesson and promised to be more flexible and responsible.

Once upon a time there lived a boy called Ben. Ben had a skin that was very special. Even though it was extremely stupid, it had the power to turn into anything he could imagine.

One day Ben decided to use his special skin and turn it into a car. He jumped up and down when he saw how fast it went. With a huge smile on his face he drove around the garden.

It wasn't long before the skin grew tired of being a car. It wanted to be something else. It whispered in Ben's ear that it wanted to turn into an Elephant. Ben smiled and nodded his head.

In an instant, the skin changed into an Elephant. Its trunk was huge, its ears were flapping and it was tripping over it's elephant feet! Ben laughed and laughed until he was almost crying.

When Ben finally said goodbye to his Elephant skin it waved it's trunk softly and turned into it's original form. Ben hugged his special skin because he was so thankful for all the cool adventures he went on. He knew that no matter how stupid it looked it was the most amazing thing in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was scared of the dark and always had a night light on. One day, her mom gave her a special pill that would prevent bad dreams. 

Lily took the pill and went to bed feeling happy and safe. She fell asleep quickly and had a wonderful dream about unicorns and rainbows. 

The next morning, Lily woke up feeling refreshed and not fearful at all. She told her mom about her good dream and how the pill helped her. Her mom was happy to hear that the pill worked and that Lily wasn't scared anymore. 

From that day on, Lily took the pill every night and never had a bad dream again. She was no longer fearful of the dark and was able to sleep peacefully.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, as she walked outside, she saw a big bird with big eyes. It was an owl! Lily thought it was so cool to observe the owl. 

But then, the owl flew down and picked up a slimy, disgusting worm. Lily didn't like that. She thought the worm was yucky. 

The owl looked at Lily and hooted. Lily waved goodbye and ran back inside to tell her mommy about the owl she observed. Even though the worm was disgusting, Lily thought the owl was still pretty neat.

Sammy had a great day. First, he went to the park with his mom and dad. They walked together and Sammy laughed when a big dog ran by. Next, they went to the beach. Sammy was so happy because there were big waves. He ran into the water, but it was wet! He laughed when he got all wet, but he knew he had to go inside and dry off.

Finally, Sammy and his mom and dad went to the ice cream store and they all got a sundae. It was so yummy! Sammyâ€™s eyes lit up and he laughed as he ate it. After that, they went home and Sammy said goodnight to his mom and dad.

As Sammy closed his eyes, he knew something good would happen tomorrow. He had a good feeling about it. He didn't know what it would be, but he had a will to find out. He giggled and soon felt asleep with a smile on his face.

Bee and Ant are friends. They like to play in the sun and look for food. One day, they find a big hive full of honey. Bee is happy. He says, "This is my home. There is a lot of honey here. Do you want some?"

Ant is hungry. He says, "Yes, please. I love honey. Thank you for sharing with me." He follows Bee to the hive. They see many other bees working and buzzing. Ant is scared. He says, "Are they angry? Will they sting me?"

Bee says, "No, they are fine. They are my family. They make honey and take care of the hive. They will not hurt you if you are nice. Come, I will show you where the honey is." He leads Ant to a comb full of golden honey. He says, "Here, you can have some. But not too much. We need to save some for winter."

Ant says, "Okay, I understand. I will only take a little bit. It is very sweet and yummy. You are very kind, Bee. I am glad we are friends." He takes a small bite of honey and smiles. Bee smiles too. He says, "Me too, Ant. You are very brave and smart. We are different, but we can share and have fun. That is what friends do." They eat some honey and then go back to play in the sun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a popular bunny named Bob. Bob had many friends because he was very nice. One day, Bob and his friends went to play hide and seek. Bob was very good at this game, so he always found his friends quickly.

"Ready or not, here I come!" shouted Bob. He looked behind a tree and found his friend, the squirrel. Then, he looked under a bush and found his friend, the mouse. Bob knew his last friend, the bird, was hiding in a high place. He looked up at the sky and saw a big tree. Bob thought the bird was hiding there.

Bob hopped to the big tree and started to climb. As he climbed, he felt something strange in his chest. He didn't know that it was his lung. When he reached the top, he saw his friend, the bird. "I found you!" said Bob. The bird smiled and said, "Good job, Bob! You are the best at this game!"

Bob was very happy. But then, he remembered the strange feeling in his chest. He told his friends about it. They all decided to go see the wise old owl for help. The owl listened to Bob's story and said, "Bob, you have discovered your lung. It helps you breathe when you climb and play."

Bob and his friends were amazed. They thanked the wise old owl and went back to play more games. Now, whenever Bob felt his lung, he knew it was helping him have fun with his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Frankie and Mary. They loved to race each other. Frankie had a number, five, and Mary had a number, one.

But before they could race, they had to be very quiet. They tiptoed to where they wanted to race and stopped in a quiet spot. They had to be extra quiet because there were other people around.

After they had been quiet for a long time, it was time for them to race. Frankie counted to three and started running. Mary counted to five, then started running. They raced and raced until they reached the finish line.
