Frankie had won! He was so happy that he jumped for joy and gave Mary a big hug. They both smiled and laughed. After that, they raced each other again and again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited to go to her first dance class. She put on her pretty pink tutu and ran to the dance studio. When she got there, she saw other girls who were also eager to dance.

The teacher told them to clap their hands and follow her instructions. Lily tried her best to clap along with the other girls. She felt happy when she did it right. 

After the class, Lily's mom asked her how it went. Lily said, "I had so much fun! I learned that when we clap together, we can make beautiful music." Her mom smiled and hugged her, and said, "That's right, Lily. When we work together, we can make wonderful things happen."

Once upon a time, there was a helpful little dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play with his group of friends in the park. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long.

One sunny day, while they were playing, Buddy's best friend, a little girl named Lily, fell down and hurt her knee. She started to cry. Buddy ran to her side and said, "Don't cry, Lily. I will help you." 

Buddy gently kissed Lily's knee, and the pain went away. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Buddy. You are so helpful!" They hugged and continued to play with their group of friends, happy and full of love.

Tom and Lily liked to jog in the park. They liked to see the trees, the flowers and the birds. They also liked to look for bugs. They had a jar to keep the bugs they found.

One day, they saw a big, shiny bug on a leaf. It had many colors and wings. Tom wanted to catch it and put it in the jar. Lily said, "No, Tom, that is a cheap thing to do. The bug is happy on the leaf. It does not want to be in the jar. Let it be free."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He ran to the leaf and grabbed the bug. He put it in the jar and closed the lid. He was proud of his catch. He said, "Look, Lily, I have the best bug ever. It is so pretty and rare. You are just jealous."

Lily was sad and angry. She said, "Tom, you are not nice. You are selfish and mean. The bug is not happy in the jar. It is scared and sad. You should let it go. It is not yours to keep."

Tom did not care. He said, "No, Lily, this is my bug. I caught it fair and square. I will not let it go. It is mine."

But then, something bad happened. The bug was not a bug at all. It was a bee. And it was very angry. It stung Tom through the jar. Tom screamed and dropped the jar. The jar broke and the bee flew away. Tom cried and held his hand. It hurt a lot.

Lily ran to Tom and helped him. She said, "Tom, I am sorry you are hurt. But you should have listened to me. You should not take things that are not yours. You should respect the life of others. That is the right thing to do."

Tom nodded and said, "Lily, you are right. I was wrong. I was cheap and greedy. I should have let the bee be. I am sorry. Can you forgive me?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Tom, I forgive you. You are my friend. But next time, please be more careful and kind. And maybe we should look for other bugs. Bees are not fun to play with."

Tom agreed and said, "Yes, Lily, you are right. Bees are not fun to play with. They are better to watch from far away. And there are many other bugs to find. Let's go and jog some more. Maybe we will see a butterfly or a ladybug. They are pretty and gentle. And they do not sting."

Lily and Tom hugged and jogged away. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be respectful and not cheap. And they had more fun with the bugs that did not hurt them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She wanted to go to the west. The west was a very quiet place, but she was excited.

This time, she heard the voice answer. It said, "Yes, I am here". The voice was so gentle that the girl felt a little bit safer.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to visit his grandma. Grandma cooked Timmy a yummy meal with his favorite food, chicken nuggets. Timmy thought the meal was so cool because he got to eat with his hands and dip his nuggets in ketchup.

One day he saw a magical bottle and he picked it up. When he opened it up, water sprayed out of it. He thought it was so fun, he sprayed the water all over himself. 

Suddenly, he was thin! All of his friends were amazed at how thin the fat horse had become. But then, the magical bottle started to spray again, and the fat horse became fat once more! 

The other horses laughed and teased the fat horse, but he was determined to keep his thin figure. So every day he picked up that magical bottle and sprayed himself with the magical water,until he was thin again.

One day, a little boy named Timmy was in his backyard. He looked up and observed the sky. It was a beautiful, deep blue color. He wanted to touch it, so he jumped up and down, hoping he could reach it. Suddenly, he heard a sweet sound coming from a tree nearby. He stopped jumping and moved closer to the tree to observe. Sitting on the branch was a tiny bird! It was flapping its wings and singing a sweet little song. Timmy watched in awe and started singing along with the bird. The bird flew away and Timmy waved goodbye. It was a wonderful day, full of sweet moments and beautiful blues.

Mia and Leo were playing in the garden. They saw a big peach tree with many ripe peaches. They wanted to pick some and eat them.

"Let's get some peaches, they look yummy!" Mia said.

"OK, but we have to be quick. Mom said we can't leave the garden," Leo said.

They ran to the tree and reached for the peaches. They each grabbed one and bit into it. But they did not like the taste. The peaches were spicy and made their mouths burn.

"Yuck, these peaches are spicy!" Mia said.

"Ow, ow, ow, they hurt my tongue!" Leo said.

They spit out the peaches and threw them away. They ran back to the garden and looked for some water. They saw a hose and turned it on. They drank some water and rinsed their mouths.

"Ah, that's better," Mia said.

"Much better," Leo said.

They heard Mom calling them from the house.

"Mia, Leo, come inside. It's time for lunch," Mom said.

They ran to the house and hugged Mom.

"Mom, we tried some peaches from the tree, but they were spicy and bad," Mia said.

"Spicy peaches? Oh, no, those are not peaches. Those are hot peppers. You should not eat them. They are for cooking, not for snacking," Mom said.

"Hot peppers? Oh, no, we did not know. We are sorry, Mom," Leo said.

"It's OK, my loves. You did not mean to. But next time, ask me before you pick something from the tree. Some fruits and vegetables are not good for you raw. Now, let's have some lunch. I made some sandwiches and some real peaches for dessert," Mom said.

"Yay, sandwiches and peaches!" Mia and Leo said.

They followed Mom to the kitchen and ate their lunch. They enjoyed the sweet and juicy peaches. They learned their lesson and never ate hot peppers again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Milly. She was playing in her garden when suddenly, the sky filled with thunder. Milly felt scared and began to tremble.

"I'm scared," said Milly.

"Don't worry," said her mummy. "We're safe inside."

Milly's mummy grabbed her hand and they went inside the house. Milly's mummy went to the window and closed the curtain.

"See, the slow rain will soon stop," said her mummy.

Milly watched the slow rain through the window and her trembling stopped. She felt warm and safe in her mummy's arms.

The rain stopped and the sun came out. Milly's mummy opened the curtain and happy sunshine flooded the room. Milly smiled when she saw the sunshine. She knew that everything would be okay.

Once upon a time there was a bad thief. He wanted to take all the good things. All the nice people were scared.

One day, two friends came by. They had special powers, and were very brave. They wanted to help everyone, so they worked together to restore things back to the way they were.

The friends used their powers to make the thief leave. He was never seen again. Everyone thanked the friends and was happy to have their good things back.

The friends had made the town safe again. They were proud of what they had done, and everyone was grateful.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big hill. They want to climb it.

Lila has flexible boots. They can bend and stretch. Ben has hard boots. They are stiff and tight. Lila says, "My boots are good for climbing. They can grip the ground. Your boots are not good. They will slip and slide."

Ben says, "No, my boots are good too. They are strong and tough. They will protect my feet. I trust my boots. Do you trust your boots?"

Lila says, "Yes, I trust my boots. Let's go climb the hill."

They start to climb the hill. Lila's boots help her move fast and easy. Ben's boots make him slow and hard. He falls down and hurts his knee. He cries.

Lila hears him and runs back. She says, "Are you okay, Ben? I'm sorry your boots hurt you. Do you want to try my boots? They are flexible and soft. They will make you feel better."

Ben says, "Thank you, Lila. You are a good friend. I will try your boots. Maybe they will help me climb the hill."

They swap boots and climb the hill again. Ben's boots fit Lila well. They are strong and tough. Lila's boots fit Ben well. They are bendy and stretchy. They both reach the top of the hill. They are happy.

They say, "We did it! We climbed the hill. We both have good boots. We both trust our boots. And we trust each other."

Once upon a time, there was a popular toy. The toy was a hammer and a nail. All the kids loved to play with it. They would hit the nail with the hammer and laugh.

One day, the nail started to complain. It said, "Ouch, that hurts! Please stop hitting me." The kids were surprised. They did not know the nail could talk. They felt bad for the nail.

The kids decided to stop hitting the nail. They played with other toys instead. The nail was happy and didn't hurt anymore. The kids learned to be kind to their toys, and they all played happily ever after.

Sam and Mia were playing near the cliff. They liked to look at the big rocks and the water below. They saw some birds flying and some fish jumping.

"Look, Sam, a big bird!" Mia said, pointing at a gray and white eagle.

Sam blinked. He was scared of the big bird. He thought it might hurt them.

"Let's go away, Mia. The big bird is angry," he said, pulling her hand.

But Mia did not want to go. She wanted to see the big bird more.

"No, Sam, the big bird is not angry. It is ancient. It knows many things. Maybe it can talk to us," she said, letting go of his hand.

She walked closer to the cliff, where the big bird was sitting on a branch. She smiled and waved at it.

"Hello, big bird. What is your name?" she asked.

The big bird looked at Mia with its yellow eyes. It opened its beak and made a loud sound.

"Kaaaw! Kaaaw!" it said.

Mia was not afraid. She thought the big bird was saying hello.

"Kaaaw! Kaaaw!" she said back.

Sam was very afraid. He saw the big bird flap its wings and fly towards Mia. He thought the big bird was going to take her away.

"Mia, come back! The big bird is bad! It will eat you!" he shouted, running after her.

But Mia did not hear him. She was too happy to see the big bird. She reached out her hand to touch it.

The big bird landed on Mia's hand. It was heavy and warm. It looked at Mia with its yellow eyes. It opened its beak and made a soft sound.

"Mia. Mia," it said.

Mia was amazed. The big bird knew her name. She felt a special bond with it.

"Wow, you can talk! You are amazing, big bird. What is your name?" she asked.

The big bird made a soft sound again.

"Ella. Ella," it said.

Mia smiled. She liked the big bird's name.

"Ella, you are my friend. I like you, Ella," she said.

Ella nodded. She liked Mia too. She felt a special bond with her.

"Mia, you are my friend. I like you, Mia," she said.

Sam reached the cliff. He saw Mia and Ella talking and holding hands. He was shocked and confused. He did not understand how the big bird could talk and be friendly.

"Mia, what are you doing? How do you know the big bird? How does it know you?" he asked.

Mia turned to Sam. She saw that he was scared and worried. She felt sorry for him.

"Sam, don't be scared. This is Ella. She is an ancient bird. She knows many things. She knows my name. She is my friend. She will not hurt us. She can be your friend too," she said.

Sam blinked. He did not know what to think. He looked at Ella. She looked at him with her yellow eyes. She opened her beak and made a soft sound.

"Sam. Sam," she said.

Sam felt a strange feeling in his chest. He felt curious and calm. He reached out his hand to touch Ella.

"Hello, Ella. You are an ancient bird. You know many things. You know my name. You are Mia's friend. You can be my friend too," he said.

Ella nodded. She was happy to have two friends. She felt a special bond with them.

"Mia, Sam, you are my friends. I like you, Mia. I like you, Sam," she said.

Mia, Sam, and Ella smiled. They felt a special bond with each other. They stayed on the cliff, talking and playing, until the sun set. They did not notice the time. They did not notice the other birds and fish. They only noticed each other. They were happy. They were friends.

Once upon a time there was a red reef in the ocean. Every day, a little fish named Mark would swim over to the reef. On sunny days, he would nibble away at some of the coral, and when he was feeling brave, he would swim inside some of the tunnels in the reef.

One day, Mark noticed something red and shiny on the reef. He swam closer to check it out, and discovered that it was an old sunken ship! Curious, Mark decided to go inside the ship and investigate what it was like.

Mark explored the old ship, discovering lots of cool things! He passed through small rooms and dark hallways. But the most exciting thing he found was a big red chest! Mark opened the chest, and discovered inside a large pile of shiny coins.

Mark was overjoyed! He swam back to his reef with the coins, and he knew he would never forget his big discovery.

One day, Tom and his best friend Sally went to the park. As they were walking around, Sally found a purple brush and showed it to Tom. Tom thought the brush was nice and said he wanted it. But Sally was teasing him and said he couldn't have it.

Tom was sad, but then he saw a bird resting in the warm sun. He pointed to the bird and said he wanted it instead. Sally teased him again and said he couldn't have that either.

Then, Tom saw a beautiful flower growing on a bush and said he wanted that instead. This time, Sally smiled and nodded her head. She handed Tom the brush and said he could take the flower.

Tom thanked his friend and took the flower and the brush. He was so happy! As he walked with Sally, he used the brush to make the flower extra soft and warm.

Once upon a time, there was a daisy. It made Jack and Mary laugh. It was very funny. Every day, the daisy played games with the children. But then one day, something changed. The daisy started to rot. The children were very sad. They tried to fix the daisy, but it did not work. Finally the children decided to bury the daisy in the ground. They said goodbye and planted a new daisy in its place. From then on, they made sure to take good care of the daisy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia was nervous because she had to show her friends the print she made. The print was a picture of a big, red apple. Mia loved apples and she wanted her friends to see her print.

On the day of the show, Mia took her print to school. She was so nervous, her hands were shaking. But her teacher, Miss Rose, told her it would be okay. Mia took a deep breath and showed her friends the print of the big, red apple.

When her friends saw the print, they all smiled and clapped their hands. They loved the print Mia made. Mia was so happy that she started to clap too. Miss Rose was proud of Mia and everyone applauded. Mia was not nervous anymore and she had a great day at school.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Jim. Jim was very happy, but he was scared too. But one day Jim found something to make him feel brave. He found a hug. 

The hug came from a steam. It was not hot like fire, but a gentle steam. It was like a warm hug. It made Jim feel safe and happy. 

But the steam was fragile. Jim had to be very careful so it wouldn't break. He gave it a gentle hug, and the steam hugged him back. 

From then on, Jim was no longer afraid. He felt brave and he knew that the hug would always be there, waiting for him.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved playing with his cart, which was his favorite toy. One day, he wanted to be popular and have lots of friends to play with.

Timmy decided to make a lemonade stand with his cart. He worked hard and succeeded in making delicious lemonade. People loved it and soon he became very popular. Timmy was happy because he had lots of friends to play with now. 

From that day on, Timmy and his cart became famous in the neighborhood. They would sell lemonade every weekend and everyone loved it. Timmy was proud of his success and loved playing with his cart even more.

Once upon a time, there was a family that lived in a tidy house. One day, the family decided to go on an adventure and invited a friend to come with them. They got on a big ship and sailed away to a faraway land. 

As the ship sailed, the family's friend looked around, exploring all the new sights and sounds. Suddenly, they saw a giant whale! It was the biggest whale they had ever seen. The friend was so excited that they invited the whale to join them on the ship. 

The family and their friend took turns feeding the whale for the rest of the voyage, until they finally reached the faraway land. The family and their friend said goodbye to the whale and thanked it for joining them. 

Since then, the family has taken many more adventures on the ship. Each time they voyage, they bring tidiness, excitement and plenty of snacks to ensure another satisfying voyage.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander around her neighborhood and explore new places. One day, she found a magic word on the ground. It was a word that she had never heard before, but it made her feel comfortable and happy.

Lily picked up the word and put it in her pocket. As she continued to wander, she noticed that the word was glowing. She wondered what could happen if she said the word out loud. But she decided to wait until she found a special place to say it.

Finally, Lily found a beautiful garden full of flowers. She sat down on a comfortable bench and took out the magic word from her pocket. She closed her eyes and said the word out loud. Suddenly, the flowers started to dance and the birds started to sing. Lily knew that the magic word had made everything around her more beautiful. From that day on, Lily always kept the magic word with her as she continued to wander and explore.

Once there was a happy little girl called Daisy. She loved to run and zoom around the garden. One day, when Daisy was running, the fog began to roll in. Daisy could barely see any further than her own feet. She was scared and stopped running.

"Momma, I can't see through the fog. What should I do?" asked Daisy.

Her momma replied, "It's okay Daisy, the fog will disappear soon. Why don't you take a break while the fog clears?"

So Daisy sat down in the garden and waited. Soon, the fog started to move away. Daisy could see the sun again. She was so happy! She jumped up and started to zoom around the garden. She played hide and seek with her momma and laughed and smiled until the sun set.

Once upon a time, there was an ignorant baby. He was sitting in the garden and playing with some rocks. Suddenly, he noticed something strange and went over to take a look.

He saw a frog, sitting there in the dirt. The baby asked the frog, "What are you doing?"

The frog replied, "I'm just minding my own business."

The baby thought this was so funny. He laughed and said, "I like that. I'm going to mind my own business too!"

He then went back to playing with his rocks and the frog went back to minding its own business. The two were happy and content, each one doing what they were meant to do. 

The End.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Jane was playing in the garden. Suddenly, she found a lemon and wanted to taste it. She asked her mom, "Mom, may I taste the lemon?" Her mom replied, "No, Jane. That lemon is too bitter for you." Jane understood and said, "Okay, I won't eat it."

After a while, Jane asked her mom, "Mom, may I make lemonade with the lemon?" Her mom said, "Yes, Jane, you may but make sure to add some sugar, or else it will be too bitter for you.

So Jane collected some sugar and mixed it with the lemon juice. She made a delicious and sweet lemonade. She took a sip and said, "Thanks mom! This lemonade tastes so good, not bitter at all!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you liked it. I'm so happy I permitted you to make lemonade."

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Nan. She was 3 years old. 
One day, she fell down and got a very big scrape on her knee. She started to cry.

Her mom came to help her. She took a bandage from the cupboard and began to wrap it around Nan's knee. As she tied the bandage, she smiled at Nan and said "I care about you".

Nan's knees stopped hurting. She felt a lot better! She thanked her mom and hugged her.

After that, Nan was a bit more careful. She was always looking where she was going, so she wouldn't get any more scrapes. Whenever she scraped her knees again, Nan knew that her mom would be there to help, with an empty bandage and lots of love.

The Chubby Rose.

Once there was a chubby rose who loved to travel. She stopped in many places, admiring the sights and sounds of her adventures. Everywhere she went she was given a warm welcome.

One day as she was travelling along she suddenly heard a loud voice. It was coming from a man. He was shouting at her, telling her to leave. The rose was very scared and she didnâ€™t know why the man was acting so angry.

â€œWhatâ€™s wrong?â€ the rose asked.

â€œYouâ€™re ruining my garden,â€ the man said. â€œYou need to travel somewhere else.â€

The rose didnâ€™t want to leave as she had grown quite fond of the place. But she realised that the man was not going to let her stay.

So with a heavy heart, the chubby rose left and continued her travels. She was sad to have been forced to leave but she was still determined to find new places to visit and to have new adventures.

Once there was a very lively girl named Alice. She had lots of friends and they all liked to play in her garden.

One of Aliceâ€™s friends noticed that there was a post in the middle of the garden and Alice wanted to climb it. Her friends warned her not to because it was too high but Alice couldn't resist.

Alice carefully made her way up the post and soon she got to the top. From the top she could see her garden and her friends. Everyone cheered for her and her friends applauded.

Alice was so proud of herself for resisting the temptation to stay on the ground and climb the post. She was now the proud owner of a fantastic view from the top of the post.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park every day. One day, she met a little boy named Jack. Jack seemed troubled and sad. Lily asked him, "What's wrong?" Jack whispered, "I lost my favorite toy last week and I can't find it."

Lily felt sad for Jack and wanted to help him. She said, "Let's look for your toy together." They searched the park, but they couldn't find it. Lily said, "Don't worry, we'll find it soon." Jack smiled and felt happy that he had a friend like Lily. 

Suddenly, Lily saw something shining under a tree. She shouted, "Look, Jack! Your toy is here!" Jack was overjoyed and thanked Lily. From that day on, they played together every day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big carpet in a small house. A little boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, played on the carpet every day. They loved to run and jump on it.

One day, Tim spilled juice on the carpet. The carpet started to rot and smell bad. Tim's mom saw the mess and said, "Oh no, the carpet is rotting! Tim, you need to clean this up."

Tim felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I will clean it up." So Tim and Spot worked together to clean the rotting carpet. They scrubbed and scrubbed until the carpet was clean and smelled good again.

Tim's mom was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and Spot, for cleaning the carpet." Tim and Spot smiled, knowing they had fixed their mistake. From that day on, they were more careful when playing on the carpet.

Once upon a time, there was a rail. It was so long, the end couldn't be seen! One day, a little girl wanted to manage it. She wanted to find out where it went! So off she went, walking down the rail.

It seemed like a long journey. Everything was dull and boring, until, oops! The girl slipped and slid right off the edge of the rail. She got back up and kept walking.

But then she saw something. What was it? It was a big, bright button! She pressed it, and all of a sudden, the rail started to move! It was so cool! The girl was thrilled!

The little girl had managed the rail! She got to ride on it and see where it went. When the ride was over, she was so proud of herself! She had managed the rail by herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. It was her birthday and she was very happy. Her mommy baked a big cake for her and it looked impressive. 

Lily's friends came over to play with her. They played with dolls and blocks. They also played hide and seek. Lily had lots of fun with her friends. 

Later, they all sang happy birthday to Lily and she blew out the candles on her cake. She got lots of presents too. It was the best birthday ever!

One day, a little girl named Emma was very excited. She had been waiting for the mail to come. When she heard the mailman coming, she ran outside to meet him. He smiled and handed her a small gray box.

"What's this?" asked Emma.

"It's a special mask for you!" said the mailman. "I think you'll like it."

Emma was so excited, she hugged the mailman and ran inside. She quickly opened the box and found a beautiful, gray mask inside. It had sparkly pink and purple sequins around the edges.

Emma smiled and put the mask on. She looked in the mirror and was so proud of herself. She loved her new mask and knew that she would wear it all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play with her board. She would ride it all around the park and have so much fun. One day, she found an ugly board lying on the ground. She felt sorry for it and decided to take it home with her.

The little girl loved her new board, even though it was ugly. She painted it pink and put stickers all over it. She was so happy to have a new friend to play with. But one day, while she was riding her board, she fell and hurt herself badly. She had to go to the hospital and couldn't play with her board anymore.

Days turned into weeks and the little girl got better, but when she went to play with her board again, she found out that it was broken. She was so sad and cried a lot. She realized that she loved her old board more than the new one, even though it was ugly. The end.

One day, Sam and his mom were playing with his toy cars in the living room. They heard a loud noise outside and saw the sky was dark and scary. Mom said, "Sam, we have to go to the basement. There is a tornado coming. A tornado is a big wind that can break things and hurt people."

Sam was scared and did not want to leave his cars. He said, "But mom, I want to play with my cars. They are fun and normal. Tornadoes are not normal. They are bad and mean."

Mom said, "I know, Sam, but we have to be safe. You can bring your cars with you. We will play with them in the basement. Come on, let's go." She took Sam's hand and his cars and ran to the basement.

They went down the stairs and closed the door. They heard the tornado roar and shake the house. Sam hugged his mom and his cars. He said, "Mom, I'm scared. Will the tornado go away?"

Mom said, "Yes, Sam, it will go away soon. We just have to wait and pause. Pause means to stop and be quiet. Can you pause with me?" She kissed his head and held him tight.

Sam nodded and tried to pause. He closed his eyes and listened to his mom's heartbeat. He felt her love and warmth. He thought, "Maybe tornadoes are not so bad. They make me pause with mom. And mom makes me feel normal." He smiled and opened his eyes. He saw his cars and said, "Mom, can we play with my cars now?"

One day, Alex and his mom were heading to a birthday party together. Alex was very excited for the party. He couldn't wait to wear his cute costume. 

"Mom, what is my costume?" he asked. 

"You'll have to wait and see!" giggled his mom. 

When they arrived at the party, Alex's mom showed him his costume. It was a red cape with a bright golden star! 

"Wow! I look so creative!" Alex was so happy he started bouncing up and down. 

His mom smiled and said, "I thought you'd like it! Now it's time to solve the biggest game of the afternoon." She pointed to a big, colorful puzzle in the corner of the room. 

Alex immediately hopped over to the puzzle, eager to begin. He soon found it wasn't very difficult to solve. In no time, Alex had solved the puzzle and was beaming from ear to ear. 

"Good job, Alex! I knew you could do it," his mom praised him. 

Alex was so proud of himself. He couldn't stop showing off his costume, and his parents couldn't stop bragging about how creative and clever their son was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She wanted to go on an adventure.

"Mommy, can I go on an adventure?" Sarah asked.

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, Sarah, you can go. But first you need to make a promise. Can you do that?"

"Yes!" Sarah said. "I can make a promise."

Her mom said, "Alright, here's your promise. You must find a new hole and explore what's inside it. But make sure you stay safe. Can you do that?"

Sarah nodded her head. She was very excited. 

"Okay, let's go!" said Sarah's mother.

So off they went, looking for a new hole. It wasn't long before they found it. It was a big hole and Sarah was scared, but she was also excited. Together, they looked inside the hole and found lots of new things.

Sarah's mom smiled and said, "See? You kept your promise. Now you can go on your adventure."

Sarah smiled and said, "Okay! Thank you mom!" 

And so Sarah's adventure began!

Once upon a time, there was a lively little dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play all day. He had many friends in the park.

One day, Spot saw a big box. He wanted to fit in the box. So, he tried to get in. But, the box was too small. Spot did not fit.

Spot's friends came to help. They found a bigger box. Spot tried again. This time, he fit in the box. Spot and his friends laughed and played. They all had fun with the box.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big tire hanging from a tree. It looked like fun.

"Can we try the tire?" Lily asked Ben.

"Sure, let's go!" Ben said. They ran to the tire and took turns to sit in it. They pushed each other and spun around. They laughed and screamed.

The tire was very attractive. It was shiny and black. It had a red ribbon on it. It was a gift from the park man. He wanted to provide something new for the kids.

But after a while, Lily and Ben felt dizzy. They stopped the tire and got out. They felt sick and tired.

"Are you okay?" Ben asked Lily.

"I don't feel good. The tire made me sick." Lily said.

"Me too. Let's go home." Ben said.

They walked slowly to their mommies. They told them what happened. Their mommies hugged them and gave them water.

"Next time, don't play too long on the tire. It can make you sick." Their mommies said.

"Okay, mommy. We're sorry." Lily and Ben said.

They learned their lesson. The tire was fun, but too much fun was not good. They decided to play with other things next time. They still liked the tire, but they liked their mommies more.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big factory. The factory made toys for kids. One day, a toy named Tim wanted to be independent. He did not want to stay in the factory anymore.

Tim said to his friend, Tom, "Let's split from the factory and go on an adventure!" Tom was scared but agreed to go with Tim. So, they left the factory when no one was looking and started their adventure outside.

As they walked, they saw many new things. They saw trees, flowers, and even a big hill. Tim and Tom were happy to be independent and have fun together. They played and laughed all day. And from that day on, they were the best of friends.

Little Jane was a helpful princess who wanted to help everyone in the kingdom. One day she heard that her older brother, the prince, was feeling very tired. Jane quickly rushed to the prince's chamber to see if she could help.

When she arrived, she saw the prince lying down on his bed. "Are you okay?" she asked him.

The prince looked sad. "I am so tired," he said.

Jane had an idea. She said, "Why don't you take a nap? You'll feel much better afterwards."

The prince agreed and fell asleep. As he dozed off, Jane quietly watched over him.

After the prince awoke, he looked refreshed. He thanked Jane for being so helpful. From then on, he knew that Jane was a princess with a very big heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little brown mouse who lived in a big chimney. One day, the mouse had a special request. He wanted to have a friend to play with. He peered out of the chimney and looked around.

Just then, the mouse saw a small brown bird perched on a nearby tree. The mouse peered at the bird and called out, "Hey! Can you be my friend?"

The bird thought for a moment, then replied, "Yes! I would like that."

The mouse and the bird played together for a long time. They both had lots of fun! They raced and hide and seek, and ran through the grass in the sunshine.

From that day forward, the mouse and the bird were the best of friends. They played together every day and were never apart. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cricket named Jim. Jim loved to sing and hop around in the grass. One day, Jim hopped into a hole and couldn't get out. He cried out, "Help! Help! I'm stuck!"

Just then, a little girl named Lily walked by and heard Jim's cries. She peeked into the hole and saw Jim's chubby body. "Don't worry, Jim. I'll get you out!" she said. She reached in and pulled him out of the hole.

"Thank you, Lily!" said Jim. "You saved me."

Suddenly, a big storm came and lightning struck a tree nearby. Lily and Jim were scared, but they stuck together and waited for the storm to pass. After the storm, they said goodbye and Jim hopped away, singing a happy song.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Timmy found a big, bright rock in his backyard. 

"Mommy, look what I found!" said Timmy, holding up the bright rock. 

"That's very pretty, Timmy," said Mommy. "But be careful, it might be sharp." 

Timmy wanted to keep the bright rock, but his little sister, Lily, also wanted it. They started to argue about who should have it. 

Just then, Daddy came outside and said, "I have an idea. Let's play a game. We'll hide the rock and whoever finds it first will get to keep it." 

Timmy and Lily agreed and started to search for the bright rock. After a few minutes, Timmy found it first and revealed it to everyone. 

"I won!" said Timmy, holding up the rock. 

Lily was sad, but Daddy said, "Don't worry, Lily. You'll find something even better one day." 

Timmy was happy to have won the bright rock and they all went inside for some ice cream.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Ben. Ben was very sleepy because he had stayed up late playing with his toys. He wanted to take a nap but he was also thirsty. He decided to go to the kitchen to get some juice. 

As he was drinking the juice, he started to yawn. He knew it was time for his nap. He went back to his room and climbed into his cozy bed. He closed his eyes and fell asleep right away. 

When he woke up, he felt much better. He was no longer sleepy and he had lots of energy to play with his toys again. From then on, he made sure to go to bed early so he wouldn't feel sleepy during the day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a furry hill. It had never been filled. Every day, a new creature would come to try to fill the hill. A rabbit tried hopping up the hill, but he could not fill it. An elephant tried to trample the hill, but he could not fill it. Then one day, a mouse came along. He was small and furry, like the hill. He filled the hill with dirt and rocks, until it was nice and full. All the animals cheered and thanked the mouse for filling the hill. They were all so happy that the hill was full! The end.

Once upon a time, there was a poor girl named Jane. She wanted to make a dress, but she didn't have a needle to sew it with. 

One day, Jane looked out her window and saw a needle on the ground. She ran to grab it, but it was stuck in a branch just out of reach. 

So Jane tried to climb the tree, but it was too tall for her. She started to cry.

Suddenly, a friendly voice came from behind. It was the old woman who lived next door. She said to Jane, "Don't worry, I can help you get the needle. What do you need?" 

Jane said, "I need a stick so I can reach the needle". 

The old woman smiled and gave Jane a long stick. Jane reached up with the stick and was able to grab the needle. 

Jane was so happy. She thanked the old woman and ran home with the needle. She was able to make her dress, and she lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small town, lived a girl named Sue. Sue had long, thin hair. She loved to play with her hair, but it was always messy. Sue wanted to make her hair look nice and clean.

One day, Sue went to the store with her mom. "Mom, can we buy shampoo for my hair?" asked Sue. Her mom agreed and they bought the shampoo. Sue was very happy!

At home, Sue used the shampoo to wash her hair. It looked so nice and clean! Sue's mom was proud of her. "Sue, you look great! You learned that taking care of yourself is important," said her mom. Sue smiled and promised to always keep her hair clean.

Lily liked to go to the gym with her mom. She liked to play with the balls and the mats and the ropes. But she did not like to share with the other kids. She wanted to have all the toys for herself.

One day, a boy named Ben came to the gym with his dad. He saw Lily playing with a big red ball. He asked her if he could play with it too. Lily said no. She hugged the ball and ran away. Ben was sad. He wanted to play with the ball.

Ben was persistent. He followed Lily around the gym. He asked her again and again if he could play with the ball. Lily said no every time. She got angry. She threw the ball at Ben. It hit him in the face. He cried.

Lily's mom saw what happened. She was not happy. She told Lily to say sorry to Ben and to share the ball. Lily did not want to. She pouted. She said no.

Lily's mom had an idea. She told Lily to reverse the roles. She asked her how she would feel if Ben had the ball and did not let her play with it. She asked her how she would feel if Ben threw the ball at her. Lily thought about it. She felt bad. She realized she was not nice to Ben.

Lily went to Ben. She said sorry. She gave him the ball. She asked him if he wanted to play with her. Ben smiled. He said yes. He wiped his tears. He thanked her. They played with the ball together. They had fun.

Lily's mom was proud of Lily. She hugged her. She told her she did a good job. Lily was happy. She learned to share. She made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a man and a little girl. The man and the little girl loved to go on walks in the woods together. On a lovely day, the man and the little girl went for a walk in the woods. 

As they were walking, the little girl saw something in the distance. She asked the man, "What is that?â€ The man replied, â€œIt's a log!"

The little girl and the man ran up to the log. The man said, â€œYou know what? Let's climb up it!â€ The little girl did not know how to climb, so the man said, â€œHere, I will help you.â€ 

The man lifted the little girl up and held her as she climbed the log. She was so excited and she laughed as she reached the top. Suddenly, the log started to wobble and the little girl started to fall. 

But the man was there and he caught her just in time. She was safe and sound. The man said, â€œSee? I told you I would take care of you!â€ The little girl smiled and she said to the man, â€œI love you." 

The man smiled back and said, â€œI love you too.â€ They hugged each other and continued their lovely walk.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ann. One day, Ann and her mum went to the hospital for a check up. Ann saw a unique nurse, who was very kind. The nurse asked Ann to stay quiet and lie down on the bed so she could measure her. So, Ann did as she was told and lay down.

The nurse looked at Ann and smiled. She smiled back. The nurse said, â€œYou can sit up now. Ann. That was very good.â€ 
Ann was very pleased. She wanted to show the nurse how happy she was and said, â€œI like you!â€ The nurse hugged Ann and said, â€œI like you, too!â€ Ann was over the moon!

After the check up was finished, Ann and her mum left the hospital. Ann was very proud of herself. She was happy to have met such a unique nurse.

Once upon a time, there was a happy monkey named Max. Max loved to sing and dance. He would sing all day long and make everyone around him happy. 

One day, Max found a big drum in the forest. He was so excited that he started playing it right away. The sound of the drum was loud and made Max feel even happier. 

As he was playing the drum, Max noticed that his friend, the bird, was feeling uncomfortable. The bird was shivering because it was cold outside. Max knew just what to do. He stopped playing the drum and hugged the bird to keep it warm. 

After a while, the bird stopped shivering and felt comfortable again. Max was happy to see his friend feeling better. He started singing a happy song to celebrate. The bird joined in and they sang and danced together all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a modest little boy named Tim. He loved to play with paint. One day, he decided to paint a picture of his house.

As Tim painted, he saw his friend, Sam, walk by. "Hi, Sam!" Tim said. "Come see my paint." Sam came over and looked at the picture. "Wow, Tim! That looks good!" Sam said.

But as they talked, Tim did not see a rock on the ground. He stumbled and fell. His paint went everywhere. Tim and Sam laughed. They had fun cleaning up the paint mess together. And from that day on, they became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to read his favorite book every night before bed. One night, he couldn't find his book anywhere. He looked under his bed, in his toy box, and even in the closet. But he still couldn't find it.

Timmy's mom came into his room and asked him why he was crying. "I can't find my book," Timmy said. "It's weird that it's not here."

"Don't worry, Timmy," his mom said. "Let's go look for it together."

They looked in the living room, the kitchen, and even outside. Finally, they found Timmy's book in the car. Timmy was so happy that he hugged his mom and said, "Thank you for helping me find my book!"

Once upon a time, there was a festival. Everyone was excited and speeded about, having lots of fun. 

Annabelle was at the festival with her mom and dad. She wanted to try something new and delicious, so she went to the food stall. She saw lots of interesting food, but the one that caught her eye was a sour treat. She excitedly asked her mom if she could try it. 

Her mom said yes, and Annabelle eagerly took a bite. The sour treat was so tangy and delicious! She couldn't help but speed away and eat some more. 

Annabelle had a great time at the festival, and she couldn't wait to go back next year. She was so happy that she got to try something new and tasty.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit. The rabbit wanted to find a good place for a nap. It hopped and hopped until it found a long, dark tunnel. The rabbit noticed the tunnel had lots of hairy edges around it. It thought it was the perfect spot.

The rabbit scratched its way around the tunnel and started to gather sticks, leaves and grass. The rabbit carefully placed them near the tunnel entrance. The rabbit was making a cosy bed to sleep in.

When the bed was finished, the rabbit hopped inside the tunnel and settled down for a nap. The tunnel was warm and safe, perfect for snuggling down. 

The rabbit slept until it heard a friendly voice calling its name. The rabbit hopped out of the tunnel and saw its friend, a squirrel, waving at it. The two animals hugged and then hopped and skipped together in the garden, gathering treats and snacks. 

What a great day! The rabbit found a perfect place to take a nap and also found a great friend to play with.

One day Grandma and Grandpa went to work. They worked in a plant. They worked hard all day to make things.

At lunchtime, Grandma and Grandpa ate some vegetables from the plant. The vegetables were bitter. Grandpa said they were good for his health. Grandma smiled and said they were yummy.

When Grandma and Grandpa were done, the sun was setting. Grandma and Grandpa said good-bye and went home.

The next day, they went back to the plant to work. Grandma and Grandpa worked hard all day again and then ate some of the vegetables from the plant. They were still very bitter, but Grandma and Grandpa said they were still tasty.

Grandma and Grandpa worked hard at the plant for many days. They were very happy to help make things. Grandma and Grandpa said goodbye when the sun was setting. They went home and were very tired from a long day of work.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the sunshine, but she didn't like when it rained. One day, Lily was playing with her toy car when she saw something special in the sky. "Look, Mommy! A rainbow!" she shouted. 

Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Lily. Rainbows happen when the sun shines after the rain." 

Lily was so excited to see the rainbow that she wanted to catch it. "I want to touch the rainbow, Mommy!" she said. 

Her mommy laughed and said, "You can't touch a rainbow, silly. It's just a pretty sight to see." 

But Lily was determined, so she ran around the yard and tried to catch the rainbow. She felt foolish when she realized she couldn't catch it, but she still loved looking at it in the sky. From that day on, whenever it rained and the sun came out, Lily would always look for the rainbow.

Once there was an adorable teddy bear named Teddy. Teddy had been very lonely all day and wanted to explore.

Just then, Teddy noticed a tall structure. He wanted to know what was inside so he poked it with his paw. The structure opened up and Teddy saw a lovely garden with pretty flowers.

He hopped through the garden and explored every corner of it. He found lots of wonderful things! He found a pond full of fish, lots of big trees, and a swing that he could play on. Teddy had a wonderful time playing around in the garden.

When Teddy was tired, he lay down in the grass and looked up at the sky. He thanked the structure for giving him such a wonderful day, and said goodnight.

Once upon a time there was a filthy operation. The operation was a mess, with items scattered all around. The operation's workers had to do something, so they decided to clean it. 

They grabbed all of their cleaning tools and got to work. First they swept the floors, then they washed the walls. They tidied up all the desks, chairs and other items. Everyone worked hard to make sure the operation was sparkling. 

The workers were so proud when they finished cleaning. The operation had gone from being filthy to spotless. Now they could feel good about their work and enjoy the operation in all its clean glory!

Once upon a time, there was a playful dog named Max. Max loved to run and jump and play with his toys. One day, Max saw a sign that said "No Dogs Allowed". Max didn't understand why he couldn't play in that area.

Max tried to go past the sign, but a man came and held him back. The man told Max's owner that dogs were not allowed in that area. Max's owner was sad and didn't know what to do.

But then, Max had an idea. He decided to release all of his toys and play with them in another area. Max and his owner found a new place to play where dogs were allowed. Max was happy again and played with all of his toys.

Once upon a time, there was a very old bird who lived in a cosy nest. He wanted to soar through the sky like his younger, faster friends did. He tried and tried, but he just couldn't fly far.

One day, a friendly fox found him and told him: "If you eat a special vegetable you can soar higher than anyone!"

The old bird was so excited! He asked the fox questions: "Where can I find this vegetable? How can I make it?" the fox answered: "There's a magical ancient vegetable. Go find it in the forest and it will help you to soar!"

The bird flew off to the forest and searched and searched. Eventually, he found the vegetable and ate it. Instantly, he felt much lighter and soon, he was soaring through the sky with so much energy!

He was so happy and said: "Thank you Mr fox! I'm so happy I can fly higher now!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anya. She was very polite and loved to skip around her house.

One day, Anya stepped outside of her house and she noticed something on the side of her house. It was a small, friendly bunny! Anya smiled and said hello to the bunny, and the bunny looked up at Anya and said, "Hi Anya!" 

Anya was so excited to meet the bunny that she started skipping around the yard. The bunny hopped around too and the two playmates soon became friends. 

Anya was so polite to the bunny. She always said hello and goodbye when she saw the bunny, and she always shared her vegetable treats with him. They had lots of fun playing together everyday. 

Anya and the bunny always skip around the side of the house together. The bunny felt so lucky to have Anya as a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a big gorilla in the jungle. He was very intelligent and knew how to find food and make a home. One day, a little boy came to visit the jungle and saw the gorilla. He stared at the gorilla with big eyes because he had never seen such a big animal before.

The gorilla was not happy that the boy was staring at him. He thought the boy was being mean and started to get angry. Suddenly, the gorilla jumped out of the bushes and chased the boy. The boy ran as fast as he could, but the gorilla was too fast. The gorilla caught the boy and took him away.

The boy's family never saw him again. They searched for him everywhere, but he was gone. They were very sad and missed him very much. They wished they had never let him go to the jungle to see the gorilla.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big hill with many trees. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side. They find a long stick on the ground. They use the stick to help them walk up the hill.

They reach the top of the hill and see a pond. The pond has many ducks and fish. Lily and Ben are happy. They want to feed the ducks and fish. They break the long stick into two pieces. They use the pieces to poke the water and make ripples.

The ducks and fish come closer to see what is making the ripples. Lily and Ben throw some bread crumbs into the water. The ducks and fish eat the bread crumbs. Lily and Ben laugh and clap. They enjoy watching the ducks and fish.

But then, a big frog jumps out of the water. The frog lands on the long stick that Lily is holding. Lily is scared. She drops the stick and screams. The frog croaks and hops away. Ben picks up the stick and chases the frog. He wants to catch the frog and make it his pet.

Lily and Ben have fun playing with the stick, the pond, and the frog. They forget about the time. They hear their mom calling them. They run back to their mom. They tell her about their adventure. Their mom smiles and hugs them. She is glad they had fun. She takes them home for a snack and a nap.

Jill and her dad were on a long walk. Suddenly, dad's phone beeped. He looked at his phone and showed a sign to Jill. It was dark and it said 'supply'. Dad said with a smile: "Let's go, Jill. We have to do a job."

They drove in the car for a while and soon stopped. Jill and her dad went out of the car and walked to a house. It was already dark outside. 

They knocked on the door and a nice lady opened. Dad gave the lady the sign with 'supply' on it. The lady smiled and gave them a box full of items. Dad said that it was the supply they were looking for. 

Jill and dad were happy to have done the job. They said their goodbyes and went back in the car. They both knew that they had done a great job.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a big, tall armchair that he loved to sit in and read his books. One day, his friend Sammy came over to play. Sammy wanted to sit in the armchair too, but it was too tall for him to climb up.

Timmy decided to share his armchair with Sammy. He helped Sammy climb up and they both sat in the armchair together. They read books and told stories, and had a lot of fun sharing the cozy armchair. From then on, whenever Sammy came over to play, they always shared the armchair and had a great time together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy jeep. His jeep was brown and had big wheels. One day, Timmy went outside to play with his jeep. He drove it around in the dirt and had so much fun.

Suddenly, Timmy saw a bird in the sky. He stopped playing with his jeep and gazed up at the bird. "Wow, look at the bird!" Timmy said to his mom who was watching him play. "It's flying so high!"

Timmy's mom smiled and said, "Yes, it's a beautiful bird. But don't forget about your jeep. It's fun to play with too." Timmy nodded and continued to drive his jeep around, but he couldn't stop thinking about the bird he had just seen.

Once upon a time, there was a fox. He was a very special fox because he liked to decorate! Every day he would go out and find wonderful things like bright leaves and shiny stones to decorate his den. His den was the most decorated den of all the foxes!

One day he found a box filled with beautiful decorations. He was so glad! He started to hang streamers and glittery paper around his den. He was so happy with the way it looked!

The other foxes heard about his decorations and came over to admire them. They were amazed and so excited. The foxes all danced and sang about how wonderful the decorations were. Everyone was glad and had a great time.

The fox was so happy he could make all the foxes smile. After that, he kept decorating his den every day. The foxes were so glad to come over and see the decorations. They were always a surprise!

Once upon a time, there was a dog and a cat. They lived next door to each other. One night, the cat decided to take a walk. He picked up a rope and began to wander. As he walked, the dog watched and gazed.

The cat saw a bird and grew curious. He started to walk towards it and began to run. Suddenly, the rope got tangled around the cat's body and he was stuck! The cat was so surprised and called for help. The dog quickly ran over.

The dog tried and tried but he couldn't manage to uncut the rope. He growled and whined in frustration. After a few moments, the dog had a good idea. He grabbed a pair of scissors and cut the rope. The cat was free!

The cat was so relieved and thanked the dog for being so smart. The dog laughed and said,"It was nothing, I'm not stupid like you!" The cat smiled and said,"Maybe not, but at least I'm not stuck anymore!" They both laughed and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and spin around in circles. One day, Lily decided to play a game of hide-and-seek with her friends. She ran and hid behind a wall, but the wall was weak and started to wobble.

Lily's friends searched and searched, but they couldn't find her. Suddenly, the weak wall collapsed and Lily fell down. She wasn't hurt, but she was scared. 

After that day, Lily learned to be careful when playing near weak walls. She also realized that spinning around wasn't always the safest thing to do. From then on, Lily made sure to play safely and have fun with her friends.

One day, a little girl found a boat. It was a really pretty boat, with a glossy red paint. She wanted to have some fun, so she decided to sail in it. She waved goodbye to her mom and jumped on board.

The boat sailed out to sea. It was a bright, sunny day and the water sparkled all around the boat. Everywhere she looked, the girl could see colorful fish swimming in the water. The air was so fresh and the waves so lively, the girl felt happy and alive.

The boat sailed for many hours. Eventually, the little girl reached a small island. When she arrived, she saw a welcoming sign. It said, â€œWelcome to the Island of Happiness!â€ Everyone on the island was so friendly and full of life. It was such a lively place.

The girl had so much fun on the island. She played in the sun and she swam in the beautiful blue water. When it was time to return, she could hardly believe how quickly time had passed. She was so happy to have been on such a wonderful adventure. 

The little girl waved goodbye to the island and sailed back home. She was tired, but full of wonderful memories from her lively adventure.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved enjoying the outdoors, especially on stormy days. Every time the sky became grey, Sarah would run outside and jump in puddles and watch the lightning.

One stormy day, Sarah went to the park with her mom. She was so excited to be outside. They enjoyed throwing a ball around, but then the rain started to come down harder. Mom said it was time to go home.

When Sarah and her mom got home, Mom said it was time for Sarah to shut her eyes and take a nap. She was so tired from playing in the rain! Sarah soon drifted off to sleep, dreaming of lightning and yummy snacks.

When Sarah woke up, her mom had made her a special treat. Sarah was thrilled to see her plate of her favorite food - scrambled eggs with toast. She quickly ate every bite and smiled with joy.

From then on, Sarah loved storms and the sound of the rain on her window. She loved going outside to play in the rain and watching the lightning. Sarah knew that no matter what, she would always be safe and cozy in bed with her mom.

Once upon a time there was a bossy dog named Max. He always wanted things to go his way. He liked to hurry around so that he could get everything done.

One day, Max went for a walk with his new friends. They decided to play tag and hurry around the park. They all laughed and had a lot of fun.

Max was the fastest runner and he was so bossy! He would tell the others to hurry up and keep up with him. He even tried to teach them his special running style. 

But, deep down Max was just trying to get the most out of their fun game. He wanted everyone to have as much fun as he did. 

The others were happy to learn Max's running style and when they stopped, everyone agreed that they had all had a great time.

One cold winter morning, a little girl named Jessie was walking near the beach when she saw a group of people waving their arms in the air. She walked closer and noticed they were making funny sounds and saying "zoom, zoom". Jessie was feeling curious so she asked her mum, "What are they doing Mum?" Mum replied, "They're Kiteboarding. It's a sport where you use the wind and a kite to glide across the beach and water". Jessie was excited and asked, "Can I do that too?". Mum smiled and said, "Maybe one day but for now, let's look at the kites". 

Then they walked up to a man waving different kites in the air. He said, "Welcome! These are some of my kites. Take a look". Jessie looked up and saw the colourful kites flying and waving. She felt so happy that she wanted to try it too. She asked her mum, "Can I have one of these kites?". Mum replied, "Yes, but don't forget to hold tight when it starts to zoom!" Jessie was very excited, holding her kite and waving it with the other people. From then on, every cold winter morning, Jessie and her mum were out together, kiteboarding and waving in the cold wind.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big tree with many leaves. They want to climb the tree and see what is up there.

"Come on, Ben, let's go up the tree!" Anna says.

"OK, Anna, but be careful. The tree is very old and the bark is rough," Ben says.

They hold on to the branches and go up the tree. They see many birds and squirrels and bugs. They also see a hole in the trunk. They are curious and look inside.

"Wow, look, Ben, there is a book in the hole!" Anna says.

"A book? In the tree? Let me see!" Ben says.

They take out the book and open it. The book has many pages with strange words and pictures. The pages are yellow and torn. The cover is leather and has a metal lock.

"This book is very old, Anna. Maybe it is ancient. I wonder who put it here and why," Ben says.

"Maybe it is a magic book, Ben. Maybe it has secrets and spells and stories," Anna says.

They look at the book and try to read it. They do not understand the words, but they like the pictures. They see dragons and fairies and castles and stars.

"This book is amazing, Anna. I wish we could keep it," Ben says.

"Me too, Ben. But maybe someone is looking for it. Maybe it belongs to someone who loves it very much," Anna says.

They think for a while. Then they decide to put the book back in the hole. They close the cover and lock it with the metal lock. They hope the book is safe and happy in the tree.

"Goodbye, book. Thank you for letting us see you," Anna says.

"Goodbye, book. Maybe we will see you again someday," Ben says.

They climb down the tree and go back to their parents. They do not tell anyone about the book. They keep it as a secret in their hearts. They always remember the book and the tree and the adventure they had.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Rita. She loved animals, so one morning she went to the zoo. 

Rita found a big enclosure with a gorilla inside. The gorilla looked very sad and was frowning. Rita asked a zoo keeper why the gorilla was so unhappy, and the zoo keeper replied in a mild voice, 
"He's been here by himself for a while, he's just lonely I think". 

Rita understood and started to wave and smiled at the gorilla. The gorilla waved back and started to smile too! 

Rita was so delighted that she came back the next day. This time, the gorilla was smiling and running around the enclosure. Rita waved and said hello and the gorilla waved back. 

Rita was very happy to see the gorilla happy, and she smiled too.

Once there was a boy who was very foolish. He liked to do things that weren't wise. One day he saw a subway. He thought it would be fun to try and lift it up. He tried and tried, but the subway was too heavy and he couldn't lift it.

He was very sad, but he didn't give up. He asked the people nearby for help. Many people stopped to help him. Together they all used their strength to lift the subway.

After the subway was lifted, everyone was very proud. The boy was happy that he was able to use his friends' help to do something wonderful. He learned that it was better to work together than alone. Doing things alone can sometimes be foolish.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved her bed. She slept in it every night and it was her favorite place to be. One day, she noticed that the bed was getting old and creaky. She asked her mommy if they could replace it with a new one.

Mommy agreed and they went to the store to look for a new bed. They found one that was big and comfortable. Lily was very happy and couldn't wait to sleep in it. The old bed was harmless, but the new one was even better.

Now, Lily sleeps in her new bed every night and she loves it even more than her old one. She's happy that they replaced it and now she sleeps soundly every night. The end.

Tim and Jen are friends. They like to play with toys and watch TV. One day, they see a big parade on TV. They see many people and cars and animals and balloons. They hear music and clapping and cheering.

"Wow, look at the parade!" Tim says. "It is so fun and pretty. I wish I could go to the parade."

"Me too," Jen says. "But we are too poor. We have no money and no car. We cannot go to the parade."

They feel sad and angry. They want to have fun like the people on TV. They want to own nice things like the cars and the balloons.

They think of a plan. They go to their rooms and find some old clothes and toys. They make their own parade. They put on hats and scarves and glasses. They use boxes and cans and bottles as cars. They blow up some balloons and tie them to strings. They make some noise with pots and pans and whistles.

They go outside and walk around the block. They smile and wave and sing. They pretend they are in the parade. They have fun and laugh.

Some people see them and join them. They bring their own clothes and toys and balloons. They make the parade bigger and louder and happier.

Tim and Jen are happy. They do not feel poor anymore. They feel rich and proud. They own their own parade.

Once there was a girl. She was very unusual. She was always talking about exciting things. One day she mentioned an elephant. The girl said she saw an elephant at the park. Everyone was so surprised. No one had ever seen an elephant in their town before.

The girl told them all about the unusual elephant. Everyone wanted to see it too. They all went to the park that afternoon. Sure enough, there was a big, grey elephant! Everyone cheered with joy.

The girl was very proud. She was so glad her friends believed her. From that day on, they always listened when she mentioned something unusual. It was a happy ending for the girl and herfriends.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They loved to play together and always tried their best. One day they wanted to try something different. They asked their mommy if they could have a fight.

At first, their mommy said no, but after thinking about it, she said yes. The two friends were so excited. They ran to the backyard and started their fight.

They punched and kicked each other, trying so hard to see who was the winner. They were both so strong and determined. Everyone who watched them was very amazed.

After a long time, one of the friends won the fight. The other friend was very envious and sad. But in the end, they both hugged each other and smiled. They reassured each other that it was only a game and that they were still the best of friends.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They saw a big wave coming and ran to the water. "Splash!" they shouted as the wave wet them.

But then they saw something terrible on the shore. It was a big fish that was not moving. It had no eyes and its skin was falling off. It smelled very bad. "Ew!" Ben and Lily said. "What is that?"

Their mom and dad came to see. "That is a fish that has rot," their dad said. "Rot means that it is very old and sick and has no life. We should not touch it or go near it. It can make us sick too."

Ben and Lily felt sorry for the fish. They wondered why it had rot and how it came to the beach. They wished they could help it. "Can we bury it in the sand?" Lily asked. "Maybe then it will not smell and other animals will not eat it."

Their mom and dad nodded. "That is a good idea," their mom said. "But we have to be careful and use a stick or a shovel. We do not want to touch it with our hands." They found a stick and a shovel and dug a hole in the sand. They pushed the fish into the hole and covered it with sand. They made a cross with two sticks and put it on top.

"Goodbye, fish," Ben and Lily said. "We hope you are happy now." They went back to play in the water and forgot about the terrible rot. They had fun with the waves and the shells. They were happy.

Sam and Bob were good friends. One day, they wanted to go to the park.

Bob said, "We can go to the park now!" Sam said, "Yes, let's go."

So they set off to the park. On the way, they met a judge. He was wearing a big black robe.

The judge said, "Where are you two going in such a hurry?"

Bob said, "We are going to the park."

The judge looked restless. He said, "You must be careful. Don't forget to look both ways before you cross the road!"

Sam and Bob thanked him, and they went to the park. They had a great time playing, running, and laughing.

And now when they go to the park, they always remember to look both ways before crossing the road!

Once upon a time, there was a clever duck named Ducky. Ducky liked to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, Ducky was playing with her friend, Bunny. Bunny said, "I am going to hide behind this tree. You will never find me!" Ducky replied, "I am very clever. I will find you!" 

Ducky looked and looked, but she could not find Bunny. Suddenly, Bunny disappeared! Ducky searched everywhere, but Bunny was nowhere to be found. Ducky was very sad and started to cry. 

Just when Ducky thought Bunny was gone forever, Bunny jumped out from behind the tree and yelled, "Surprise!" Ducky was so happy to see Bunny and they hugged each other. Bunny said, "I knew you would find me, clever Ducky!" From that day on, Ducky and Bunny always played together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Alice. She was three years old and loved to have fun. One day, Alice's mommy brought home a new comb for her. It was bright blue and smooth.
Alice was so excited and ran to the mirror. She was ready to use the comb and make her hair look beautiful.

Alice ran her comb through her long, golden locks. The comb felt so smooth on her hair. She loved it. After brushing her hair, Alice grabbed a book and sat back in a big, comfy chair.

Alice closed her eyes and took a deep breath. She felt relaxed and very happy. She smiled and snuggled in the chair as she read her book. She felt so peaceful with the soft sound of the comb in her hair and the sound of the pages turning.

Alice enjoyed her relaxing day until it was time to go to bed. She had a big, wide smile on her face. She was very content with the way she had spent the day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a kind man named Tom. Tom was a helper. He helped people follow the law. He made sure everyone was safe and happy.

One day, Tom saw a big box in the middle of the road. He thought, "Someone put the box there, and it is not safe. I must move it so no one gets hurt." Tom knew he had to act fast to keep everyone safe.

Tom went to the box and pushed it off the road. Just then, a little girl came running up to him. She said, "Thank you, Tom, for moving the box. You saved my cat!" The girl was happy, and Tom felt good. He knew he had done the right thing by following the law and keeping everyone safe.

Once upon a time there was girl called Rachel. She was 3 years old and very curious. One day Rachel's parents left her alone in her room. She had been warned not to go near the big wardrobe in the room. 

As soon as her parents left, Rachel went over to the wardrobe and opened the door. To her surprise, it was much bigger inside than it was from the outside. Rachel went inside and the door closed shut. She was worried and started to cry.  

Suddenly she heard a voice. "Hello Rachel! I'm the wardrobe! I'm not scary, I promise." Rachel wiped away her tears and replied, "Hello wardrobe! What happened?" 

The wardrobe replied, "I shrunk you! Now you can explore my world." Rachel was excited to explore the wardrobe and went off on her adventure. She discovered a magic world inside and remained there for hours. 

When Rachel was ready to leave, the wardrobe welcomed her back and said, "Welcome back Rachel! I'm glad I didn't scare you away."

Once upon a time, there were two friends - a rabbit and a bear. They were very excited as today was their special day - a day to celebrate!

The bear grabbed the rabbit's paw and said, "Let's go and watch the ugly television to make our special day even more fun!"

They hopped excitedly all the way to the bear's house and quickly turned on the television. They were so mesmerized by the colorful moving pictures, they couldn't pull their eyes away.

It was so much fun that they decided to celebrate their day together every year.

The bear and the rabbit laughed and cheered and had the best time. They would always remember this special day and all the fun they had. They even promised to watch the ugly television to celebrate every year.

Once there was a little boy named Tim who lived on a farm. Tim liked helping his parents with the farm work, but one day he had a bad idea. Tim saw the cauliflower in the garden and thought he could grab it for himself.

So Tim grabbed the cauliflower, it was hot from being in the sun! He quickly put it in his pocket and ran off into the woods.

But when he got to the woods, Tim felt guilty. He knew he should have not taken the cauliflower without asking his parents. Tim felt so bad he decided he would put it back.

When Tim put the hot cauliflower back into the garden he realised how wrong it had been to take it without permission. Tim knew that it was important to always respect a grown-up's rules.

From then on, Tim never stole anything again and was a very good boy. He learned that it's okay to want something, but it is important to always must ask first!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys and read books. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to have a surprise visitor.

Lily jumped up and ran to the window. She opened the curtains and saw a beautiful chair outside. She wondered if the surprise visitor would sit in the chair. 

Later that day, Lily's grandma came to visit. She sat in the chair outside and said, "Thank you for allowing me to sit in this comfy chair. It's perfect for enjoying the sunshine." 

Lily smiled and felt happy that she helped her mom prepare for the surprise visitor. She also felt proud that she opened the curtains and saw the beautiful chair.

John was a strong, brave boy. He was always ready for adventures. Today he put on his special vest for a very important adventure. It was purple and sparkly and made him feel special.

John set off in search of the most difficult challenge he had ever faced! He was so excited to see what lay ahead!
