Once upon a time, there was a clever fox. He had a card that he liked to show to his friends. The card had a picture of a tree on it. One day, the fox decided to travel to the forest to find that tree. He walked and walked until he saw the tree. It was very big and had lots of leaves. The fox was very happy and showed his card to the tree. The tree didn't say anything, but the fox knew it was impressed. From that day on, the fox and the tree became good friends and would travel together around the forest.

One day, a little boy and a little girl wanted to play together. But they were very far away. So, they decided to unite. That meant they both traveled to the same place.

The result was they were both able to play. They had a great time. They raced cars and built sandcastles on the beach. They laughed and smiled.

But then something terrible happened. It started to rain. So, the two had to separate and go home. But even though it was terrible, the result was still good. They now knew they could unite if they ever wanted to play together again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was a careless boy who did not like to bathe. One day, he put on his uniform to go to school. His uniform was dirty because he did not clean it.

On his way to school, he met his friend, Sam. Sam said, "Tim, your uniform is dirty. Did you not bathe today?" Tim just laughed and said, "No, I did not. I don't like to bathe. It takes too much time."

At school, Tim's teacher saw his dirty uniform and knew he did not bathe. She was not happy. She sent him home to clean up. Tim was sad because he missed his favorite class. From that day on, he learned to not be careless and to always bathe before going to school.

Once upon a time, a small cube lived in a tight box. The cube was sad because it could not move or play with its friends. One day, a kind girl named Lily found the box and opened it.

"Hello, little cube," said Lily. "Why are you so sad?" The cube told Lily that it was sad because it could not move or play. Lily wanted to help and comfort the cube. So, she took the cube out of the tight box and held it in her hands.

Now, the cube could move and play with its friends. The cube was very happy and thanked Lily. "Thank you, Lily, for making me happy!" From that day on, the cube and Lily became best friends, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Daisy. Daisy was playing outside with her friends. She found a glove on the ground and decided to pick it up. She passed the glove to her friend, saying, "This glove is for you!"

Her friend smiled and said, "Thanks, Daisy, this is a nice glove!"

Daisy was so happy that she started jumping and spinning around. Suddenly she got so dizzy that she fell down. Her friends quickly came to her side and asked if she was okay.

"I'm fine," said Daisy. "I'm just a bit dizzy from spinning so much!"

Her friends laughed and shared a big hug. They continued playing, until it was time for Daisy to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a small nail. It was lonely and wanted to be useful. It asked the other nails in the toolbox, "What can I do?"

But the other nails just looked at it and said nothing.

So the nail decided to make a plan by itself. It said, "I will give my best to do something. Even if it takes me a long time, I will keep at it!"

The nail was very persistent. It tried and tried to work, but it just couldn't do what it wanted.

Then one day, a carpenter saw the nail. The carpenter said, "Don't worry. I will give you an important job."

The nail was made part of a big project and it was happy. It learned that being patient and persistent can make things happen.

Moral of the story: Being persistent can help turn dreams into reality.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man. He loved to play with balloons. One day, he found a big, red balloon in his yard.

He wanted to see how high the balloon could go. So, he started to push the balloon up into the sky. The balloon went higher and higher. The elderly man was very happy.

As the balloon went up, a little bird saw it. The bird liked the balloon too. The bird helped the elderly man push the balloon even higher. They all had lots of fun together. And they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was three years old and he liked to sit on the porch. One day he saw a lady walking by the house. She was wearing a big hat.

The little boy said "hello".

The lady smiled and said "hello there".

The little boy asked the lady if he could sit with her.

The lady said "sure, you can sit here".

The little boy sat with the lady and they talked. The lady told him stories and they laughed together. It was nice.

But then the little boy did something bad. He threw dirt at the lady. She was very angry. She asked him why he did something so bad.

The little boy said he was sorry. He promised to never do it again.

The lady smiled and said it was alright. She said she forgave him and they continued to sit together and talk. The little boy learned that it was wrong to do bad things.

Ben and Mia like to draw with colors. They have many colors: red, blue, yellow, green, and more. They draw on big papers and make pictures of animals, flowers, and cars.

One day, Ben and Mia have a problem. They both want to use the same color: purple. Purple is their favorite color. They both reach for the purple color, but they pull too hard. The purple color breaks in half. Ben and Mia are sad and angry.

"It's my purple color!" Ben says.

"No, it's mine!" Mia says.

They start to tear the papers with their pictures. They tear and tear until the papers are in small pieces. They make a big mess on the floor.

Mom comes in and sees the mess. She is not happy. She tells Ben and Mia to stop tearing the papers and to share the colors. She says tearing is not nice and it wastes the papers. She says they can make new pictures with the broken purple color.

Ben and Mia feel sorry. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. They hug and make up. They pick up the pieces of paper and put them in the trash. They take the broken purple color and tape it together. They draw new pictures with the purple color and other colors. They make beautiful pictures and show them to Mom.

Mom is proud of Ben and Mia. She says they are successful artists. She hangs their pictures on the wall. Ben and Mia smile and say thank you. They are happy and they share the colors.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Fred. Fred loved to hop and play with his friends. One day, Fred saw an attractive red blanket on the grass. It was a picnic! He hopped over to take a closer look.

At the picnic, there were many yummy foods like apples, cheese, and bread. Fred's tummy rumbled. He wanted to eat some food too. But there was a big, mean bird at the picnic. The bird said, "No, Fred! You can't have any food. This is my picnic!"

Fred felt sad and hungry. He hopped back to his friends and told them about the mean bird. His friends wanted to help. They all hopped together to the picnic. There were so many frogs hopping that the bird got scared and flew away.

Now, Fred and his friends could enjoy the picnic. They shared the yummy food and had a great time. From that day on, they knew that together they could face any problem. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved Sundays because that was the day her family went to the park. One Sunday, Lily woke up feeling grumpy. She didn't want to go to the park.

Her mom asked her, "Why are you grumpy, Lily?"

"I don't want to go to the park," Lily replied.

Her mom said, "Let's reverse your mood. We can play a game on the way there."

Lily smiled and they played a game of counting trees. When they got to the park, Lily had so much fun that she forgot why she was grumpy in the first place.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we need to reverse our mood and find ways to make ourselves happy.

One night, Timmy was looking up into the sky. He saw something large and round. It was the moon! He asked his mom what it was.

"That's the moon, sweetie," said his mom. "You can read about the moon in a book."

Timmy wanted to read about the moon. So the next morning, he raced to the library to find a book about the moon.

He found a large book about the moon and looked at it for a long time. After reading, he learned all about the things he had seen in the sky the night before.

Now Timmy can look up into the sky and know just what he's looking at. He knows that the large and round thing he saw was the moon.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. The sky was blue and the sun was warm.

"Let's go to the slide!" Lily suggested. She liked to slide down fast and feel the wind in her hair.

"OK!" Tom agreed. He followed Lily to the slide and waited for his turn.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was thunder. They looked up and saw dark clouds. The wind started to blow hard and the leaves flew in the air.

"Oh no, a storm is coming!" Tom said. He was scared of storms. They made him feel cold and wet.

"Let's go home!" Lily said. She grabbed Tom's hand and ran to the gate. They saw their mom waiting for them in the car.

"Mom, mom, we're here!" they shouted. They got in the car and buckled their seat belts.

"Good job, kids. You came back just in time. The storm is very big and strong. We have to drive carefully." Mom said. She was busy looking at the road and the traffic.

"Can we listen to some music, mom?" Tom asked. He wanted to forget about the storm.

"Sure, honey. What do you want to hear?" Mom asked.

"Something happy and fun!" Lily said.

Mom smiled and turned on the radio. They heard a song they liked and started to sing along. They felt better and happier. The storm was still outside, but they were safe and cozy inside.

Once there was a shy little girl who liked to play outside. She liked to chase butterflies and roll around in the grass. One day she found something very special. It was a big red building. It was so tall that it reached the sky. The little girl was so excited! She rolled around the building, touching its shiny walls. She was sure that it was the most beautiful building in the whole world. 

She kept playing around the building until it was time to go home. As she walked away, the little girl waved goodbye to her special building and promised to come back soon. She knew she would always keep it in her heart.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Tamika. She loved to go outside and play with her friends. One day, on a warm afternoon, Tamika and her friends decided to go on an adventure. 

As they explored, they came to a spot where they found many red pastels. The pastels were so bright and colorful that they were surprised! Tamika's friends decided to pick some of the pastels and put them in a basket.

Tamika wanted to pick some too, but before she could the ground started to shake. Out of nowhere a giant red dragon emerged from the ground! Tamika's friends were terrified and quickly ran away.

"Don't be afraid Tamika," said the dragon. "I'm here to protect the pastels." He then explained to Tamika that the pastels were very special and needed to stay away from people. He was happy that Tamika was not trying to take any.

Tamika said goodbye to her new friend and ran off to meet her friends. She told them all about the dragon and they were super surprised.

From then on, the friends knew to always be careful around the red pastels and never to take any. What a surprise!

Tim and Mia were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big, yellow and black animal in the bushes. It had spots and sharp teeth. Tim and Mia were curious and wanted to see it better.

"Look, Mia, it's a leopard!" Tim said. "Maybe it's lost and needs help."

"Or maybe it's hungry and wants to eat us!" Mia said. She was scared and wanted to run away.

"Don't be silly, Mia. It's just a cat. A big cat. Maybe we can pet it and make it happy." Tim said. He was brave and thoughtful. He walked slowly towards the animal.

"Tim, no, don't do that! It's dangerous!" Mia said. She tried to stop him, but he didn't listen.

The leopard saw Tim coming and growled. It was not happy. It was angry and hungry. It jumped out of the bushes and attacked Tim. Tim screamed and fell to the ground. The leopard bit him and dragged him away.

Mia was shocked and sad. She cried and ran to get help. But it was too late. Tim was gone. The leopard had eaten him. Mia wished she had never seen the leopard. She wished Tim had listened to her. She wished they had stayed away from the bushes and played somewhere else. She wished they could relax and be friends again. But they couldn't. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little puppy. He was always running around and getting into trouble. One day, he was out in the woods when suddenly he heard a tiny, quiet voice. It came from a bush nearby. The puppy was eager to meet the voice, but when he approached, the voice vanished!

The curious little puppy decided to investigate, so he started digging around the bush. To his surprise, he found a tiny door leading to a secret tunnel. He peered inside and called out, but all he heard was silence. He was about to give up, but then he heard the same voice again. This time, it was calling out to him, so he stepped inside the tunnel.

The puppy followed the voice until he came to a clearing. There he saw a beautiful fairy, who was the source of the voice. She welcomed him, and asked why he was so naughty. The puppy hung his head in shame and apologised. Suddenly, the fairy waved her wand and made the naughty puppy fly away with her into the sky.

The puppy never returned, but the voice lingers in the woods, telling the other animals about the lessons he learned about being good.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his toys. One day, he fell and hurt his knee. His mommy came outside and asked, "Are you okay, Timmy?" Timmy said, "Ouchie, mommy. My knee hurts." 

Mommy took Timmy inside and gave him a snack. She gave him some crackers and cheese. Timmy loved snacks! After his snack, mommy cleaned Timmy's knee and put a bandage on it. She said, "This will help your knee heal, Timmy." 

Timmy felt much better and wanted to go back outside to play. But mommy said, "Not yet, Timmy. Let's tidy up your toys first." So, Timmy and mommy tidied up his toys and then he was allowed to go back outside and play. Timmy was happy and grateful for his mommy's help.

Once upon a time, there was a kind elephant who lived in a big theater. He loved playing all kinds of different games and making others smile. 

One day, he decided to invite all his friends to the theater. They all partied together and had a lot of fun. 

But then, something bad happened. One of the other animals decided that it wasn't fair that the elephant got to have all the fun, so they started taking the games away from him. 

The elephant was so sad and disappointed. He felt like he had done something wrong, but he had been so kind to his friends. No matter how many times he asked, they wouldn't give the games back to him.

At the end of the day, the moral of the story is that there are some people who take advantage of those who are kind to them. They don't understand that kindness should be rewarded, not taken advantage of.

Sandy was a little girl who loved dolls. She had a special doll that she always took with her everywhere she went. One day, when she was playing with her doll, it fell to the ground and broke. Sandy was very sad. She looked at the broken doll and didn't know what to do. 

Sandy's mom saw the broken doll and decided to help. With some glue and tape, she was able to put the doll back together. Sandy was so happy that she could raise her doll again.

When it was all put back together, Sandy hugged her doll and smiled. She was happy that her toy wasn't broken anymore. From then on, she was always very careful and never dropped her doll again.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Sally. One day, Sally decided to go for a walk. She went outside and followed the path in front of her. As she walked, the path lead to a small dry cabin.

When she arrived at the cabin, Sally was curious to find out what was inside. She opened the door and found a surprise.

There was a squirrel inside the cabin. Sally said, "Hello squirrel! What are you doing in this dry cabin?".

The squirrel smiled and said, "I was looking for a place to hide, and this dry cabin was the perfect spot!". 

Sally and the squirrel then became friends. They played together in the cabin all day.

At the end of the day, Sally said goodbye to the squirrel and went home. From that day forward, Sally visited the dry cabin every day to follow and play with the squirrel.

Molly loved her bicycle. She always rode it up and down her street. Whenever the day was bright, she would take it out of her tight garage. She always put her seat and her handlebars just so. She was so proud of it and always gave it a big hug.

One day, she tried to ride it and her legs were too short. She needed help to make it go. Her mom saw her struggling and taught her how to pedal and how to keep it steady.

Molly was so happy and felt so proud when she finally rode it on her own. She was spinning around in her drive way and the experience was just grand!

From then on, Molly and her bicycle were like two best friends. They were together all the time, and she would love to ride it even when days were gray. She would wobble and try new tricks and her mom watched her with a smile.

Molly's bicycle was tight on days that it rained. But she always liked to take it out to feel the warm sun on her face. Her bicycle was her pride and joy and she would never trade it for anything else in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a cozy hole in the wall of a big house. One day, Timmy went outside to look for some cheese. He saw a big cat that looked very dangerous. The cat saw Timmy and said, "Hello little mouse, what are you doing out here all alone?" Timmy replied, "I'm just looking for some cheese." The cat smiled and said, "Well, be careful little mouse. I might eat you for lunch!" Timmy quickly ran back to his cozy hole and was happy to be safe at home.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy was playing in the park with his friends. They were having fun playing tag and hide-and-seek. Suddenly, Timmy saw something shiny on the ground. He went to pick it up and saw that it was a cool pistol.

Timmy's friend, Billy, saw the pistol too and said, "Wow, that's so cool! Can I hold it?"

Timmy replied, "Sure, but be careful. Don't point it at anyone."

Billy took the pistol and laid it on the ground. They all looked at it and wondered where it came from. Then, they heard a loud voice saying, "Hey kids, what are you doing with my pistol?"

It was the park ranger. He explained that the pistol belonged to him and that it was not a toy. The kids apologized and promised to never touch it again. They continued playing, happy to have learned an important lesson about safety.

John looked out of the open window and saw the rain falling. He felt sad because he couldn't go outside and play.

His mom saw this and said, "Why don't we stretch our bodies?"

John smiled and said, "Yes!"

So, they both put on their warm clothes and opened the door. The cold rain hit their faces and they both began to stretch. They reached up to the sky with their hands and toes pointed to the ground.

After they had finished their stretching, John's mom said, "Let's go inside, I'm getting wet!"

John laughed and said, "OK. Next time, can we stretch when it's sunny?"

His mom smiled and said, "Sure thing!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Katy. Every day, Katy and her Dad would go to the park. Today, Katy wanted something special. She asked her Dad if they could go to the video store.

Katy's Dad said yes, so they went to the video store. When they arrived, Katy looked around and saw lots of delicious videos. She pointed to a video and said to her Dad, â€œCan I order this one?"

Her Dad said, â€œNo, Katy, you shouldn't order anything without asking. You should always be polite and ask first."

Katy nodded and said, â€œI remember. Sorry, Dad.â€

Katy's Dad smiled and said, â€œIt's okay. You can order the video if you ask nicely.â€

So, Katy asked and said, â€œMay I please order the video?"

Her Dad said, â€œYes, of course you can.â€

Katy was so happy that she could order the video. This taught her an important lesson: always be polite and ask nicely before ordering anything.

Once upon a time, in a modest little house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy weapon, a small sword. He loved to play with it every day.

One day, Tim was playing with his toy sword in the park. A bigger boy named Max came up to Tim and tried to take his toy weapon away. Tim did not want to give it to Max. They both wanted the toy sword.

Tim was scared but he knew what to do. He went to his mom and told her what happened. His mom went to Max's mom and told her too. Max's mom told Max to give the toy sword back to Tim.

Tim was happy to have his toy sword back. He played with it all day long. He learned that it is important to tell someone when you need help. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big yellow slide that looked fun. They ran to the slide and waited for their turn.

"Can I go first?" Lily asked Tom.

"OK, you can go first," Tom said. He was a good brother.

Lily climbed up the steps of the slide. She was very happy. She looked down and saw Tom waiting for her. She smiled and waved. Then she slid down the slide.

But when she reached the bottom, she saw something strange. A big yellow dog appeared next to the slide. It had a long tail and floppy ears. It looked friendly, but Lily was scared. She did not know the dog.

"Tom, Tom, help!" Lily cried. She ran to Tom and hugged him.

Tom saw the dog too. He was not scared. He liked dogs. He walked to the dog and said, "Hello, dog. What is your name?"

The dog wagged its tail and licked Tom's face. It barked and said, "Woof, woof. My name is Sunny. I live in the park. I like to play with children."

Tom laughed and petted the dog. He said, "Hi, Sunny. You are a nice dog. Do you want to play with us?"

Sunny nodded and said, "Yes, yes. I want to play with you. Can I go on the slide too?"

Tom looked at Lily and said, "Lily, this is Sunny. He is a friendly dog. He wants to play with us. Can he go on the slide too?"

Lily looked at the dog. She saw that he was not mean. He was just lonely. She felt sorry for him. She said, "OK, Sunny can go on the slide too. But he has to wait his turn."

Sunny barked and said, "Thank you, thank you. You are very kind. I will wait my turn."

Lily and Tom and Sunny played on the slide. They had a lot of fun. They became friends. They were happy.

Once there was a wise owl. He lived in a tall tree. One day he was feeling grumpy and he wanted to do something fun. So he decided to build a stack. But it didn't turn out the way he planned. 

The stack just kept getting higher and higher. Soon it was the highest stack ever made! The wise owl was so excited that he started to yell out loud. Everyone in the forest heard him and came to see the tall stack. 

The animals all cheered and clapped for the wise owl. They couldn't believe how big the stack was. They all thanked the wise owl for making such a fun stack. 

From then on, the wise owl would build a stack whenever he felt grumpy. It always cheered him up and made him happy. He became the most famous owl in the forest!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Mandy. Tom was very brave, and Mandy was very clever. One day, Tom and Mandy were walking through the forest. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise behind them.

They stopped and looked around. A scary monster was running towards them! Tom and Mandy were so scared!

Tom grabbed the nearest weapon he could find--a big stick. He bravely rushed at the monster, waving the stick and shouting. Mandy was impressed by Tom's courage.

"You are so brave!" cried Mandy.

"Haha, I have to be!" said Tom as he continued to rush at the monster.

The monster was no match for Tom's bravery and the weapon he was carrying. After a few more rushes, the monster backed away and ran away.

Mandy thanked Tom for his bravery and intelligence.

"You saved us!" she said.

Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome, my friend!"

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play outside when the weather is nice. Today, the sun is shining and the sky is blue. They go to the park with their moms.

"Look, Lily, a swing!" Ben says. He runs to the swing and sits on it. He pushes himself with his feet and goes up and down.

"Can I have a turn, Ben?" Lily asks. She likes swings too. She waits for Ben to stop.

Ben smiles and says, "Sure, Lily. You can have a turn. We can share the swing. Sharing is good."

He gets off the swing and helps Lily get on. He pushes her gently and she laughs. They take turns on the swing and have fun.

Their moms watch them and are grateful. They are grateful for the weather, for the park, and for their children. They are grateful for their friendship. They hug each other and say, "We are lucky to have each other."

Tom and Sue like to play in the park. They see a big pond with many fish. They want to catch some fish. They find a rod and a hook near a bench. They think someone left it there.

"Look, Tom, a rod! Let's use it to catch fish!" Sue says.

"OK, Sue, but be careful. The hook is sharp. It can hurt you." Tom says.

They take the rod and the hook and go to the pond. They put the hook in the water and wait. Soon, a fish comes and bites the hook. Sue pulls the rod and the fish comes out of the water.

"Wow, Sue, you caught a fish! It is big and shiny!" Tom says.

But the fish is not a normal fish. It has big teeth and eyes. It is a mysterious fish. It is angry and scared. It opens its mouth and bites Sue's hand. Sue screams and drops the rod and the fish.

"Ow, ow, ow! The fish bit me! It hurts!" Sue cries.

Tom runs to Sue and tries to help her. But the fish is still on the hook. It swings and hits Tom's head. Tom falls and hits his head on a rock. He bleeds and does not move.

"Tom, Tom, wake up! Please, wake up!" Sue cries.

But Tom does not wake up. He is very hurt. The fish is still angry and scared. It tries to get free. It makes a loud noise.

The noise attracts a big dog. The dog sees the fish and the rod. It thinks they are toys. It runs to them and grabs them with its mouth. It shakes them and tears them. The fish dies. The rod breaks.

The dog sees Sue and Tom. It thinks they are also toys. It runs to them and bites them. Sue and Tom scream and cry. They are very hurt. They cannot run away.

The dog plays with them until it gets bored. Then it leaves them alone. Sue and Tom lie on the ground. They are bleeding and crying. They are very sad and scared. They want their mom and dad. But no one comes to help them. They are alone in the park. The end.

Once upon a time there was a bell. Every day it would ring loud and clear. Everyone who heard it smiled and danced.

One day a little boy found a pin. He was so excited that he did not see the broken part. He picked it up, and ran to the bell with the pin.

He carefully put the pin in the bell and then he stepped back to watch the magic. He watched and waited, and then, at last, the bell began to ring.

The little boy smiled and danced. He was so happy that he had made the bell ring. And so everyone in the village could enjoy the beautiful sound of the bell.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to sleep. He would sleep all the time, no matter where he was. One day, he was sleeping in his bed when a strange man walked in the room. The boy was scared and he jumped up. The man said to him, "Don't worry. I'm a fine man and I only want to say hello to you." The boy smiled and said hello back. The stranger said goodbye, and the boy was happy to see him go. The boy went back to sleep, feeling safe and fine. The end.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the woods. They had a big ball that they would roll down the hill and chase after. One day, they saw a big axe near a tree. Tom wanted to touch it, but Sam was fearful.

"Tom, don't touch the axe. It is sharp and can hurt you," Sam said.

"But it looks fun. I want to see how it works," Tom said. He did not listen to Sam and picked up the axe. He swung it around and tried to chop the tree.

Sam watched with fear as Tom played with the axe. He saw a big branch above Tom's head. It looked like it was going to fall. Sam shouted, "Tom, watch out! The branch is falling!"

Tom heard Sam and looked up. He saw the branch coming down fast. He dropped the axe and tried to roll away. But he was too late. The branch hit him on the leg and made him cry.

Sam ran to Tom and hugged him. He was sorry for his brother. He said, "Tom, are you okay? I told you not to touch the axe. It is dangerous."

Tom was in pain and felt sorry too. He said, "Sam, you were right. I was foolish. I should have listened to you. I'm sorry."

They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and to listen to each other. They never played with the axe again. They only played with their ball. They were happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a pupil named Tim. Tim was a restless boy who liked to run and play all day. One day, Tim saw a girl named Sue. Sue was very nice and they became good friends.

One day, Tim and Sue had a big fight. Tim wanted to play with his toy car, but Sue wanted to play with her doll. They could not agree on what to play. This made them very sad.

Then, Tim had an idea. He asked Sue, "Will you marry me when we grow up?" Sue thought about it and said, "Yes, I will marry you." They were happy again and played together all day.

Tom and Mia were playing on the beach. They liked to make sand castles and look for shells. They saw a big boat in the water. It was loud and smoky. They wondered what it was doing.

"Look, Mia, there are dolphins!" Tom said, pointing to the water. He saw some gray and white shapes jumping and splashing. They were beautiful and fast. Mia smiled and clapped her hands. She loved dolphins.

But the boat did not like the dolphins. It had a big net that it threw into the water. It wanted to catch the dolphins and take them away. The dolphins were scared and tried to swim away. But the net was too big and strong. Some of the dolphins got stuck in the net. They cried and struggled.

"Stop, stop, stop!" Tom shouted at the boat. He was angry and sad. He did not want the boat to hurt the dolphins. He wanted the dolphins to be free and happy. Mia shouted too. She wanted to help the dolphins.

The boat did not hear them. It pulled the net closer and closer. The dolphins were in trouble. They had no way out. They had to surrender. They stopped fighting and waited for the boat to take them.

But then, something amazing happened. A big wave came and hit the boat. It made the boat shake and tilt. The net fell into the water and opened. The dolphins saw their chance. They quickly swam out of the net and away from the boat. They were free again. They thanked the wave and the sea for saving them.

Tom and Mia cheered and clapped. They were so happy for the dolphins. They waved at them and said goodbye. The dolphins waved back and smiled. They were grateful to Tom and Mia for caring about them. They were humble and kind. They hoped to see them again. They jumped and splashed and made a big splash. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to know more about magnets. She asked her mom, â€œWhat are magnets?â€ Her mom told her, â€œMagnets are very impressive. They pull things to them.â€

Lily was excited. She wanted to see a magnet for herself. She went to the store and found the most incredible magnet. It was a rainbow and it glittered in the light.

Lily was so excited and she wanted to show her friends what she knew about magnets. She took out the magnet and showed them how it would attract things. It was so impressive! Her friends were so amazed. They all learned more about magnets.

Lily was proud. She now knew a lot about magnets and had an impressive rainbow magnet to show her friends. She was so happy that she had learned something new.

Once there was a big pirate ship. It was old, but the crew loved it. They had a captain who was very bossy. He would always request them to do a lot of work.

One day, the crew heard a strange noise. It was coming from a small boat. The crew looked out and saw a little pirate. He was a very brave pirate and he requested to join the big ship. 

The captain told the little pirate that he was too small to join the crew. However, the little pirate was very bossy and clever. He asked the captain to give him a chance and the captain agreed.

The little pirate proved to be a great help for the captain and the crew. He was always helping them with their work and soon, everyone on the ship got used to having the little pirate around. 

The little pirate was so brave and everyone on the ship was proud of him. They had found a new friend who was really bossy, but also super helpful.

Lily and Tom are playing with blocks. They want to make a big tower. They add more and more blocks to the tower. They are happy.

But then, a big wind comes. It blows on the tower. The tower falls down. Lily and Tom are sad.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "Our tower is gone!"

Tom has an idea. He says, "Let's make a new tower. But this time, let's use some rub."

"What is rub?" Lily asks.

"Rub is something sticky. It can hold the blocks together. Look, I have some rub here." Tom shows Lily a tube of glue.

"Wow!" Lily says. "How do we use it?"

Tom says, "We put some rub on the blocks. Then we stick them together. Like this." Tom squeezes some glue on a block and sticks it to another block.

Lily tries it too. She says, "This is fun!"

They use the rub to make a new tower. The tower is bigger and stronger than before. They are proud.

The big wind comes again. It blows on the tower. But the tower does not fall down. The rub holds the blocks together. The tower is mighty.

Lily and Tom cheer. They say, "We did it! We made a mighty tower!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to class every day to play with her friends and learn new things. One day, Lily's teacher brought a fragile vase to show the class. It was very pretty, but they had to be careful not to break it.

Suddenly, it started to rain outside and the wind blew hard. The raindrops were tapping on the window, and Lily and her friends watched as the rain poured down. They were happy to be inside, safe and dry.

After class, Lily's mom picked her up and they walked home in the rain. Lily splashed in the puddles and laughed as the raindrops fell on her face. When they got home, they cuddled up with a warm blanket and watched the rain fall outside. It was a cozy and peaceful day.

Lily and Tom were going to the park with Mom. They liked the park. They could play on the swings, slide down the slide, and run on the grass. They were very happy.

But on the way, they saw a cat. The cat was on the road. It looked scared and hurt. It had a cut on its leg. Lily and Tom felt sorry for the cat. They wanted to help it.

"Mom, can we stop and help the cat?" Lily asked.

"Of course, dear. We can delay going to the park for a little while. The cat needs our help. You are very compassionate, Lily and Tom," Mom said.

Mom parked the car and got out. She took a blanket and a bottle of water from the trunk. She gently wrapped the cat in the blanket and gave it some water. The cat purred and licked Mom's hand.

"Thank you, Mom. You are very kind," the cat seemed to say.

Lily and Tom smiled. They were glad the cat was feeling better. They petted the cat and talked to it softly.

"Can we take the cat home, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Well, we have to find out if the cat has a home already. Maybe it has a collar or a tag with its name and address. If not, we can take it to the vet and see if they can find its owner. If no one claims the cat, then maybe we can adopt it. How does that sound?" Mom asked.

Lily and Tom nodded. They liked that idea. They hoped the cat would be their new friend.

They got back in the car and drove to the vet. They did not mind delaying going to the park. They had found a better way to spend their day. They had shown compassion to a cat in need. And they had learned a valuable lesson. Sometimes, helping others is more fun than playing.

Lily was nervous. She had to do something new today. She had to go to school. She did not know the school or the teacher or the other kids. She wanted to stay home with Mom and Dad and play with her toys.

Mom and Dad took Lily to the school. They walked with her to the classroom. They saw the teacher. She was smiling and friendly. She said, "Hello, Lily. I'm Miss Lee. I'm your teacher. Welcome to school. You will have fun here. You will learn and play and make friends."

Lily looked at the teacher. She looked at the classroom. She saw many things. She saw books and crayons and puzzles and blocks. She saw a big rug and a small table and some chairs. She saw some kids. They were sitting on the rug. They were listening to a story. Some of them looked at Lily. They smiled and waved.

Mom and Dad said, "Lily, this is your school. This is your teacher. These are your classmates. They are nice. They want to play with you. You will like school. We will come back later to pick you up. We love you. Have a good day."

Lily felt a little less nervous. She said, "Bye, Mom. Bye, Dad. I love you too. I will try school." She gave them a hug and a kiss. She took her backpack and followed the teacher. The teacher said, "Lily, come and join us. We are reading a story about a cat and a mouse. Do you like stories?" Lily nodded. She liked stories. She sat on the rug next to a girl. The girl said, "Hi, Lily. I'm Mia. Do you want to be my friend?" Lily smiled. She said, "Hi, Mia. Yes, I want to be your friend." She felt a little more happy. She listened to the story. She did something new today. She went to school.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spike. Spike was a big dog with a lot of fur. One day, Spike went to the park with his owner. At the park, Spike saw a fancy lady with a pretty dress. She had a bag with treats for dogs. Spike barked and wagged his tail. The lady gave Spike a treat and he was very happy. Spike loved going to the park and meeting new friends.

One day, a green frog named Mark was playing near the pond. He liked to jump and stretch his long legs. He saw a big leaf and decided to jump on it.

"Ribbit, watch me stretch and jump," said Mark to his friend, a little bird. The bird watched as Mark stretched his legs and jumped high in the air. Mark landed on the big leaf, and it made a funny sound.

The little bird laughed and said, "That was a great jump, Mark! Let's play together." So, Mark and the little bird played all day, stretching and jumping from leaf to leaf. They had so much fun, and they were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Katie. She was very adventurous and loved to explore the world around her. One day, Katie was walking through the forest with her mother and they came across a small pond.

"Look, Mom!" Katie said, pointing at the pond. "Look at all the fish swimming inside!"

Her mother smiled and mentioned how the pond water was so clear and the fish were very colorful.

"Do you think that's special, Mommy?" Katie asked.

"Not really, sweetie," her mother replied. "Ordinary things are special, too." She pointed to the sauce they had been spreading on their sandwiches while they were walking. "For example, this sauce is ordinary, but it's delicious!"

Katie thought about this for a moment and then smiled. She understood that ordinary things could be special. You just had to look at them in a different way.

The moral of Katie's story is that ordinary things can be special, too. So the next time you come across something ordinary, don't forget that it can be just as special as something extraordinary.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going on adventures, so he decided to take a journey through the forest. He packed his backpack with snacks and water, and set off on his journey.

As he walked through the forest, he saw a big zip line hanging from a tree. Timmy was very excited and decided to try it out. He zipped down the line with a big smile on his face.

But then, something serious happened. Timmy tripped and fell off the zip line. He hurt his head and couldn't get up. He was all alone in the forest, and no one could hear him cry for help.

Sadly, Timmy never made it home from his journey. His family searched for him, but they never found him. They were very sad and missed him very much.

Once there was a little boy who was very eager to explore the world. One day, the boy discovered a big and colorful tunnel. He wanted to go inside the tunnel, but his mom didn't allow it.

Instead, his mom said that he could look from the entrance of the tunnel and see the wonderful colors coming from it. As the boy looked, he saw that the tunnel was full of all sorts of colors: blues, reds, yellows and greens.

The little boy stared and stared at the tunnel, until his mom said it was time to go home. He reluctantly left and promised himself that he would come back and explore more of the colorful tunnel someday soon.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play together in the park. One day, Tom has a gift for Anna. He gives her a big box with a bow.

"What is it?" Anna asks.

"Open it and see," Tom says.

Anna opens the box. Inside is a toy dinosaur. It is green and has sharp teeth. Anna thinks it is scary.

"Ah!" Anna screams. She drops the box and runs away.

Tom is sad. He likes the dinosaur. He thinks it is cool.

"Why are you scared?" Tom asks. "It is not real. It is just a toy."

Anna stops and looks at Tom. She sees that he is holding the dinosaur. He is not scared. He is smiling.

"Are you sure?" Anna asks.

"Yes, I am sure," Tom says. "Look, it can make noises. Roar!"

He presses a button on the dinosaur. It makes a loud roar. Anna jumps.

"Wow, that is loud," Anna says.

"But it is fun," Tom says. "Do you want to try?"

Anna is curious. She walks back to Tom. She takes the dinosaur from him. She presses the button. It roars again.

"Roar!" Anna says. She laughs.

Tom laughs too. He is happy. He admires Anna. She is brave.

"Thank you for the gift, Tom," Anna says. "It is scary, but it is also cool. I like it."

"You are welcome, Anna," Tom says. "You are my best friend."

They hug. They play with the dinosaur. They have fun.

Once upon a time, a curious bunny was hopping in the forest. The bunny saw a trap on the ground. The trap was made of metal and had sharp teeth. The bunny knew it was dangerous, so it didn't go near it. 

Suddenly, the bunny saw a carrot on the other side of the trap. The bunny really wanted the carrot, but it didn't want to get caught in the trap. So, the bunny had an idea. It decided to part the trap in the middle with a stick. 

The bunny was able to get the carrot without getting caught in the trap. It was happy and ate the carrot. From that day on, the bunny was very careful when it saw traps in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the rain. One day, Timmy went outside to play and found a big hole in his backyard. He leaned over to look inside the hole and saw that it was very deep. 

Suddenly, Timmy's little sister, Lily, came outside and wanted to play too. She saw Timmy leaning over the hole and wanted to see what he was looking at. Timmy told her it was a big hole and that she shouldn't lean over it because it was wet and slippery. 

Lily didn't listen and leaned over the hole anyway. She slipped and fell into the hole! Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. He ran inside to tell his mom and dad. They came outside and helped get Lily out of the hole. From then on, Timmy and Lily knew to be careful around holes and always listen to each other.

Once there was a big black bear who liked to run. Everywhere he went he would turn and look around to see if he was being followed. One day, he got very tired and stopped to take a rest.

Suddenly, he heard something behind him. He turned and saw a little girl wearing a pink dress. She was looking right at him with a friendly smile.

"Hello!" said the little girl.

The black bear smiled back. "Hello!" he replied.

The little girl asked, "What were you doing?"

"I was running," the black bear replied.

The little girl smiled and said, "I like to run too! Can I run with you?"

The black bear was so happy, he nodded his head and said, "Yes, let's go!"

So the little girl and the big black bear went running together, turning and looking around and making sure no one was following them. They had a lot of fun running around and before long, they had forgotten all about being tired.

Lily wanted to help Mommy decorate the big green tree. She saw many shiny things that Mommy hung on the tree. They were called ornaments. Lily liked the ornaments. She wanted to touch them and play with them.

She reached for a red ball that looked like a shiny apple. But when she pulled it, it fell off the tree and broke on the floor. Lily heard a loud noise and saw many pieces of the red ball. She felt scared and sad. She started to cry.

Mommy heard Lily cry and came to see what happened. She saw the broken ornament and the mess on the floor. She felt frustrated and angry. She said to Lily, "Why did you do that? You know you are not supposed to touch the ornaments. They are not toys. They are fragile. You could have hurt yourself. You made a big mess. You embarrassed me."

Lily felt worse. She did not mean to break the ornament. She did not mean to make Mommy angry. She did not mean to embarrass Mommy. She said to Mommy, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I just wanted to help. I just wanted to see the shiny thing. I didn't know it would break. Please don't be mad at me. Please don't be embarrassed by me."

Mommy saw Lily's tears and heard her words. She felt sorry for Lily. She realized that Lily was just curious and did not understand. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm not mad at you. I'm not embarrassed by you. I love you. You are my little helper. But you have to be careful with the ornaments. They are not for playing. They are for looking. Next time, ask me before you touch them. Okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mommy. I love you too. Can I still help you decorate the tree?"

Mommy smiled and said, "Of course you can. But only with the soft ornaments. Like this one." She gave Lily a fluffy snowman that had a carrot nose and a hat. Lily smiled and hung it on the tree. She felt happy and proud. She helped Mommy decorate the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He lived in a small house with his mom, dad, and a humble cat named Muffin. They were a happy family.

One day, Tim's dad went to work. He worked with coal, a black rock that people use for heat. Tim wanted to join his dad at work, but he was too little. So he played with Muffin instead.

After a fun day of playing, Tim's dad came home. He was covered in coal dust. Tim laughed and gave his dad a big hug. Then they all had dinner together. The end.

Ben and Mia are playing in the garden. They have a big bucket of water and some cups. They like to fill the cups and pour the water on the flowers and the grass.

"Look, Mia, this flower is very pretty. It has many colors," Ben says, holding a cup of water.

"Yes, it is. Let me see," Mia says, walking towards Ben.

But Ben is naughty. He splashes the water on Mia's face and laughs. "Ha ha, you are wet!"

Mia is not happy. She feels the water on her eyes and nose and mouth. She is cold and angry. She grabs another cup of water and throws it at Ben. "No, you are wet!"

They start a water fight. They run and chase and splash each other. They have fun, but they also soak their clothes and shoes and hair.

Suddenly, they hear a loud sound. It is the bell. It is time to go inside. Mom is calling them for lunch.

"Come on, Ben and Mia, lunch is ready. What are you doing?" Mom says, looking at them.

They stop and look at each other. They are dripping and dirty and hungry. They smile sheepishly.

"We are playing with water, Mom. It is interesting," they say together.

Mom shakes her head and laughs. "You are silly. Come on, let's go and dry you up. And then you can tell me all about your interesting game."

Bob was very excited to go to the park today. He had been waiting for so long! He ran outside, but his mom insisted that he wear his coat. Bob grumbled and groaned. Eventually, he reluctantly put it on and they left. 

At the park, Bob found the perfect climbing structure. He wanted to climb it all the way to the top, but his mom insisted he only go to the middle. Bob asked to go higher, but his mom said no. Bob started to complain, but his mom said he had to listen to her. 

Suddenly, an idea occurred to Bob. He had an escape plan! He pretended to listen to his mom and he went to the middle of the structure. Then he ran to the top of it, smiling all the way. His mom was so surprised that she couldn't react quickly enough. Bob was so excited to have escaped his mom's rules! He had climbed to the very top of the structure. He celebrated by raising his arms in victory. 

Bob's mom finally reached the top, very annoyed. She said, "That was very naughty of you, Bob". Bob said, "I'm sorry, mommy. I just wanted to feel like I had escaped the rules". His mom said, "Well then, next time you feel like escaping, be sure to ask me before you act!" Bob agreed, but inside he was still very excited.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play with toys. They have a big box of toys. They have cars, dolls, balls, and books. They also have a dragon. The dragon is green and soft. It can make sounds. Lily and Max like to pretend that the dragon is real.

One day, they decide to play a game. They want to make the dragon fly. They think of a plan. They find a long stick and a string. They tie the string to the dragon's tail. They hold the stick and the string. They run around the room. They make the dragon lift in the air.

"Look, the dragon is flying!" Lily says. "It is so fast and strong!"

"Yes, it is!" Max says. "It is the best dragon ever!"

They have fun with the dragon. They make it go up and down. They make it roar and breathe fire. They pretend that the dragon is their friend. They are happy.

But then, something happens. The string breaks. The dragon falls to the floor. It stops making sounds. Lily and Max are sad. They run to the dragon. They hug it.

"Oh no, the dragon is broken!" Lily says. "What can we do?"

"I don't know," Max says. "Maybe we can fix it."

They look at the dragon. They see a button on its back. They press the button. The dragon makes a beep. It opens its eyes. It starts to make sounds again.

"Wow, the dragon is not broken!" Lily says. "It is a modern dragon!"

"Yes, it is!" Max says. "It is a smart dragon!"

They are happy again. They play with the dragon. They love the dragon. The dragon loves them. They are friends.

One day a little girl had an idea. She wanted to build a nice, soft fort out of sacks. She ran to the sack and asked her mom if she could take one. Her mom said yes and she started to drag it to her room.

The little girl started to build the fort. She arranged the sack in a circle and tucked them in so they were nice and soft. She put some pillows, a blanket, stuffed animals and books inside.

The little girl was so proud of her fort. She jumped inside and felt so safe. She brought a special storybook and read it quietly until she felt very sleepy. Then, she hugged her stuffed animal and fell asleep in her soft little fort.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Max. Max loved to run and play outside. One day, Max found a trail in the woods. He was very excited to see where it went.

Max walked on the trail and saw many things. He saw big trees, pretty flowers, and little bugs. Max wanted to protect all his new friends in the woods. He barked at the birds to keep them safe.

At the end of the trail, Max found a big lake. He jumped in and splashed around. Max was very happy to find such a fun place. He knew he would come back to the trail and protect his friends every day. And Max lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a colorful shield that she loved to play with. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her shield. She saw a boy who was sad because he lost his toy. Lily wanted to help the boy, so she signed to him that she would help him find his toy. 

Lily and the boy looked all around the park, but they couldn't find the toy. Lily didn't give up, though. She kept looking until they finally found the toy. The boy was so happy and he thanked Lily for helping him. 

Lily learned that it's important to help others when they need it. She felt proud of herself for being kind and helpful. From that day on, Lily always carried her colorful shield with her, as a reminder to be a good friend and help others.

Once there was a penguin named Sam. Sam was a compassionate penguin who always tried hard to help others. One day, Sam noticed that some of his animal friends had no homes, so he decided to try and help them find a place to stay.

Sam set off on a mission to find his animal friends a cozy place to live. He searched and searched until he finally spotted something special in the distance. It was an igloo! Sam was so excited to see it.

Sam quickly rushed to his animal friends and told them about the igloo. They were all so grateful for Sam's help. Together, they decided to try and move into the igloo. With lots of effort and patience, Sam and his animal friends managed to settle into their lovely new igloo.

The animal friends were so happy and thanked Sam for his compassion. "You are the best," said one of the animals. Sam smiled and said, "Thank you, I just wanted to help."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and dress up in her pretty dresses. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to clean up her room and organize her toys. Lily didn't want to do it, but she knew it was important to listen to her mommy.

As she was cleaning, Lily found a shiny mirror under her bed. She picked it up and looked at herself. She smiled and saw that her hair was messy. She decided to use her brush to fix it. When she was done, she put the mirror back where she found it.

After Lily finished cleaning, she felt proud of herself. She went to her mommy and said, "Look mommy, my room is clean and organized!" Her mommy was happy and gave her a big hug. Lily felt happy too and went to play with her toys with her room open and bright.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park near her house. One day, she saw a big fountain in the middle of the park. She was so excited to see it!

Lily wanted to touch the fountain, but her mom told her not to. She said it was lucky to throw a coin into the fountain and make a wish. Lily didn't understand why it was lucky, but she listened to her mom.

As they were leaving the park, Lily saw a boy who threw a whole handful of coins into the fountain. She thought it was silly, but the boy said he was hoping to get rich. Lily turned to her mom and said, "I don't think that's how luck works."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's right, Lily. Luck isn't about getting rich. It's about being grateful for what you have." Lily felt lucky to have such a wise mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Princess Emily. She was only three years old and she was very excited to meet all the people in her town. Everywhere she went, she smiled and waved to all the people she saw.

One day, on her way to school, she saw a new boy in her neighbourhood. He was standing alone, looking a bit sad. Princess Emily walked up to him, smiled and said "Hi! What's your name?".

The boy was a bit shocked and didn't say anything. Princess Emily tried again and asked the same question, but the boy still didn't answer. She started to feel a bit frustrated and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, another little boy ran up to the sad boy and started to talk to him. Then, the sad boy smiled and waved to Princess Emily! He said his name was Joe and he was very glad to meet her.

Princess Emily was so happy that she had made Joe feel better. She waved goodbye with a big smile and they decided to meet again the next day.
