Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived with her mommy. The little girl was always excited to see her mommy. Every night her mother would come home from work and give her a big hug.

Tonight was different. When her mommy came home, there was something special in her hands. The girl was so excited! She knew it must be something special.

Her mother opened her hands, and a bright light glowed from them. It was the most beautiful thing the girl had ever seen. The bright light kept getting brighter and brighter.

The girl's mother told her the light was a special gift just for her. She said it was a magical glow that could only be seen by special people and always stay close to her.

The little girl hugged her mommy tightly and thanked her. She knew everything was going to be alright, because she always had her special glow to protect her, and her mommy watching over her.

There was a wall in the bedroom. It was tall and thick. It was there for a long time. 

One day, a fast truck came and brought a new wall. It was bigger and brighter. The workers put the new wall in place of the old wall. They took away the old wall and replaced it with the new one. 

The new wall looked shiny and pretty. Everyone was very happy. It was much better than the old wall.

The family had so much fun with the new wall. They hung up toys and made it a play area. They used it as a background for fun family photos. They had many hours of enjoyment with the new wall. 

The new wall was much better than the old one. It was faster, brighter and it made everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Betsy. Betsy loved to eat pastries, especially ones with sprinkles on top. One day, Betsy saw a little bird trying to build a nest in a tree. 

But Betsy didn't like the bird because it made too much noise. She decided to ignore the bird and keep eating her pastry. But the bird didn't give up and kept chirping louder and louder. 

Betsy got angry and tried to scare the bird away, but it wouldn't budge. She realized that ignoring the bird wasn't the right thing to do. So, she decided to share her pastry with the bird as a peace offering. 

The bird happily accepted the pastry and Betsy learned that sometimes it's better to be kind and not ignore others. From that day on, Betsy and the bird became good friends and Betsy even helped the bird build its nest. The end.

One day, there was a careless pilot who decided to change their plans. They wanted to go on a special adventure. So, the pilot got into their plane and began flying. They flew up high in the sky and as they flew, they started to change direction.

The pilot flew higher and higher until they reached the clouds and felt so happy. But then, a big change happened. Suddenly, the plane started to shake and swerve back and forth. The pilot had become careless and forgotten to check the weather.

The pilot started to worry and tried to make the plane change direction, but it didn't seem to work. The plane kept shaking and swaying. Eventually, the pilot was able to get the plane under control and flew back to the ground safely.

The careless pilot learned an important lesson that day - to be careful when flying and always check the weather first!

Tim and Sue liked to play in the park with their dog, Max. They liked to run, slide, swing and throw a ball for Max to catch. One day, they saw a big van in the park. It was white and had many pictures on it. They wanted to see what was inside.

They walked to the van and saw a door. They opened the door and saw many books and toys. They were very happy and started to look at them. They did not see the elderly man who was sleeping in the back of the van. He was the owner of the van and he was very tired.

The elderly man woke up and heard some noise. He got up and went to the front of the van. He saw Tim and Sue playing with his books and toys. He was not happy and shouted at them. He told them to get out of his van and leave his things alone.

Tim and Sue were very scared and ran out of the van. They grabbed Max and ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. They told her what happened and she hugged them. She told them they should not go inside a stranger's van without asking. She said it was not safe and it was not nice.

Tim and Sue said they were sorry and they learned their lesson. They said they would not do it again. They asked their mom if they could play some more in the park. She said yes, but they had to stay close to her. They agreed and went to play. They saw the elderly man drive away in his van. They waved at him and said sorry. He waved back and smiled. He was not so angry anymore. He lay down in his van and took a nap. He dreamed of his books and toys.

Anna and Ben love to play soccer. They have a small ball and two goals in their backyard. They pretend they are in a big stadium with many people watching them. They cheer and clap when they score a goal.

One day, their mom tells them they can go to a real stadium. She has tickets for a soccer game. Anna and Ben are very happy. They put on their soccer shirts and hats. They get in the car with their mom and dad.

At the stadium, they see many people wearing different colors. They hear loud noises and music. They find their seats and watch the players on the field. They see their favorite team in blue and white. They shout and wave their flags.

The game is very exciting. Both teams try to score goals. Sometimes, the ball hits the post or goes over the bar. Sometimes, the goalkeeper makes a great save. Anna and Ben cheer and boo with the crowd.

Near the end of the game, the score is tied. The blue and white team has a chance to win. One of their players runs with the ball and shoots. The ball flies towards the goal. But the goalkeeper from the other team jumps and reaches the ball. He saves it with his hand. The crowd gasps.

"Wow, what a save!" Ben says.

"That was so close!" Anna says.

The game ends in a draw. The players shake hands and thank the fans. Anna and Ben clap and smile. They had a lot of fun. They think the stadium is beautiful. They want to come back again. They hug their mom and dad and say thank you. They go home and dream of playing soccer in the stadium.

Once upon a time, there was a big blue door. Every day, the door shut tight and made a terrible noise. One day, a 3 year old boy named Sam was playing near the door. He heard a strange noise coming from the door and put his hand in his pocket.

Sam: "What is that noise?"

Sam's mom: "That's the door. It shuts every day."

Sam: "Why does it make a terrible noise?"

Sam's mom: "That's just how it works. It shuts tight so it can stay closed."

Sam thought about this for a minute. He put his hand back in his pocket and looked at the door. He thought it was very strange that the door made such a terrible noise. But he decided he liked it anyway. He smiled and said, "I like the door."

One day, Bob saw something amazing. In the sky, he saw a giant oak tree. The oak tree was tall and strong, with wide branches and a thick trunk. Bob was in awe and could not look away from the oak tree. 

Bob wanted to get closer to the tree, so he decided to climb. He was brave and determined, so nothing could stop him. Bob was about to climb the tree when he heard a loud rumble. Suddenly, everything began to change.

The ground shook and the wind blew fiercely. Bob was alert and scared, so he quickly climbed down from the tree. Standing on the ground, Bob watched as the oak tree changed from a majestic state to a pile of rubble. 

Bob was shocked and confused, but he also felt a sense of awe. He knew that the oak tree was gone, but he was thankful that he had the chance to see it and experience its beauty before it changed.

Tom and Sue were at the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Mom and Dad said they could have a picnic later, but first they had to wait for the tide to go down.

"Why do we have to wait?" Tom asked.

"Because we want to find some oysters," Dad said. "Oysters are yummy and they live in the water. But when the water is too high, we can't see them or reach them. We have to wait until the water is low and then we can dig them out."

"What do oysters look like?" Sue asked.

"Oysters are round and hard and gray," Mom said. "They have a wide mouth that opens and closes. Inside, they have a soft part that we can eat. But we have to be careful, because sometimes they have a sharp thing inside that can hurt us. It's called a pearl."

"A pearl?" Tom and Sue said. They wanted to see a pearl. They wondered if it was shiny and pretty.

They waited and waited for the water to go down. They played with their toys and made a sandcastle. They watched the birds and the boats. They saw some crabs and some fish. But they did not see any oysters.

"Can we have the picnic now?" Tom asked. He was hungry and tired of waiting.

"Not yet," Dad said. "The water is still too high. We have to delay the picnic a little longer. Trust me, it will be worth it."

Tom and Sue sighed. They did not like to delay. They wanted to eat and see the oysters and the pearls.

Finally, the water was low enough. Dad took a bucket and a shovel and walked to the edge of the water. He started to dig in the sand and the rocks. He looked for oysters.

"Come on, kids, help me find some oysters," he said.

Tom and Sue ran to join him. They helped him dig and look. They found some oysters. They were round and hard and gray, just like Mom said. They had a wide mouth that opened and closed.

Dad put the oysters in the bucket. He opened one with a knife. He showed Tom and Sue the soft part inside.

"See, this is what we can eat," he said. "It's delicious. Do you want to try?"

Tom and Sue shook their heads. They did not want to eat the soft part. It looked slimy and gross.

"Maybe later," Mom said. "Let's see if there are any pearls inside."

Dad opened another oyster. He looked inside. He smiled.

"Look, kids, we found a pearl!" he said. He showed them a small, shiny, white thing. It was a pearl. It was beautiful.

Tom and Sue gasped. They wanted to touch the pearl. They wanted to keep it.

"Can we have it, Dad?" they asked.

"Sure, you can have it," Dad said. "It's a lucky find. You can share it or take turns with it. It's yours."

Tom and Sue were happy. They thanked Dad. They hugged the pearl. They forgot about the picnic. They forgot about the delay. They only cared about the pearl. They had found a treasure.

Sara liked to paint. She had many colors and brushes. She painted flowers and birds and stars on paper. She was happy when she painted.

One day, she saw a new scooter in the yard. It was red and shiny. It had big wheels and a horn. Sara wanted to ride the scooter. She asked her mom.

"Mom, can I ride the scooter?" Sara said.

"No, Sara, that is not your scooter. That is Ben's scooter. He is your cousin. He will come to visit us soon. You can play with him and the scooter then." Mom said.

Sara was sad. She did not want to wait. She wanted to ride the scooter now. She had an idea. She took her paints and brushes. She went to the yard. She painted the scooter. She painted it with many colors. She painted flowers and birds and stars on the scooter. She thought it was pretty.

But Ben did not think so. When he came to visit, he saw his scooter. He was angry. He did not like the colors. He did not like the flowers and birds and stars. He thought his scooter was ugly.

"Who did this? Who painted my scooter?" Ben shouted.

"I did. I painted your scooter. I made it pretty." Sara said.

"No, you did not. You made it ugly. You ruined my scooter. I hate you." Ben said.

Sara was shocked. She did not understand. She thought Ben would like her painting. She thought he would be happy. She started to cry.

Mom heard the noise. She came to the yard. She saw the scooter. She saw Sara and Ben. She was not happy.

"Sara, why did you paint Ben's scooter? That was not nice. You should have asked him first. You should have respected his things." Mom said.

"Ben, why did you yell at Sara? That was not nice. You should have been kind. You should have appreciated her effort." Mom said.

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry. They said sorry.

"I'm sorry, Sara. I was mean. I know you wanted to make me happy. But I liked my scooter the way it was. Can we wash it?" Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I was naughty. I know you loved your scooter. I wanted to ride it. Can we share it?" Sara said.

Mom smiled. She hugged them. She helped them wash the scooter. She let them ride it together. They had fun. They became friends. They learned a lesson.

Once upon a time, a mom and dad had a son named James. He was 3 years old and loved the outdoors.

One day, James's parents told him, "It's time to go to the park." James was so excited that he jumped up, grabbed his shoes, and ran outside.

When they got to the park, James was in awe. He saw a big pond with birds floating on it, and the moment he saw them, he started pointing and saying "Look! Look!"

His mom said, "Do you believe that if you throw a penny in the water, the birds will bring you money?" James didn't understand what she said but he just kept looking and pointing at the birds.

Mom then said, "Here, why don't you try it?" She gave him a penny, but it was so heavy that James couldn't throw it far enough for the birds to get it.

His dad then said, "It's okay, James. You can keep the penny. One day you'll be able to throw it and know the magic of believing." 

James smiled and hugged his parents tight. He felt warm and happy inside. From that day on, he believed that money was magic.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had his own toy sword. He liked to play with his sword every day. He would pretend to be a brave knight, fighting dragons and saving the day.

One day, Tim saw a big, angry dog in his yard. The dog was barking very loud. Tim was scared, but he knew he had to protect his family. So, he grabbed his toy sword and went outside.

Tim waved his sword at the angry dog. The dog stopped barking and looked at Tim. Tim said, "Go away, dog!" The dog listened to Tim and went away. Tim felt very brave and happy. He knew his toy sword helped him be a hero that day.

Once upon a time there was a man. He was walking very fast. He didn't slow down, until he saw something shining in the grass. He looked closer, and he saw a big, pink Stop sign. He stopped so he wouldn't hit it. He looked around, but nothing was there. He scratched his head and looked normal.

Then he heard some noise. He looked in every direction, and then he saw another man. The other man was holding a shiny red ball. Suddenly, the man holding the ball started running away. The other man started to run after him.

He ran and ran, until he caught up to the other man. Then he stopped and said, "Hey, why are you running away so fast?"

The other man looked a bit scared and said, "I'm sorry, I was just trying to have some fun!"

The other man smiled and said, "That's OK. Let's just have a normal game of catch instead."

Once upon a time, there was a family. The mom, dad, and their two children. The two children were named Susie and John. One day the family decided to go on a zoom. 

They zoomed around in the car for a very long time. They enjoyed looking at the trees and sky. As they were zooming, they began to see lots of bright lights and make crazy sounds. 

John was amazed by the lights and wanted to get a closer look. So mom and dad decided to stop the car and let him out. He was so happy to explore. 

John saw something twinkling on the ground and he picked it up. It was a little rock! He was so excited to have found this treasure. But then, he started to think, maybe it had value. He thought it was too special to keep, so he put it back where he found it. 

John was proud of himself for valuing the little rock. He got back into the car and they continued with their zoom.

Once upon a time, there was a little robot named Robby. Robby liked to dress up in fun clothes. One day, he found a big box of dress-up clothes. He was so excited!

Robby tried to put on a hat, but it was too big. He asked his friend, Sally, "Can you help me dress up?" Sally was patient and kind. She said, "Of course, I will help you, Robby!" Sally helped Robby put on a small hat and a pretty scarf. They laughed and played together.

The moral of the story is to be patient and help your friends. When you are kind and patient, you can have a lot of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint with her fingers and make pretty pictures. One day, she went for a walk and found a lonely stone on the ground. 

Lily felt sad for the stone because it was all alone. So, she decided to paint it with pretty colors to make it happy. She used her red, blue, and yellow paint to make a rainbow on the stone. 

Now, the stone was no longer lonely. It had a friend in Lily and a pretty rainbow to look at. Lily was happy too because she made a new friend and painted something beautiful. From that day on, Lily always painted stones when she went for walks, and she never felt lonely again.

One day, Sally was spinning in her room. She spun around and around and around, so fast that her dress started to spin and her hair twirled around her ears. She spun so quickly and so dizzyingly that she made herself feel like she was flying. 

After a few minutes, Sally stopped spinning and saw a purple, round orange spinning on the floor. She bent down to pick it up, and realized it was a lollipop. She smiled to herself and it crawled up to her mouth, when suddenly, she heard her mom's voice in the living room. 

"Sally!" shouted her mom, "What have you done?"

Sally thought she was in trouble. She had forgotten that she was not allowed to eat sugary treats without asking first! She knew she was going to get scolded for her naughty behavior. 

Just then, her mom walked into the room. She saw the orange lollipop in Sally's hand, shook her head and told Sally to put it away. Sally was so disappointed. She was looking forward to finally tasting something this yummy, but her mom said she had to wait. 

Sally sadly dropped the lollipop on the floor and watched it slowly spin away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the store with her mommy. They wanted to buy a soft blanket for her bed. While they were walking around the store, they saw a big leopard toy. 

Lily said to her mommy, "I want to buy the leopard toy, please!" 

Her mommy said, "Okay, we can buy the leopard toy and the soft blanket for your bed." 

Lily was very happy and hugged her new leopard toy. When they got home, she put the soft blanket on her bed and cuddled with her new friend, the leopard. They both slept soundly all night long.

Molly was walking through the forest. She was so excited, because she was looking for a special treat. She had heard that there might be some delicious cheese hidden in the trees.

Molly stopped to look up into the branches of the nearest tree. Then, she spotted it - a thick wedge of cheese! She couldn't believe her luck.

She reached up and tried to grab it, but it was too high. She tried again and again, but still no luck. All of her jumping and stretching wasn't doing the trick.

Molly sighed. Just then, a kind squirrel popped out of the tree and said, "Do you need help?"

Molly smiled and nodded. The squirrel kindly reached up and handed her the cheese.

Molly thanked the squirrel and said, "I knew there would be something special in this forest!"

The squirrel smiled and said, "You're welcome!"

Molly happily skipped away, munching on her thick slice of cheese.

Once upon a time there was a gray sailboat. It sat in the water all by itself, but it wanted someone to take it for a ride. So it asked the sun to help it find a friend.

The sun smiled warmly and pointed to a little boy who was standing on the shore. The sailboat called out, "Hey! I'm over here! Do you want to come for a ride?"
The little boy couldn't believe what he was hearing. He ran to the sailboat and smiled.

Boy: What a cool sailboat! Can I ride it?

Sailboat: Sure, hop on!

The boy hopped onto the sailboat and they sailed away. The little boy felt the cool breeze on his face and laughed with joy. Soon they arrived at a magical beach.

Boy: Wow! This beach is so cool! Look at all of the shells and sand!

Sailboat: Yes, and I know something special we can do with all of this sand! 

The sailboat told the little boy about how he could mix sand and water together to make fun shapes in the sand. The boy was so excited! 

The little boy and the sailboat mixed the sand and the water together to make a castle. They played with the sand for hours until the sun went down. The little boy thanked the sailboat and said goodbye. 

The sailboat

Tom and Lily were twins. They liked to play with their toys and make things. One day, they decided to make a display of their toys for their mom and dad. They used a big box, some paper, and some glue.

They put their toys on the paper and glued them to the box. They had cars, dolls, animals, and blocks. They made a road, a house, a farm, and a tower. They were very proud of their display. They wanted to show it to their mom and dad.

They called their mom and dad to come and see their display. Mom and dad came and looked at the box. They smiled and clapped. They said, "Wow, what a wonderful display! You are very creative and clever, Tom and Lily!"

Tom and Lily were happy. They hugged their mom and dad. They said, "Thank you, mom and dad! We love you!"

Mom and dad said, "We love you too, Tom and Lily! You are our special and unusual youth. You always make us happy!"

Once upon a time there was a small gray bird. The bird lived in a very big tree. Every morning it looked out of its nest to see the world.

One day, the bird saw a scary thing. It was a big, nasty cat. It was filthy and mean. The bird was so scared! It started to chirp to tell its family about the cat. 

The family of birds was scared, too. But then, the biggest bird in the family stepped forward to protect them all. The big bird swooped around the cat and scared it away. 

The family of birds was happy and safe. And from that day on, the big bird always made sure to protect them from nasty cats!

Once upon a Tuesday there was a boy named Jack. He was very excited because today he was going to slide. He went outside and the sun was shining brightly. Jack had a big slide in his garden and he couldn't wait to have fun. 

Jack ran to the top of the slide, put his hands above his head and he started to slide. He laughed so loud. Jack slid down the slide so many times. At the end, he was so happy and smiling from ear to ear. 

He went back to the top of the slide and did it again. Jack was so excited that he wanted to slide all day. He was having so much fun! 

The day then came to an end and it was time for Jack to go inside. He was a bit sad, but he reminded himself that he would get to slide again on another Tuesday.

Ma and Pa had a puppy. It was so small and cute. All day, it would run and play with Ma and Pa. It would sometimes forget their rules. 

One day, Ma was making dinner. She was busy and forgot about the puppy. The puppy was very sad. It wanted to be able to play with Ma and Pa. 

Suddenly, it had an idea. It ran up to Ma and hugged her very tight. Ma was surprised and gave the puppy a big hug back. She wasn't mad anymore! 

The puppy was so happy. Ma and Pa played with it all evening. They would never forget this special moment.

Olly woke up one morning and wanted a cup of coffee. He asked his mom for the coffee and she said yes.

He went to the kitchen and opened the cupboard. He found the coffee but it was messy! He had to spend a few minutes picking it up so it was all neat.

Once the coffee was tidied up, Olly made the coffee himself. He put in the milk, sugar and coffee beans. Then he pressed the button and waited.

When it was ready, the coffee smelled good. Olly drank it while standing in the kitchen. He liked the taste and thanked his mom for the coffee.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old and very happy. 

One sunny day, she went for a walk in the woods. As she walked through the woods, she heard a whistle coming from somewhere in the trees. Amy followed the sound, wondering who was whistling. 

After a moment, she came across an old wise owl and he had a beautiful bracelet in his claws. The owl flew down and gave the bracelet to Amy.

Amy was very grateful and put the bracelet around her wrist. She thanked the owl, who then nodded and flew away. She watched him go, then started whistling as she walked back home, feeling very happy. 

The bracelet was now her special treasure to keep forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to take pictures with his camera. One day, Timmy went to the park to take some pictures of the flowers and the trees. 

While he was taking pictures, a little girl came up to him and asked, "What are you doing?" Timmy replied, "I'm taking pictures with my camera." 

The little girl said, "I don't understand. Why do you take pictures?" Timmy explained, "I take pictures to remember all the pretty things I see." 

The little girl smiled and said, "That's so cool! I wish I had a camera too." Timmy felt proud and happy. He wasn't ashamed to love taking pictures anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy bear named Bobo. Bobo lived in a nice, green land. The land was called the nation. All the animals in the nation were happy and played together.

One day, a big storm came to the nation. The storm broke many trees and homes. All the animals were sad. They wanted to fix their homes and make the nation nice again.

Bobo the bear had an idea. He wanted to help restore the nation. So, Bobo and all his friends worked together. They fixed the trees and the homes. Soon, the nation was nice and green again. All the animals were happy and played together once more.

Anna and Ben were very happy. They were going to the festival with their mom and dad. The festival had many fun things. There were balloons, games, music, and food. Anna and Ben wanted to see everything.

They saw a big clown with a red nose and big shoes. He made funny faces and noises. He gave Anna and Ben each a balloon animal. Anna got a pink bunny and Ben got a blue dog. They thanked the clown and ran to the next thing.

The show started with a man in a black hat and a cape. He had a wand and a box. He said he was going to make a rabbit appear from the box. He waved his wand and said some words. He opened the box and everyone gasped. There was no rabbit. There was a big sneeze.

The man looked surprised and confused. He looked inside the box again and saw a small boy with a red face and a runny nose. The boy had sneaked into the box and was hiding there. He had sneezed because of the dust. He said he was sorry and ran out of the box.

Everyone laughed except the man. He was angry and embarrassed. He said the show was over and left the tent. Anna and Ben felt sorry for the man. They thought he was not a good magician. They wondered why the boy was in the box.

They saw the boy outside the tent. He was holding a yellow cat. He said his name was Tom and he liked magic. He said he wanted to see the rabbit and he was jealous of the man. He said he did not have a ticket for the festival and he had to hide. He said he liked the cat and he had found it in the street.

Anna and Ben felt sorry for Tom. They said he could be their friend and share their balloons. They said they had tickets for the festival and they could show him around. They said they liked the cat and they asked if they could pet it. Tom smiled and said yes. He said he was sorry for ruining the show and he thanked them for being nice. They all became friends and had fun at the festival.

Ben and Lily were playing a game with their toys. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Ben was a lion and Lily was a zebra. They chased each other around the room and laughed.

"Roar!" Ben said. "I am the king of the jungle and I will catch you, zebra!"

"Neigh!" Lily said. "You can't catch me, lion! I am too fast and smart!"

They ran and ran until they were very tired. They decided to take a nap on the couch. They cuddled with their toys and closed their eyes.

But Ben was not very sleepy. He opened his eyes and saw Lily's toy zebra next to him. He had an idea. He was careless and did not think about how Lily would feel. He grabbed the toy zebra and hid it under the pillow. He thought it would be funny to see Lily's face when she woke up and could not find her toy.

He smiled and closed his eyes again. He waited for Lily to wake up.

But Lily did not wake up for a long time. She was very sleepy and had a nice dream. She dreamed that she was a real zebra and ran in the grass with her friends. She was happy and free.

When she woke up, she stretched and yawned. She looked for her toy zebra, but she could not see it. She felt sad and scared. She thought she lost her toy.

"Ben, Ben, where is my toy zebra?" she asked. "Did you see it?"

Ben opened his eyes and pretended to be surprised. He looked around and said, "No, I don't see it. Maybe it ran away."

Lily started to cry. She loved her toy zebra very much. She thought it was her best friend. She felt alone and hurt.

Ben saw Lily's tears and felt bad. He realized that he was careless and mean. He did not want to make Lily cry. He wanted to make her happy.

He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was just playing a game. I have your toy zebra. Here it is." He gave her the toy zebra from under the pillow.

Lily stopped crying and hugged her toy zebra. She was glad to have it back. She looked at Ben and said, "Thank you, Ben. But don't do that again. It was not a nice game. It was a bad game. It made me sad."

Ben nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. You are right. It was a bad game. I will not do that again. I will be nice to you and your toy zebra. Can we still be friends?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can still be friends. But you have to be careful and kind. And you have to share your toys with me."

Ben smiled and said, "OK, I will. And you have to share your toys with me too."

They hugged and said, "We are friends."

They decided to play another game with their toys. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. But this time, they were careful and kind. They shared their toys and did not hide them. They were happy.

Molly was a brave girl, and she loved to try new things. She asked her daddy, "Can I dare to do something?"

Her daddy smiled and said, "Of course! What did you want to do?"

Molly thought for a moment. She wanted to try something fun. After a few seconds, she said, "I want to fly!"

Her daddy nodded. He said, "Well, let's look outside to see what's out there. Maybe something will give you a chance to fly!"

They both went to the window and looked outside. Molly saw a tree with some branches just right for her.

Her daddy said, "I think this tree looks like a good dare for you. Are you ready?"

Molly felt a little scared, but she was also very glad. She nodded and said, "Yes, I'm ready!"

Her daddy said, "Alright, then let's do it! Just remember to be careful, okay?"

Molly nodded and reached for the tree branch. She grabbed on tight and jumped. She was flying!

Molly was so proud of herself. She had done it! Daddy clapped and said, "Well done, Molly! I knew you could do it!"

Molly smiled and she felt glad. She had dared to try something new, and it was amazing!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy bull. It was his favorite toy in the whole wide world. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his bull. He was having an incredible time running around and pretending his bull was real.

One day, they found a big engine in the garage. It was black and shiny and had many buttons and wires. Lily and Tom were curious and wanted to play with it.

"Let's see what this engine can do!" Tom said. He climbed on the engine and started to push the buttons.

"No, Tom, don't!" Lily said. She was anxious and scared. She knew the engine was not a toy and could be dangerous. "We should ask dad first!"

But Tom did not listen. He pushed more buttons and pulled some wires. The engine started to make strange sounds and smoke. Lily and Tom felt the engine shake and tremble.

"Help! Help!" they cried. They tried to get off the engine, but it was too late. The engine exploded with a loud bang. Lily and Tom were hurt by the fire and the metal. They screamed and cried.

Dad heard the noise and ran to the garage. He saw the engine in flames and his children on the ground. He was angry and sad. He called the ambulance and the firemen. He hugged Lily and Tom and said, "Why did you play with the engine? You could have died! You should have listened to Lily and asked me first!"

Lily and Tom were sorry and ashamed. They learned a hard lesson. They should never play with things they don't know. They should always be careful and obey their parents.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange box. It had a soft velvet lid on top. One day a little girl came to see the box. She was three years old and very curious. She put her hand on the lid and said, "I want to open it." But the lid wouldn't open. "Oh no, it's shut," the little girl said.

Then a magical thing happened. The box flew up into the air and the lid flew open. Inside the box was a big, soft orange velvet blanket! It was so lovely that the little girl just had to hug it. She was so happy! Now she would have something warm and comfy to snuggle up in at bedtime.

The little girl gave the box a big hug and said, "Thank you box! I love my orange velvet blanket very much." Then the lid shut and the box flew up into the sky and away.

The little girl never saw the box again, but she kept her orange velvet blanket close for many, many years. She was always very happy to snuggle up in it when it was time for bed.

Once upon a time there were two little friends, Ben and Lola. Both of them loved to take naps in the afternoon.

One day, Lola took Ben to her garden. She showed him the radishes she had grown. The radishes were big and red and round. They were very fair!

Ben said he'd like to take a nap, so Lola made a bed for him out of radish leaves. Then she tucked him in, and away he went to dreamland!

When he woke up, the sun was setting and Lola was munching on radishes. Ben ate one too, and he said it was delicious!

The two little friends spent the rest of the day playing, until the sky turned dark and it was time for them to go home. But they knew they would come back again soon to take another nap in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. Joe liked to play outside. One day, Joe's mum said to him, "Joe, it's time to go inside. Let's go."

Joe stepped inside his house, but he saw a strange thing! On the floor was an order that said "Feed the doggy!" Joe didn't know what to do. He asked his mum, "What does that mean?"

Mum said, "It means that you have to give some food to our doggy. Do you know how to do that?"

Joe nodded. He knew how to feed the doggy because his mum had taught him. He grabbed a bowl from the cupboard and then got the dog food from the shelf.

He stepped into the garden and scooped some food into the bowl. Then he placed it in front of the doggy.

The doggy loved it! He quickly ate it all up.

Mum said, "Listen to orders, Joe. They can be useful."

Joe smiled. He was glad he listened to his mum's order.

Lily and Tom were twins. They liked to play and have fun. One day, their mom and dad said they would go on vacation. Lily and Tom were happy. They wanted to see new things and have new adventures.

But mom and dad said they had to go on a cheap vacation. They did not have a lot of money. They could not go on a plane or a train. They could only go on a bus. The bus was old and slow. It had no TV or games. Lily and Tom were sad. They did not want to go on a cheap vacation.

On the bus, they met a girl named Anna. Anna was friendly and funny. She told them stories and jokes. She showed them her toys and books. She said she was going on a cheap vacation too. But she did not mind. She said she was happy to go anywhere with her mom and dad. She said they loved her and she loved them. She said that was the most important thing.

Lily and Tom listened to Anna. They thought about what she said. They looked at their mom and dad. They saw them smile and hug. They felt their love and warmth. They realized Anna was right. They did not need a fancy vacation. They had each other. They decided to be happy too.

They joined Anna in playing and laughing. They made new friends on the bus. They saw new things out the window. They had fun and learned a lot. They had a good vacation after all.

The moral of the story is: Happiness does not depend on how much money you have, but on how much love you have.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she decided to explore a room in her house that she hadn't been allowed in before. It was a big, dusty room.

Suddenly, Jane heard a loud noise in the room. It was very strange. Suddenly, she saw a big yellow bird flapping its wings. It looked helpless, like it needed help. Jane felt an urge to help the bird.

She slowly stepped closer to the bird, and said "Don't be scared. I'll help you." The bird stopped flying and stayed still. Jane carefully opened the window and the bird flew out.

Jane watched as the bird flew away into the clear blue sky. She felt proud that she had been able to help the helpless bird.

Once upon a time, there was a purple cube. It was very special. The cube was special because it could change shape. It could be a cube, a rectangle, and sometimes even a square. Every day the cube was a different shape.

One day, the cube was very excited. It was changing shape on its own. The cube was becoming bigger and bigger until it was as big as a house. It was amazing!

The purple cube was so happy, it wanted to show everyone its new shape. The cube went outside and flew around the town. Everyone was delighted to see the wonderful purple cube.

Finally, the purple cube changed back to its cube shape. It was happy it could share its shape-changing secret with the world!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brown puppy named Max. One day, Lily's mommy said, "Lily, we need to prepare for Halloween. Do you want to help me decorate the house?"

Lily replied, "Yes, mommy! I love Halloween. What should we do first?"

"We need to make some spirit ghosts to hang up outside. Can you help me make them?" asked her mommy.

Lily said, "Yes, mommy! I can help you make the spirit ghosts. How do we make them brown?"

"We can't make them brown, silly. Ghosts are usually white. But we can use brown paper bags to make them. That will make them look different," said her mommy.

Lily and her mommy worked together to make the spirit ghosts. They cut out eyes and mouths and hung them up outside. Max the puppy barked happily as they finished decorating. Lily was so proud of their decorations and couldn't wait for Halloween night.

Once upon a time, in a deep, deep forest, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to play with her toy iron. One day, she took her toy iron and went to the forest to play.

As she played, she heard a loud scream. Lucy was scared, but she wanted to help. She picked up her toy iron and followed the sound of the scream.

She found a small bird stuck in a hole. The bird was very scared and screamed again. Lucy used her toy iron to help the bird get out of the hole. The bird was so happy and flew away. Lucy felt good for helping the bird and went back home with her toy iron.

Once upon a time there were two special people. One was named Tom, and one was named Jane. Tom and Jane liked each other very much and wanted to be together forever. So they got married and were very happy.

At the wedding, Tom gave Jane a special gem. It was very sparkly and pretty. He told her it was very important. Jane was so happy and thanked him for it.

The special gem was so pretty that it shone in all different colors. Everyone at the wedding was amazed by it. Jane was so proud that she wore it every day.

Tom and Jane were so happy that they married. The gem was important because it made them remember how much they love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike, but he never wore his helmet. His mom always told him to wear it, but he thought it was too tough to wear.

One day, Timmy decided to go for a ride without his helmet. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice a big rock in his path. He hit the rock and fell off his bike. He hurt his head really badly and had to go to the hospital.

After that, Timmy always wore his helmet when he rode his bike. He learned that it's important to follow safety rules, even if they seem tough. The moral of the story is that safety should always come first, even if it's not fun or easy.

Zoe likes to count. She can count to ten with her fingers. She knows zero is when you have no fingers up. She likes to hold zero in her hand and pretend it is a ball.

One day, Zoe goes to the park with her mom. She sees a big slide. She wants to go on it. She holds zero in her hand and runs to the slide. She climbs up the steps and sits on the top.

But then she feels scared. The slide is too high and too fast. She wants to go back down. She cries and calls for her mom. She squeezes zero in her hand.

Her mom hears her and comes to the slide. She tells Zoe to be calm and brave. She says she will catch her at the bottom. She says zero will help her too.

Zoe listens to her mom. She takes a deep breath and lets go of the slide. She slides down and feels the wind in her hair. She smiles and laughs. She lands in her mom's arms. She hugs her mom and shows her zero. She says zero is her friend. Her mom says she is proud of her. They go to play some more.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his rug, it was soft and blue. One day, Timmy's mom came into his room and asked him to clean up his toys. Timmy didn't want to, so he shrugged his shoulders and said "no". His mom got upset and told him to clean up or he wouldn't be able to play with his toys later. Timmy didn't like this, so he tried to pull his rug tight over his toys so his mom couldn't see them. But his mom saw what he was doing and told him to clean up properly. Timmy finally listened and put his toys away.

Once there was a hippo who was very tired. He wanted to go to sleep, but he had a hurt foot. He looked around for a soft place, and he spotted a big comfy bed. He hopped on, and quickly snuggled in.

He let out a big yawn and closed his little eyes. Then, ever so slowly, he began to drift off to sleep. As he dozed off he had dreams about running and eating and playing. 

But then, just as he was about to drift off completely, he heard a noise! He quickly opened his eyes and saw a big fat mouse nibbling on his bed. He was so startled he jumped up and the mouse scurried away.

But then he remembered how tired he was and decided the mouse could keep the bed. He hopped off and found a grassy spot under a shady tree. He snuggled in and finally fell fast asleep. 

The hippo slept soundly all through the night until the morning sun woke him up. He felt much better after his long nap and he knew that he would be able to play and explore all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a deer named Bambi. Bambi wanted to play with his friends in the forest, but he couldn't find any comfortable clothes to wear. He tried on many clothes, but none of them fit him well. 

Bambi felt sad and worried that he wouldn't be able to play with his friends. Suddenly, he saw a rabbit hopping towards him. The rabbit asked Bambi what was wrong, and Bambi told him about his problem. 

The rabbit had an idea and took Bambi to a nearby store. There, they found a perfect outfit for Bambi that fit him just right. Bambi was so happy and grateful to the rabbit. He put on his new clothes and ran to play with his friends. 

From that day on, Bambi learned that it's important to ask for help when you have a problem and that there's always a solution to every problem.

Once there was a bald man who liked to paint roads. Every day he would get up early and find a road to paint. He would start at one end and make sure to paint everything completely. He'd even paint the curbs and poles. 

The bald man enjoyed his work. He liked the smell of the paint and seeing the roads in bright colors. One day, he was painting a road when a little girl on her tricycle stopped to watch. She was fascinated by the bald manâ€™s hard work.

After he was done, the little girl asked if she could help paint the road. The bald man said yes and handed her a brush. She was so excited as she painted the road with him. It was a beautiful sight to see bright colors on an otherwise gray road. 

When they were done, the little girl thanked the bald man and went on her way. He was so happy that he had shared this special moment with her. Now, the bald man and the little girl will always remember the day that they painted the road together.

Once there was a little girl. She was 3 years old and very brave. One day she got lost in the big park. She looked around but couldn't find her way home! She started to worry.

Suddenly, she saw a leaf floating by. It was a special leaf with different colors and shapes. She was about to reach for it, but then the leaf flew away.

The little girl started to follow the leaf. She walked and walked until the leaf stopped near a big tree. There, she saw a kind old lady.

The little girl asked the lady if she could help her find her home. The lady smiled and said: "Don't worry, I will show you the way". She pointed at the big tree and said "See that tree? Just walk in that direction and you should find home".

The little girl thanked her and followed the lady's instructions. Soon enough, she arrived home. She was happy, but also a bit hot from the walk!

Every Saturday, Henry would take his mule to the market to supply things to the people. Henry was a serious worker, always doing his best to make sure his customers got what they wanted.

One sunny Saturday, Henry stopped by Mrs. Tom's stand. She had been a regular customer of Henry's for many years.

Mrs. Tom smiled at him. She said, "Henry, I need some apples for my son. Can you supply me with some?"

Henry patted his mule's head. "Of course I can, Mrs. Tom," he said. He lifted a basket full of red apples off of the mule and handed it to Mrs. Tom.

She thanked him and handed him some coins. "You run a serious business, Henry," she said.

Henry nodded, tipping his hat. "Yes, I take this job very serious," he said. He thanked Mrs. Tom and continued on his way.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went for a walk in the park with her mom. They saw a beautiful landscape with trees, flowers, and a river. Lily loved it so much that she wanted to touch the water. But as she got closer, she slipped and fell into the river!

Lily's mom quickly pulled her out and hugged her tightly. They went back home, and Lily felt sad because her clothes were wet and dirty. Her mom tried to cheer her up by showing her a fake flower she had bought at the store. Lily smiled and hugged her mom, feeling happy again.

Later that day, Lily's mom took her to the store to buy new clothes. They also bought some fake flowers to decorate their house. Lily loved the new clothes and the flowers, but she never forgot about the beautiful landscape in the park. She promised herself that she would be more careful next time she went there.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Jane. She was always full of joy and could never sit still. She was always singing and dancing, no matter what.

One day, Jane's mum gave her a special gift. It was a tiny magnet that glittered when the sun shone on it. Jane was so happy with her present and thanked her mum for it.

The next day, Jane took her magnet out to the garden, singing and dancing as she went. But when she got there, she noticed that the ground was really dirty. She was about to try and clean up the mess, when her mum stopped her. She said, "Jane, I know you want to help, but sometimes it is better to leave thing as they are. It's ok to just go outside and enjoy the sunshine."

Jane listened to her mum and said, "Ok, I will". And so she just sang and danced, with her little magnet glittering in the sunshine. She was filled with such joy and happiness, and she knew deep in her heart that what her mother said was right.

The moral of this story is that helping is important, but sometimes it is better to just enjoy life, no matter what. We must take time to appreciate the beauty around us and be thankful for it.

Jim was a smart boy. He was always curious and loved to learn new things. One day, his mom gave him a special toy. It was a soft yellow bear with a big smile. Jim loved it.

He hugged it tight and said, "Thanks, Mom!"

Jim squeezed the toy. He wanted to know what was inside of it. He squeezed and shook it but nothing came out. Then he heard something rattling inside. He smiled, excited to see what it was.

Jim looked up at his mom and said in a loud voice, "Mom, what's inside?"

His mom patted him on the head and said, "Go ahead and squeeze it, Jim. You'll find out!"

Jim smiled and squeezed it hard. Suddenly, it popped open! Inside were small chips and colorful buttons. Jim was so surprised. He had found a surprise inside!

He quickly put the pieces back and hugged the toy tight. He knew he was smart for finding it!

Once upon a time, there lived two friends: Ben and Sam. They loved playing together and having lots of fun. One day, Ben found an incredible diamond in the park and was very excited! He wanted to share it with Sam, so he ran back to show him.

When Ben found Sam, he said, "Look! I found a diamond!" But when Sam saw the diamond, he said, "It's broken. It's no good." Ben didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, Ben had an idea! He said, "Let's try to repair it. We'll make it as good as new!" Sam was excited.

They spent the afternoon trying to repair the diamond, and after a lot of hard work, they succeeded! The diamond was as good as new.

Ben and Sam were so proud of their work. They smiled and hugged each other, happy that their incredible diamond was back and ready for them to share.

Tom and Lily are going on a big trip with Mom and Dad. They are very happy and excited. They pack their bags and toys and get in the car. Mom and Dad drive to the airport.

At the airport, they see many people and planes. They have to wait in a long line. Then they have to show their passports to a man. A passport is a small book with your name and picture. It tells where you are from and where you can go.

"Can I see your passport, please?" the man asks Tom.

"Here you go," Tom says. He opens his passport and gives it to the man. The man looks at it and smiles.

"Very good, Tom. You have a reliable passport. It is not old or broken. It is valid and safe. You can go on the plane," the man says.

"Thank you," Tom says. He takes his passport back and puts it in his pocket.

"Can I see your passport, please?" the man asks Lily.

"Here you go," Lily says. She opens her passport and gives it to the man. The man looks at it and frowns.

"Oh no, Lily. You have a problem. Your passport is not reliable. It is old and torn. It is not valid and safe. You cannot go on the plane," the man says.

"What? No!" Lily says. She starts to cry. She does not want to stay at the airport. She wants to go on the big trip with Tom and Mom and Dad.

"Don't worry, Lily. We will fix this. We will get you a new passport. It will be fast and easy. Then you can go on the plane," Mom says. She hugs Lily and wipes her tears.

"Really?" Lily says.

"Really," Mom says.

They go to another place where they can get a new passport. They take a picture of Lily and fill out a form. They pay some money and wait for a little while. Then they get a new passport for Lily. It is shiny and new. It has her name and picture. It is reliable.

"Here you go, Lily. You have a new passport. It is reliable. It is valid and safe. You can go on the plane," the lady says.

"Thank you," Lily says. She opens her new passport and smiles. She is happy and excited again.

They go back to the line and show their passports to the man. The man nods and lets them go. They walk to the gate and board the plane. They find their seats and buckle their belts. They are ready for the big trip.

"Are you happy, Lily?" Tom asks.

"Yes, I am happy, Tom. I have a reliable passport. I can go on the big trip with you and Mom and Dad," Lily says.

"Me too, Lily. Me too," Tom says.

They hold hands and look out the window. They see the plane take off and fly in the sky. They are going on a big trip. They are very happy and excited.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy who loved to bathe in the big blue ocean. She liked to feel the warm water against her skin and the sunlight on her face. 

Whenever she went to the beach, Lucy always noticed the beautiful landscape. The scenery was filled with sand and sea, as far as the eye could see. She admired the rolling waves, the big rocks against the shore and the seagulls flying in the sky. 

Often, Lucy's parents took her to a cheap hotel near the beach. They would put her in a big tub and fill it with warm water. Then, the little girl would splash with glee as she bathed. She would splash and giggle until it was time to get out. 

Afterwards, Lucy felt all refreshed and clean. She loved being able to bathe in the ocean with her family. Every time she was done, she thanked her parents for allowing her to enjoy the beautiful landscape by the beach.

John and Jack were best friends. One day they were playing at Jack's house. John saw a tray of snacks on the table, yummy cookies and colourful pieces of fruit.

John said "Can I have some?" but then Jack started to tease him. He said "No, you can't have any. It's all mine!"

John felt sad but then he saw some disgusting food on the tray. There was a slimy green potato and a smelly fish. John made a face and said "Ew, that's disgusting!"

Jack laughed and said "Okay, you can try the disgusting food - but only if you dare!" John was brave and he decided to take the tray and try the food. He thought it was really yucky but he was really proud that he didn't let Jack tease him. They both had a good laugh.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Tilly and Jack. They were both very restless and loved to play together in the fields.

One day, Tilly had an idea. She wanted to find a great truth. But how could they do that? Then Jack had an idea. He said, "Let's go on an adventure and explore the world for the great truth!" Tilly was so excited about this that she jumped up and down.

So they set out on their adventure. They visited every corner of the world together and asked many people, but no one could give them the great truth. But they kept searching and searching.

Finally they reached the top of a tall mountain. There, they asked a wise old man. He said, "The truth can only be found when you search inside your heart."

So Tilly and Jack sat still and quiet, and searched inside their hearts until they found the great truth they had been looking for. Then they smiled and hugged each other, happy that they had found the truth.

One day, a little girl was feeling sad. Her aunt saw this and wanted to help her. She scooped her up into her arms and gave her a big hug. It felt warm and comforting. 

The aunt said kind words and explained to the little girl that bad things can happen but it's ok to feel sad. But she also said that she was there to help her through it. 

The little girl felt a lot better after that. Her aunt was so caring and understanding. Even though she had been feeling sad, she was now smiling. 

The aunt had been so patient and kind, even though her little niece had been acting rude. She had been acting out and throwing a tantrum, but the aunt had stayed calm and comforted her. 

The little girl was glad that she had someone like her aunt to help her when she was feeling sad. She was very thankful for her loving and kind aunt.

Once there was a mother. She had a blue box that she wanted to organize. Every day she thought to herself, "I should organize the box." But there were so many things in it that she couldn't decide what to do.

One day she decided to ask her 3 year old child for help! She asked, "Will you please help me organize my blue box?" The child was excited and said yes.

Together, the mother and the child sorted through the blue box and began organizing it. They put things in piles and sorted them by type. When they finished, the box looked neat and tidy. 

The mother was very happy with the work her child had done. She thanked him for his help and gave him a big hug. From then on, the mother was always sure to ask her 3 year old child to help her organize things!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the rain. The rain made her hair and clothes wet. She ran around and splashed in the puddles.

Suddenly, she saw a big chamber in the garden. She went inside and saw many things she had never seen before. She started to question what they were and how they worked. She was very curious and wanted to learn more.

After exploring the chamber, Lily went back home. She told her mommy and daddy all about her adventure in the wet garden and the mysterious chamber. They were proud of her for being so brave and inquisitive.

Bob was so excited, he just got a new wallet! His mum said he could keep it, if he helped build something. He said yes with a smile.

His mum gave him some big wooden blocks. She said, "let's build a tower Bob". Bob took some of the blocks, stacked them up one by one and soon the tower was so tall it reached the top of the room.

His mum said "good job Bob, now let's make something tasty to eat". Bob suggested they make some pancakes. His mum said sure and they started gathering all the ingredients.
Bob stirred the bowl of pancake batter and watched as his mum fried up the pancakes on the stove.

When they were done, Bob carefully placed them on plates and added some yummy strawberries and bananas. He took a bite and said "these pancakes are so tasty!"

His mum said, "you did a great job helping me build and cook. Your new wallet will be filled with tasty treats for your hard work. Now how about one more pancake?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress and loved to play outside. One day, Lily's mom asked her to go to the store to buy some sugar.

Lily was excited to go to the store, but when she got there, she saw a big line. The line was very long, and it made her feel sad because it would delay her from getting home to play.

She waited patiently in line and finally got the sugar. On her way back home, she met her friend, Timmy. Timmy said, "Wow, Lily, your dress is so pretty!" Lily smiled and replied, "Thanks, I went to the store to get some sugar, but the line was so long that it delayed me." Timmy said, "That's okay, let's go play!" And they ran off to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety lived in a tree with his family. One day, Tweety saw a big bird flying high in the sky. He said to his mom, "I want to become a big bird too!" 

His mom said, "Tweety, you are perfect just the way you are. You don't need to become anything else." 

But Tweety didn't listen. He tried to fly higher and higher every day to become a big bird. One day, he flew too high and got trapped in a cage. He was very grumpy and sad. 

A little girl saw Tweety in the cage and felt sorry for him. She opened the cage and let Tweety fly away. Tweety learned that it's better to be happy with who you are than to try to become someone else.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jenny who loved spending time outside. One day Jenny found a boat by the river and couldn't wait to explore. She said excitedly "I'm going in the boat."

As she jumped inside and grabbed the oars, her dad said, "Be careful Jenny, and enjoy your journey!" 

Jenny began to row and soon the river started to move with her. She felt the breeze on her face and the sun on her skin. She was so excited that she rowed until the river seemed to be standing still.

Suddenly Jenny heard an owl call out. It was so lazy and relaxing, just like the boat, that Jenny stopped rowing and lay down in the boat. The river moved slowly and Jenny watched the clouds and the birds flying above. She felt so happy and content. As she lay there, she enjoyed the calmness, like she was in a dream.

At sunset, Jenny's dad found her still lying in the boat, smiling away. He said, "Have you enjoyed your journey? Come on, little one, let's go home now." 

Jenny nodded, feeling tired but happy. She smiled as the boat slowly moved back towards the shore.

Once there was a little boy named Tim. He was only three years old and loved exploring his garden. One day, he thought it would be fun to fish in the pond.

He got out his net and went to the pond. He looked around and spotted a big, hairy fish!

Tim said to the fish, 'Hi there! What's your name?'

The fish replied, 'I guess my name is Fred.'

Tim was so excited, he started to jump up and down. He used his net to scoop up the fish. 'Come and live with me!' He exclaimed.

Fred the fish wasn't so sure, but he decided he should go along. From that day forward, they became the best of friends. They played together in the pond and even went for walks in the garden.

Tim and Fred loved each other very much and they lived happily ever after.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, they find a big red can in the garage. It has a picture of a car on it.

"Look, this is gas for cars!" Tom says. "Let's put some in our trucks and make them go faster!"

Sam is not sure. He sees a word on the can that he does not know. It says "danger".

"Tom, I don't think this is a good idea," Sam says. "This gas might be bad for us. It says danger."

Tom does not listen. He thinks Sam is scared. He opens the can and smells the gas. It makes him cough.

"It's fine, Sam. Don't be a baby," Tom says. He pours some gas in his truck and puts it on the floor. He pushes it and it zooms away.

"Wow, that's cool!" Tom says. He pours more gas in his truck and in Sam's truck. He gives Sam his truck and says, "Come on, let's race!"

Sam does not want to race. He feels sick from the gas. He wants to go home.

"Tom, I don't want to play with this gas. It makes me feel bad. Let's go outside and play with something else," Sam says.

Tom does not reply. He is too busy racing his truck. He does not see the gas spill on the floor. He does not see the spark from his truck. He does not see the fire.

Sam sees the fire. He screams and runs away. He calls for help. He hopes Tom is okay.

But Tom is not okay. The fire burns him and his truck. He cries and cries. He wishes he listened to Sam. He wishes he played with something healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in the forest. The bear was very fierce and had a loud roar. One day, it started to rain and the bear needed a shelter to stay dry. It looked around and found a cave where it could hide. 

As the bear was sitting in the cave, it saw a little bird flying by. The bear wanted to play a joke on the bird, so it pretended to be asleep. The bird saw the bear and thought it was really sleeping. The bird then flew into the cave and started singing loudly. The bear suddenly jumped up and scared the bird. 

The bird flew away quickly and the bear laughed at the joke it played. It was happy to have a shelter from the rain and a fun time playing jokes. The end.

Ben and Lily are playing with their toy cars in the garden. They make them zoom on the grass and the dirt. They pretend they are racing drivers and make loud noises.

"Vroom, vroom, I'm the fastest!" Ben says.

"No, I'm the fastest!" Lily says.

They zoom their cars towards each other and crash them. They laugh and pick them up.

"Look, there's a note on your car!" Lily says. She sees a piece of paper stuck on Ben's car.

"What does it say?" Ben asks. He can't read yet.

Lily can read a little bit. She looks at the note and says, "It says, 'This car is very important. It belongs to Daddy. Please be careful with it.'"

Ben gasps. He didn't know the car was Daddy's. He thought it was his.

"Uh-oh, we broke Daddy's car!" Ben says. He feels sad and scared.

"Don't worry, Ben. We can fix it." Lily says. She is a good sister. She helps Ben find some tape and glue. They stick the car back together. It looks a bit funny, but it still zooms.

They write a new note and put it on the car. It says, "Sorry, Daddy. We love you."

They hope Daddy will not be mad. They hug each other and wait for him to come home.

There was a furry animal who was walking through the woods. He had a big appetite, and he was looking for something to eat. Suddenly, he came across a big cherry tree. The animal was so excited that he began to chew on one of the cherries.

Then a voice said, "Be careful! Some of those cherries are sour!"

The animal looked up and saw an owl perched on a branch. "You shouldn't just eat all of these cherries without tasting them first because some of them are sour," the owl said.

The animal thanked the owl and began to taste each cherry before he chewed it. Sure enough, the owl was right. Some of the cherries were really sour! Luckily, he found lots of sweet cherries too and he was able to fill up his hungry stomach.

The animal looked up to the sky and thanked the wise owl. He was so happy that he had listened to the owl's advice. He wouldn't have been able to eat all of those cherries if he hadn't tasted them first. The furry animal had found a feast of sweet cherries in the woods, thanks to the owl!

Once there was a dark lizard who liked to sit. He was a friendly lizard and he liked to sit on the rocks in the sunshine. He liked the sun so much, he would stay and sit forever!

One day, the lizard saw something that looked yummy. He thought it might be a treat, so he scuttled over to check it out. When he got there, he saw it was a big bug. The bug was dark and the lizard was very excited. He liked to eat bugs!

He sat down and started to eat, but something strange happened. As soon as he took a bite, he started to run away! He was scared and he didn't know why. He ran and ran until he jumped onto a rock and he sat there, trying to figure things out.

Suddenly, the dark bug moved! The lizard was so surprised he almost fell off the rock. He quickly realized that the bug was alive - it was a dark lizard, just like him!

The two lizards just sat there for a moment, looking at each other. Then suddenly, the dark lizard started to run away again. The other lizard was too scared and confused to follow, so he just sat and watched his friend go.

Tom and Lily are hungry. They want to eat some food. But their mom is not at home. She went to the shop. She told them to be obedient and wait for her.

Tom and Lily look in the kitchen. They see a big jar of cookies. They love cookies. They want to eat them. But the jar is on a high shelf. They cannot reach it.

Tom has an idea. He says to Lily, "Let's solve this problem. We can use a chair and a stick. I will stand on the chair and poke the jar with the stick. Then it will fall down and we can eat the cookies."

Lily thinks this is a good idea. She says, "OK, let's do it. But we have to be quick. Mom will be back soon."

Tom and Lily find a chair and a stick. They move the chair to the shelf. Tom climbs on the chair. He holds the stick. He tries to poke the jar. But the stick is too short. He cannot reach the jar.

Tom says, "Oh no, this is not working. We need a longer stick."

Lily says, "Wait, I have an idea. I will go and get the broom. It has a long handle. It will work."

Lily runs to the closet and gets the broom. She brings it to Tom. Tom takes the broom. He pokes the jar with the broom. The jar wobbles. It falls down. It breaks on the floor. Cookies spill everywhere.

Tom and Lily cheer. They say, "Yay, we solved the problem. We can eat the cookies."

They jump off the chair. They run to the cookies. They pick them up. They eat them. They are happy.

But then they hear the door. Mom is back. She sees the mess. She sees the broken jar. She sees the cookies. She is angry.

She says, "Tom and Lily, what have you done? You were not obedient. You made a big mess. You ate all the cookies. You are in trouble."

Tom and Lily are scared. They say, "Sorry, mom. We were hungry. We wanted to eat some food. We tried to solve the problem. But we made a mistake."

Mom says, "You should have waited for me. I bought some food for you. I bought some fruit and some milk. They are healthy and yummy. You should eat them instead of cookies. Cookies are not good for you. They will make you sick."

Tom and Lily feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We will not do it again. We will eat the fruit and the milk. We will be obedient."

Mom says, "I hope you learned your lesson. Now, help me clean up this mess. Then we can have some fruit and some milk. And maybe one cookie each. But only one."

Tom and Lily say, "OK, mom. We will help you. We love you."

Mom says, "I love you too. But next time, listen to me. And do not try to solve problems by yourself. Ask me for help. I will always help you."

One day, Mommy and Baby went to the park. Baby saw a fly zooming around and became very excited. Baby shouted, "Mommy look! A fly!" Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Baby, that's a cute fly." Baby watched the fly buzzing around the park. Baby came up with a plan and shouted, "Mommy, let's park the fly in our home!" Mommy chuckled and said, "No, Baby, we can't park the fly in our home, but it sure is a cute fly!" Baby then enjoyed the rest of the day playing in the park.

One day, a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue went to play in the park. They liked to run and laugh. They were very happy. Tim liked to tell jokes to make Sue laugh. 

But there was a big boy in the park too. His name was Max. Max was ignorant and did not like jokes. He saw Tim and Sue running and laughing. Max did not like that. He wanted them to stop. So Max went to Tim and Sue and told them to stop laughing and running.

Tim and Sue did not want to stop. They just wanted to have fun. So Tim told Max a joke to make him laugh. Max did not laugh at first, but then he started to smile. Max learned to like jokes and running too. Now, Tim, Sue, and Max all played together in the park, running and laughing. They were all happy friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big zoo in the town. Everyone in the town was worried because lots of animals had gone missing.

The people decided to work together to find the noisy animals. They searched everywhere, but the animals were no where to be found.

Soon, the people heard a noise. They followed the loud sound and they saw a group of lost animals in a meadow. They were tired and sleepy, so they could not move anymore.

The people were very glad that they had found the animals and they put them in the zoo. The animals had a nice place to rest.

The animals were happy to be back in the zoo, and the people were not worried any more. Everyone was happy, and had a good rest. The End!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Bob and he was three years old. One day, Bob wanted to build a tower. So he asked his mom to bring him some bricks. But his mom only had one brick, and it was different than the kind of brick Bob wanted.

"No, Mom, I need a different kind of brick!" shouted Bob.

His mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, Bob. I will find a different brick for you!"

So his mom searched all around her house for a different brick. Finally, she found it and brought it back to Bob. When he saw it, Bob was so happy. He immediately began to build his tower. When he was done, it was the tallest tower in the world!

From then on, Bob would always remember his mom and the special brick she had brought him.

Once upon a time, there was a mild infant playing near a big door. She was delighted to be able to explore the world. She asked her mom, "What's behind this door?" Her mom smiled and said, "It's a secret until you can unlock it." The infant looked around and tried to find something to open the door, but she wasn't able to.

The infant's mom could see the disappointment on her daughter's face and said with a gentle hug, "Don't worry, I know how to unlock this door!" She grabbed a big key, and with a big smile said, "Letting you use my big key to unlock it would be the best way to let you learn something new!"

The infant was elated and exclaimed, "Yes! Let me try it!" She cheerfully grabbed the key and tried to find the right hole, but it was difficult. After several attempts, she finally managed to unlock the big door.

The infant ran inside and discovered a mysterious new world. She was so excited that she had been able to unlock the door. She will never forget the feeling of accomplishment she felt.

John looked up at the tall tree. He leaned his head back and saw the stars in the night sky. He smiled and clapped his hands together. He wanted to reach the stars and touch them!

John turned around and saw his candle on the table. He had left it open. He picked it up and gave it a big hug. He liked the way the candle glowed in the dark.

John looked back up at the tree. He leaned the candle up against the trunk and it stayed there. The candle lit up John and the tree. The stars looked like they were twinkling down at John and the open candle.

John smiled and said good night to the stars! Then he walked slowly back to his house, feeling warm and happy. The candle shone in the night and watched him go.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big bear. He lived in a forest with lots of trees. One day, the bear was walking around when he saw a big, big rock. The rock was so large that the bear could not move it. 

The bear wanted to play with the rock, but he couldn't. So, he thought of an idea. He went to his home and got a small rock. He put the small rock where the big rock was and took the big rock to his home. 

The bear was happy because he could play with the big rock now. He played with it every day for one week. But, at the end of the week, the bear was tired of playing with the big rock. So, he went back to the forest and replaced the big rock with the small one. The bear was happy again and played with the small rock.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She wore her favorite shirt with a big, happy sun on it. Lucy loved to play with her friends and show them her shirt. She was always polite and kind when she played.

At the park, Lucy saw a boy named Tim. Tim was sad because his shirt was dirty. He had fallen in the mud and now his shirt was all brown. Lucy wanted to help Tim, so she thought of a plan.

Lucy took Tim to her house and showed him her special box of shirts. She let him pick a shirt to wear. Tim picked a shirt with a big, happy sun just like Lucy's. They both wore the same shirt and went back to the park. Tim was very happy and said "thank you" to Lucy. They played together and had lots of fun.

The other kids at the park saw Lucy and Tim being polite and sharing. They all wanted to be kind and share too. Soon, everyone was playing nicely and sharing their toys.

The moral of the story is to always be polite and share with others. When you are kind, it makes everyone happy and helps make new friends.

Tom and Lily liked to play with blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. They could create anything they wanted with their blocks. One day, they decided to create a nation with their blocks.

They used purple blocks to make a big castle. The castle was the home of the king and the queen of their nation. They used yellow blocks to make a wall around the castle. The wall was to keep the nation safe from bad people. They used green blocks to make fields and trees. The fields and trees were for the animals and the food of their nation. They used blue blocks to make a river and a lake. The river and the lake were for the water and the fish of their nation.

Tom and Lily were very proud of their nation. They gave their nation a name. They called it Purple Land. They made a flag with a purple star on it. They put the flag on top of the castle. They pretended to be the king and the queen of Purple Land. They made rules and laws for their nation. They had fun and played with their blocks. They loved their nation. They loved Purple Land.

Once upon a time, there was a small Black bird. All day long it flew around, searching for food and making friends. But one special day, the bird noticed something very special in the air. It was a wonderful smell of Poppy.

The bird knew that these Poppy flowers only grew once a year and so it quickly gathered them up. Gathering up all of the Poppies, it filled its beak with as many as it could. When it was finished, it flew away back to its nest.

The small bird gave all of the Poppy flowers to its family and friends. They were all very happy to see the Black Poppies, and thanked the small bird for its kindness. Everyone was filled with joy and celebrated the special Poppy flowers all day long.

The bird was glad it had gathered all of the Poppies for its family, and it flew up into the sky and danced in the air. Everyone lived happily ever after.

Lily and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy.

"Let's go inside now," said Lily. "It is cold and Mommy made hot cocoa for us."

"No, I want to play more," said Ben. He was stubborn. He did not want to stop.

"But you are wet and shivering," said Lily. "You need to wear a coat. Mommy will be angry if you get sick."

"I don't care," said Ben. He threw a snowball at Lily. It hit her in the face. She cried.

"Ben, that is not nice!" said Lily. She ran to the house. She opened the door and entered. She took off her wet gloves and boots. She saw Mommy in the kitchen.

"Mommy, Ben is mean!" she said. "He threw a snowball at me and he does not want to come inside."

Mommy hugged Lily and wiped her tears. She gave her a cup of hot cocoa. She looked out the window and saw Ben still playing in the snow.

"Ben, come inside now!" she shouted. "You will catch a cold. Put on your coat and come here."

Ben heard Mommy. He did not listen. He was stubborn. He made another snowball and threw it at the snowman. He missed. He slipped and fell. He hurt his knee. He cried.

"Mommy, help!" he said. He wanted Mommy to come and hug him. He was sorry.

Mommy heard Ben. She put down her cup and ran to the door. She opened it and entered the snow. She picked up Ben and carried him inside. She took off his wet clothes and put on his coat. She kissed his knee and gave him a band-aid. She gave him a cup of hot cocoa.
