The skeleton apologized with a sweet smile. He promised he would never do it again, and he wished that everyone would give him another chance.

At first everyone was scared and didn't know what to do. But then one little boy said that he would forgive the skeleton. That made the skeleton so happy, and soon all the other children followed. 

The skeleton was thrilled and everyone was friends again. They all laughed, danced and had a wonderful time together. 

The skeleton was so thankful for the little boy's kindness and generosity. He realized that forgiveness can be sweet, just like honey!

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes, but they always wanted more. One day, their mom took them to the toy store and said they could each choose one car to buy.

Tim ran to the shelf and picked a big red car that had shiny leather seats and a loud horn. He was very happy with his choice and showed it to his mom. Sam looked at the shelf and saw a small blue car that had soft leather seats and a quiet horn. He liked the blue car, but he was jealous of Tim's red car. He wanted to have the biggest and loudest car too.

He said to Tim, "Your car is not good. It is too big and too noisy. My car is better. It is small and quiet. Let me have your car and you can have mine."

Tim said, "No, I like my car. I chose it first. You can have your own car. Stop being jealous."

Sam was angry and did not listen. He grabbed Tim's car and tried to take it away from him. Tim held on to his car and did not let go. They both pulled and pushed and shouted. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong.

She saw them fighting over the red car and was very upset. She said, "You are both being very naughty. You should not fight over toys. You should be happy with what you have and share with each other. Because you did not behave, you will not get any car today. I will take them back to the store and you will go home with nothing."

She took the cars from their hands and put them back on the shelf. Tim and Sam cried and begged, but their mom did not change her mind. She took them by the hand and left the toy store. They went home with nothing and learned a hard lesson.

One day, a girl named Lily was playing in the park. She saw a big red car with a loud noise. Lily did not know what it was. She asked her mom, "What is that big red car?" Her mom said, "That is an ambulance. It helps people who are hurt."

Lily watched the ambulance drive very fast. It was big, but it moved like a graceful bird. She liked how it looked and wanted to know more. She asked her mom, "Can I help people like the ambulance does?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can be a helper when you grow up."

Lily was happy to know that she could help people too. She played in the park and pretended to be an ambulance. She made the loud noise and moved like a graceful bird. Lily knew that one day, she would be a great helper just like the ambulance.

Once upon a time, there was a big TV in a house. The TV was very large and it had many colors. One day, a boy was playing with a toy and he accidentally hit the TV. The TV fell down and broke. The boy was very sad because he loved watching cartoons on the TV. His mom told him not to worry and that they would get a new TV. The new TV was even bigger and sharper than the old one. The boy was very happy and he watched his favorite cartoons on the new TV every day.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl called Lucy. Every day Lucy would look out of her window, at the landscape outside. One day when she was looking out, she saw something funny. The sky was covered in a blanket of white!

"Mummy, what is it?" Lucy asked.

"It's snow, sweetheart,â€ Mummy said. â€œIt's very pretty, isn't it?â€

"Yes, it is pretty," Lucy said. She bravely decided to go outside and play in the snow. She pulled on her warm coat and covered her head and hands with a scarf and gloves.

Once Lucy stepped into the winter wonderland, she was filled with joy. She scooped up big handfuls of snow and tossed them in the air. She made a snowman and danced around it as if it were alive. Lucy was filled with courage as she enjoyed the beautiful winter landscape. 

The sun set and before long it was time to go back inside. Lucy's mama tucked her snugly in bed, looking out the window at the star filled sky she saw that night. In the morning, when Lucy opened her eyes the snow had covered the landscape again, and she realized it had been a magical night.

Tim and Sue are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bag on a bench. They are curious. They want to see what is in the bag.

They walk to the bench. They open the bag. They see a lot of balloons. They are happy. They like balloons. They take some balloons out of the bag.

Suddenly, they hear a loud voice. It is a man. He is angry. He says, "Hey, those are my balloons! Give them back!"

Tim and Sue are scared. They drop the balloons. They run away. The balloons rise in the air. They fly away.

The man is sad. He says, "Oh no, my balloons! Come back!"

Tim and Sue are sorry. They did not know the balloons were his. They hide behind a tree. They watch the balloons go up and up. They hope the man will find his balloons. They say, "Sorry, mister. We did not mean to take your balloons."

Mia was at the beach with her mom. She was so excited! She looked around and saw a dolphin swimming in the water. She asked her mom if she could catch it. Her mom said it might be too hard for little Mia, but if she was patient, she could try. 

Mia was determined to catch the dolphin. She waited and watched the dolphins for a long time. Finally one of the dolphins swam close to the shore. Mia ran in the water and tried to grab the dolphin. She was getting closer and closer and then, finally, she caught it! Mia was so excited she could hardly believe it. 

Mia held on to the dolphin tight and it jumped and splashed around in the water. Mia was so proud of herself. She had been patient and it paid off. Mia and her dolphin played together until sunset and then the dolphin swam away. Mia had a great day with her new friend and would never forget it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and make funny sounds. One day, Timmy took his favorite toy car and accidentally broke it. He felt bad and wanted to fix it, but he didn't know how. 

Timmy's friend, Bobby, came over to play and saw the broken toy car. Bobby was angry and yelled at Timmy. Timmy felt sad and cried. But then, Bobby forgave Timmy and they played together again. 

Later that day, Timmy's mom called him for dinner. Timmy was excited because he loved his mom's cooking. But when he got to the kitchen, he saw that his little sister had eaten all the food. Timmy was upset and thought it wasn't fair. 

Timmy went to bed that night feeling sad and hungry. He wished for a better day tomorrow. But unfortunately, Timmy got sick and had to stay in bed for a long time. Timmy was very sad and missed playing with his friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She wanted to study and learn lots of things. So every day, she would get her stuff, like her books and pencils, and sit down to study.

Sometimes it would hurt her. The numbers and letters looked hard. But she kept studying and eventually she got better and better.

After awhile, she had learned lots of stuff. She was so proud of herself. Then, she started to teach her friends what she had learned. They all liked learning from her.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Annie. She was only 3 years old, but very brave. 

Annie was walking in the park when she saw a man who was walking a big dog. The dog was wearing a big belt. Annie wanted to have a closer look and so she moved closer.

The man saw this and yelled "No! Go away!". Annie was a bit scared and so she took a few steps back.

Annie began to feel a bit sad but then the man said "Do you want to see the dog's belt?". Annie was very excited and nodded her head. 

The man let Annie look at the belt and she was very grateful. She thanked the man and they both went on their separate ways, feeling very happy.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. They had a small plant that they watered every day. The plant had green leaves and purple flowers.

One day, Anna was feeling bossy. She wanted to water the plant by herself. She said to Ben, "Go away, this is my plant. You can't touch it."

Ben was sad and angry. He said, "No, it is our plant. We share it. You are not nice."

Anna and Ben started to fight. They pulled the plant from each other. The plant was hurt. Some of the leaves and flowers fell off.

Anna and Ben stopped fighting. They saw the plant and felt sorry. They said to the plant, "We are sorry, plant. We did not mean to hurt you. Please forgive us."

The plant did not say anything. But it still looked alive. Anna and Ben decided to be nice to each other and to the plant. They hugged and said, "We are friends. We share the plant. We are not bossy."

They watered the plant together and put it in a sunny spot. The plant was happy. It grew new leaves and flowers. Anna and Ben were happy too. They played in the garden and took care of the plant. They learned to forgive and share.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play soccer with his friends. One day, Timmy's team was losing the game. Timmy wanted to help his team score a goal, so he ran as fast as he could with the ball. He kicked the ball and it went into the goal! Timmy was so lucky that he scored the goal. 

After the game, Timmy's friends congratulated him. They all wanted to touch the ball that Timmy used to score the goal. Timmy was happy to share the ball with his friends. They all touched the ball and said, "Wow, this ball is lucky!" From that day on, Timmy's friends called him "Lucky Timmy" because he scored the winning goal.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play by the ocean and watch the fish swim. One day, he saw an octopus in the water. The octopus was confused because he lost his way home.

Timmy asked the octopus, "Why are you confused?"

The octopus replied, "I don't know where my home is."

Timmy thought for a moment and then said, "I can help you find your way home." He then jumped into the water and swam with the octopus until they found his home.

The octopus was very happy and said, "Thank you for helping me. You are a good friend."

Timmy smiled and replied, "I am happy to help. Friends help each other."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her shiny crystal. One day, Lily's brother came into her room and accidentally knocked over her crystal. It fell to the ground and snapped into two pieces. 

Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her brother felt bad and said, "I'm sorry Lily, I didn't mean to break your crystal." 

Lily wiped away her tears and said, "It's okay, but it was noisy when it snapped." 

Her brother hugged her and promised to be more careful with her toys in the future. From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful with her special things, including her noisy crystal.

Once there was a doggy who was tumbling around on the grassy field. The doggy was very happy! Then he saw a man and asked the owner, "who are you?". The man smiled and said, " I am your new owner and I will take very good care of you". The doggy barked with excitement and followed the man to his house.

When the doggy arrived he was very surprised. The house was much bigger than he expected and it was very modern. He raced around and explored the new amazing home! Later, the doggy asked his owner, "what is this box that makes noise?". The man replied, "well, that is the radio. It will play music and stories". The doggy knew he was going to love his new home. 

The doggy curled up and fell asleep in his ownerâ€™s lap. He was very happy he had asked the man who he was. It was the best decision he ever made!

Molly was a 3 year old who had a lemon tree in her garden. One day, she decided to pick a lemon from the tree. She was so excited. As she grabbed the lemon, juice started to drip from it. Molly quickly wiped the juice away with her sleeve.

Molly then asked her mom if she could make a lemonade. Her mom agreed and gave her a recipe. It included lemon juice and sugar. Molly got to work and started to squeeze the lemon. She was having a great time. 

Molly started to worry when she noticed that her hands had become sticky from the lemon juice. She asked her mom: â€œHow do I stop my hands from getting sticky?â€ Her mom replied: â€œYou need to wipe your hands. Thatâ€™s perfectly normal.â€

Molly took a cloth and wiped her hands until they were clean and nice again. After that, she finished making her lemonade. She couldnâ€™t wait to take a sip and show the lemonade to all of her friends!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Bob. He had a net and he loved to play with it. One day, he went to the park with his net and saw a big pond. He decided to use the net to catch some fish.

He started to scoop the water with his net, but every time he only caught weeds. He was very disappointed. Then Bob saw a frog near the pond. He used his net to try and catch the frog.

The frog was very scared and shouted "No! Please do not catch me!" Bob was very surprised. He stopped and put his net away.

"I'm sorry," he said. "Why don't you jump into my net? Then I can carry you away from the disgusting pond."

The frog agreed and jumped into Bob's net. Bob held it carefully and carried the frog away from the pond. He put it down in the grass, safe and sound. He folded his net and went home, happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Megan. She was only three years old and had a big, strong heart.

One day, her parents gave her a special task. They handed her a bowl of sweet apples and told her to go outside and taste them.

Megan was so excited. She ran outside onto the grass, clutching the bowl of apples. She started tasting the apples, one by one. "Mmmm, these apples are so delicious!" she said as she finished her task.

Just then, her dad came out. He smiled and said, "What do you think of the apples? Do you like the taste?" Megan was so happy she almost burst.

"The apples are amazing!" she shouted with joy. After that day, Megan thought of those apples whenever she felt strong.

Jill's mum was drying her daughter's clothes when she noticed something strange. Jill was watching curiously. 

"What is it?" asked Jill.

"My daughter's clothes have painted designs on them," said her mum.

Jill was so curious. She wanted to know who painted the designs. "Who painted these?" She asked her mum. 

Her mum didn't answer. She smiled and said, "That's our secret". 

Jill was frustrated. She wanted to know so badly, but her mum seemed determined to keep it a secret. But Jill was not giving up. She was determined to find out the secret. 

Jill started asking everyone around but no one knew. She searched near and far and still couldn't get an answer. She was getting closer, but could she really find it?

Once upon a time, a nosy fireman lived in a big city. Jake the fireman was always looking out of his window and peeking around, wanting to know what was happening.

One day, he noticed a little girl across the street. He saw her grab a bright red balloon, and take it home. 

Jake thought it was weird and he wanted to know more. So, he ran across the street to talk to her. He asked her, "Where did you get the balloon?"

The little girl looked up and said, "A kind man gave it to me." She showed him all the other balloons the man gave to the other kids.

Jake smiled and said, "That was very nice of him."

The moral of the story is that it is always nice to be kind and help those who need it. Being nosy can make us miss out on seeing the good in people.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mommy. She saw a bird on a tree and stared at it for a long time. 

Suddenly, a boy came and asked, "What are you looking at?" 

"I'm staring at the bird," Lily said. 

The boy said, "I know a poem about birds. Do you want to hear it?" 

Lily nodded her head and the boy recited a poem about birds. It was so beautiful that Lily's face lit up with joy. 

But then, the boy said, "I don't like your dress. It's too plain." 

Lily felt sad because she loved her dress. She said, "I like my dress. It's my favorite." 

The boy realized he hurt her feelings and said sorry. They became friends and played together in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a small pebble named Pebby. Pebby lived in a big garden with many other pebbles. One day, Pebby saw a big rock talking to the other pebbles. Pebby wanted to understand what the big rock was saying.

Pebby went closer to listen, but the big rock saw Pebby and laughed. The big rock said, "You are too small to understand!" Pebby felt very sad and ashamed. Pebby wished to be big like the other pebbles so they could understand the big rock too.

One day, a nice bird saw Pebby feeling sad. The bird told Pebby, "You don't have to be big to understand. You just have to listen and learn." Pebby listened to the bird and started to learn from the other pebbles. Soon, Pebby could understand what the big rock was saying. Pebby was very happy and was no longer ashamed.

Zara was very enthusiastic. She wanted to try sewing with a needle.

So Zara asked her mom for a needle. Mom said yes, and gave her the needle.

Zara studied the needle carefully. Then she started to sew some old pieces of fabric. She was so excited!

But sewing with a needle was much harder than she thought. She kept pricking her finger, so she stopped for a bit and sucked her finger.

Mom saw Zara trying her best, and said, "You're so determined. You can do it!" 

Encouraged by her mom's words, Zara picked up the needle and kept sewing. Soon, she had made a beautiful blanket! She was so proud of her achievement and ran to show her mom. 

Mom was so impressed, and said, "You did it! You're the best!" 

Zara was overjoyed, and hugged her mom in happiness. Now she could make anything with a needle!

Lily was an adventurous girl who liked to explore new places. One day, she saw a big hill covered with snow. She wanted to slide down the hill on her sled. She put on her red mitten and ran to the hill.

But when she got there, she saw that there was another boy on the hill. He was also sliding on his sled. He had a blue mitten. He looked at Lily and said, "This is my hill. You can't slide here. Go away."

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "No, this is not your hill. This is a big hill for everyone. I want to slide too. You have to share."

The boy said, "No, I don't have to share. I was here first. You have to yield. That means you have to let me go first and wait for your turn."

Lily said, "No, you have to yield too. That means you have to take turns and be fair. You can't have the hill all the time."

The boy and Lily started to argue. They did not listen to each other. They did not have fun. They only made noise.

Then, they heard a loud roar. They looked up and saw a big bear coming down the hill. The bear was hungry and angry. He saw the boy and Lily and wanted to eat them.

The boy and Lily were very scared. They forgot about their sleds and their mittens. They ran away from the hill as fast as they could. They did not stop until they reached their homes.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that it is better to share and yield than to fight and be greedy. They learned that being adventurous is good, but being careful is also good. They learned that sometimes, a big hill is not worth a big trouble.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Ella. She was only three years old but she was very brave. One day Ella decided to go for a walk in the woods.

As she was walking, Ella heard a noise coming from behind the trees. She was scared at first, but she mustered up the courage to peek behind the trees.

To Ella's surprise, there was a beautiful fairy standing there. The fairy said, "Hi Ella, I have a special prize for you. I think it's very special, but I have to warn you: it might look very ordinary at first."

Ella was curious, so she said, "Yes please, can I have it?" The fairy smiled and waved her wand. A bright star appeared in her hands!

The fairy said, "This is your prize. It will always be with you, no matter where you go. Now you have a star, just like all the other stars in the night sky!"

Ella thanked the fairy and ran off with her prize, a bright, shining star. From that day on, she was never scared to explore the woods, knowing that her star would always be with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. He wanted to play with his bucket. So, he held it tight and started running around the garden. Suddenly, Jack got very dizzy. He wobbled and wobbled until he suddenly fell down. He started crying and mention his mommy.

His mommy heard his cries and quickly ran to find him. When she did, she saw him holding a bucket, lying on the ground. She asked him what happened and Jack explained that he got so dizzy while playing. His mom comforted him with a hug and then they went inside.

Jack was happy that his mom was so understanding. He felt better after they talked it out. From that day on, Jack remembered to take it slow and not make himself too dizzy. He still enjoyed playing with his bucket, only a bit more slowly.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy gears. He had big gears and small gears, and he would work hard to make them fit together.

One sunny day, Tim met a new friend, Sam. Sam was enthusiastic about the gears and wanted to play with Tim. They both sat down and started to work together. "Look, Tim! We can make the gears move faster when we work together!" said Sam.

As they played, they learned that working together made everything more fun. Tim and Sam became best friends, and they always worked together to make their gears spin. The moral of the story is that working together can make things easier and more enjoyable.

Once upon a time, there was a little radio. It was very heavy. The radio lived in a small room with a big window. The radio liked to be near the window so it could hear the birds sing.

One day, a little girl named Amy came to the room. She saw the heavy radio and said, "Oh, you are so heavy! Can you be my friend?" The radio was happy and said, "Yes, I can be your friend." Amy and the radio liked to play together.

Every day, Amy would come to the room and listen to the radio. They would sing songs and listen to stories. The heavy radio was happy to be Amy's friend. They had lots of fun together. And they lived happily ever after.

Once there was a lucky animal who lived in the forest, far away from humans. Every morning the animal woke up and roared, the sound echoing through the beautiful trees.

One day, a little girl stumbled upon the forest and heard the powerful roar. She was so curious and wanted to see what made such a sound. Walking carefully on a path, she spotted the animal. It was a tiger! The tiger looked at the little girl, and she to it. She ran towards it, shouting out of excitement.

The tiger was taken aback. It waved its paw, warning her to stay away. But the girl kept moving closer. Just as she was about to reach it, the tiger roared so loudly that the little girl stumbled back, startled.

She stayed put, waiting for the tiger to become calm. After some time, the tiger stepped forward with a calm look in its eyes. Then it opened its mouth and let out a much quieter roar. The little girl was relieved and very lucky that nothing bad had happened. From that day onwards, they were the best of friends. Roaring together in the beautiful forest.

Once there was a little girl called Molly. Molly was three years old. Every day her parents would tidy her room and make it very clean.

One day, her Aunt came to visit. Auntie brought a present for Molly. It was an extra special present that made Molly very happy. Auntie hugged Molly and she felt so comforted.

After the visit, Molly's parents were very pleased. They said to Auntie that she was so tidy. Then Molly gave her a big hug and thanked her for her visit.

Molly and Auntie spent the rest of the afternoon playing together and Molly felt very comforted by her Aunt's presence. 

When it was time to say goodbye, Molly's parents thanked Auntie for her visit. Molly hugged her again and gave her a big smile. Auntie was so happy that she had come to visit. 

Molly's parents said that they would like her to visit them again soon. Before she left, Auntie promised Molly that she would come and visit soon. 

Molly was feeling so comforted as she said goodbye to her Aunt. She couldn't wait until the next visit.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to gather nuts to eat. One day, Nutty found a big nut, but it was stuck in a tree. Nutty tried and tried, but couldn't get the nut out. Nutty started to scream for help.

A kind bird named Tweetie heard Nutty's screams and flew over to help. Tweetie calmly flew up to the tree and gently knocked the nut loose. Nutty was so happy and grateful that he shared his nuts with Tweetie.

From that day on, Nutty and Tweetie were the best of friends. They would gather nuts together and have fun playing in the trees. Whenever Nutty needed help, he knew he could scream for Tweetie and she would come to his rescue.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the color pink and had a pink dress that she wore all the time. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a boy who didn't have any friends to play with. Lily knew it wasn't kind to leave someone alone, so she went over to him and asked if he wanted to play with her. 

The boy was happy and they played together for a while. Lily noticed that the boy's shirt was also pink, just like her dress! She thought it was funny and they laughed together. After a while, it was time for Lily to go home. She said goodbye to the boy and gave him a big hug. 

Lily was happy that she could be kind to someone who needed a friend. She skipped all the way home, thinking about her new friend and how they both liked the color pink. It was a wonderful day at the park!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream, but his mom said he couldn't have any until he ate his vegetables. Timmy didn't like vegetables, but he tried his best to eat them all up.

After dinner, Timmy's mom asked him to help put away the leftovers. "Can you help me fit this container in the freezer, Timmy?" she asked. Timmy tried to put the container in, but it was too big. "It doesn't fit, Mommy," he said.

"That's okay, Timmy. We can put it in the fridge instead," his mom said. Timmy was happy that he didn't have to try and fit it in the freezer. "That's fair," he said with a smile.

Later that night, Timmy's mom surprised him with a bowl of ice cream. "You ate all your vegetables, so you deserve a treat," she said. Timmy was so happy and thanked his mom for being so fair.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers named Jack and James. They were playing catch with a ball in the garden, when suddenly their mother came running towards them. She wanted to prevent them from staying outside too long, so she called out: "Jack and James, it's time to come inside now and wait for dinner!" 

The boys reluctantly stopped their game, but Jack said: "Oh, please can we wait a little bit longer until the game is finished? We were having lots of fun!" 

But their mother just shook her head, and said: "No, you must come inside now. Come on, time to go!"

The boys did as they were told, and followed their mother into the house. Soon, the delicious smell of dinner cooking filled the air and made them all very happy. They all enjoyed their dinner, and both boys had lovely, contented smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a square. The square was very filthy. It did not like being filthy, so it wanted to move to a clean place.

The square started to move. It moved very slow. As it moved, it saw other shapes. The shapes were not filthy. The square wanted to be like them.

One day, the square met a circle. The circle was very clean. The circle saw the filthy square and wanted to help. The circle told the square to jump into the water. The square jumped into the water and became clean. Now, the square was happy and played with the circle and other shapes.

Once upon a time, there was a thief. He was not a very nice thief. He liked to pinch people. He would pinch people when they weren't looking.

One day, the thief wanted to pinch something very special. He thought and thought, and finally had a creative idea. He decided to pinch a diamond necklace from the jeweler.

So the thief waited until the jeweler was not looking. Then he quickly ran over and pinched the diamond necklace. He put it in his pocket and ran away, so no one could see him.

The jeweler saw him, but it was too late. The thief had already pinched the necklace and was gone. The jeweler was very sad. 

But, with some clever thinking, the jeweler managed to catch the thief. The thief was so surprised that someone was able to catch him! 

The thief learned a lesson that day. He never tried to pinch anything ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a little fly. The fly liked to shake its wings. It would shake, shake, shake all day long. The fly was very patient. It would wait for the perfect time to shake its wings.

One day, the fly met a big dog. The dog said, "Why do you shake your wings so much, little fly?" The fly replied, "I shake my wings because it makes me happy. I am patient and wait for the perfect time to shake them."

The dog thought about what the fly said. The dog decided to be patient too. It waited and waited for the perfect time to shake its tail. When the time was right, the dog shook its tail. It felt very happy just like the fly.

The fly and the dog became good friends. They would play and shake their wings and tail together. The other animals saw them and wanted to join in the fun. Soon, all the animals were shaking and being patient, waiting for the perfect time to shake.

And so, the little fly and the big dog taught everyone how to be patient and have fun. They all lived happily ever after, shaking and playing together in the warm sun.

Once, a bee wanted to have a hive to live in.

But the hive was expensive. The bee couldn't afford to buy it.

The bee was very sad.

So, it decided to return home.

On the way, it saw a cheap hive.

The bee was very happy, and immediately bought it.

It returned to its home with the new hive.

The bee was so excited to be in its new home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was walking through a park. She saw a big pole in the middle of the park, so she went over to it.

The girl touched the pole and it started to turn. She squeaked with excitement and started to turn it around and around. It was very easy to move and the girl could spin it around with one hand.

The girl played with the pole the whole day. She laughed as she felt it turn beneath her hand. She had so much fun spinning it around, it made her happy.

As the day ended and the sun started to set, the girl realised how much fun she'd had spinning the pole. She smiled, thanked the pole for the fun, and skipped away.

Little Kate and her family were out for a picnic. Everyone was very excited. Kate liked to observe the world around her.

She watched a family of birds. The parents were building a nest and the babies were happy and jumping around. That made Kate smile.

Kate looked around and saw lots of other families. One family had a lot of children, while another family had two children. Each family was flexible and did different things.

Kate looked back at her own family. Her parents hugged each other and her brother giggled. She smiled at the sight and knew that her family was special.

Ben and Lily wanted to make a cake for their mom's birthday. They were very enthusiastic and ran to the kitchen. They found a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, some sugar and some butter. They also found a spoon and a mixer.

"Let's mix everything together!" Ben said.

"OK!" Lily agreed.

They cracked the eggs and put them in the bowl. They added some flour, some sugar and some butter. They used the spoon to stir the mixture. It was hard and sticky.

"Let's use the mixer!" Lily suggested.

"Good idea!" Ben said.

They plugged in the mixer and turned it on. The mixer made a loud noise and spun very fast. It splashed the mixture all over the bowl, the table, the floor and themselves.

"Uh-oh!" Ben and Lily said.

They turned off the mixer and looked at the mess. They were covered in sticky cake batter. It felt wet and gooey on their skin and clothes. They also felt a strange sensation.

"Ben, I itch!" Lily said.

"Me too!" Ben said.

They scratched their arms, their legs, their faces and their hair. They realized they were allergic to something in the cake batter. Maybe it was the eggs or the flour or the butter. They didn't know.

They started to cry. They wanted to make a nice cake for their mom, but they made a big mess and got an itch. They felt sad and sorry.

Their mom heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw the disaster and her children's red and swollen skin. She was shocked and worried.

"Oh, my poor babies!" she said. "What happened?"

She hugged them and kissed them. She took them to the bathroom and washed them with warm water and soap. She put some cream on their itch and gave them some medicine. She told them they were brave and sweet and that she loved them very much.

She also told them that they didn't have to make a cake for her birthday. She said that their hug and kiss were the best gifts she could ever have. She said that they could make a cake another day, with her help and with different ingredients.

Ben and Lily felt better. They smiled and hugged their mom back. They said they were sorry for the mess and that they loved her very much. They said they wanted to make a cake another day, with her help and with different ingredients.

Their mom smiled and said that it was OK. She said that they were the best children she could ever have. She said that they could clean up the kitchen together and have some fun. She said that they could have some ice cream instead of cake.

Ben and Lily were happy. They said yes to ice cream and yes to fun. They followed their mom to the kitchen and helped her clean up. They were still enthusiastic, but more careful. They learned a lesson and had a good day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and very curious. One day she asked her mummy, "Where is the ocean?"
Her mummy smiled and said, "It's very far away!" So, Jane made a plan. She said, "Mummy, I want to see it!"

Her mummy said, "OK, let's go!" So, they both packed their bags and caught a boat. It was a long journey but soon they arrived at the ocean. It was so big and blue. Jane was amazed. She said, "Mummy, it's so beautiful!"

Then they went to the beach and Jane ran straight into the waves. She laughed and shouted, "It's so delicious!" She jumped around in the waves until she was all wet and then they went home. 

Jane will never forget the day she went to the ocean. It was the best day ever!

One day, there was a tornado. It was loud and exciting. The wind sprayed a lot of water everywhere. Nobody wanted to go outside because it was too dangerous. Everyone stayed inside and watched the tornado go by.

It was very boring inside. The little boy was getting sleepy from watching the tornado. He decided to try something different. He opened the window and stuck his head out. He saw the wind spraying the water around. 

The little boy liked it so much that he started to spray the water himself. He had so much fun. He was spraying water everywhere. He sprayed water on his mom, his dad, and even his dog. They all laughed, and the tornado seemed less scary all of a sudden. The little boy was having a great time. 

The tornado finally left and the little boy stopped spraying. Everyone went outside and had a wonderful time. They laughed and played and talked about the tornado. Nobody thought it was boring anymore.

Once there was a little giraffe called Happy. He loved to stand on the top of the hill and watch the sun set. One day, he saw a strange operation going on down at the bottom of the hill. A group of animals were gathered around a grey box that was making loud noises.

Happy walked over to the animals to try and find out what was happening. One elephant told him they were trying to fix the box before it caused any harm.

"What could be so dangerous?" Happy asked in surprise.

"We don't know," the elephant said, "But the grey box is unpredictable and it could be harmful if we don't fix it quickly."

Happy didn't know what to do. He was worried about the grey box, but he also wanted to help the animals. After a few moments of thinking, he stood up and volunteered to help. He got to work helping the animals repair the box.

After a few hours of hard work, the box was fixed and the animals were relieved. It had been a harmless operation, and everyone was very thankful to Happy for his help.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah who loved to explore outside. She was very brave and one day decided to go explore a creek.

Sarah came to a creek which was very filthy. The water was dark and had a bad smell. But Sarah was not scared. She loved to explore, so she stepped closer. 
Suddenly, Sarah lost her balance and fell into the creek. She was very afraid and started to cry out for help.

A kind lady heard Sarah's cries for help and quickly came to the creek. Together she and Sarah pulled herself safely out of the creek. 

The lady said to Sarah, "You were very brave to explore the creek, but it's too dangerous for a little girl like you.  Next time make sure you stay away from this filthy creek!" 

Sarah thanked the kind lady and promised never to fall into the creek again. She went away happily and never explored that filthy creek again.

One day, a little girl named Sue was playing in her room. She saw her mom's big armchair in the living room. Sue thought it would be fun to jump on the armchair. She climbed up and started to jump.

Sue's mom heard her and yelled, "Sue, stop jumping on the armchair!" Sue stopped and looked at her mom. She felt sorry for what she did. Sue said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I won't do it again."

Later, Sue's dad came home. He saw the armchair and said, "Wow, this armchair looks very nice and clean!" Sue's mom smiled and said, "Yes, Sue helped me keep it that way." Sue felt happy and proud that she learned her lesson.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. One day, Sarah went to the store with her Mommy. There were lots of interesting things in the store. In the fruit section, Sarah saw something very unusual. It was a big, green fruit with funny stripes. It was very exciting!

Mommy asked if Sarah wanted to try the unusual fruit. Sarah said yes and Mommy bought it. When they came home with the fruit, Mommy helped Sarah cut it open. There was a special surprise inside. It was a bright yellow fruit with lots of sweet juice!

Sarah couldn't wait to try the unusual fruit. She liked it very much. Next time they go to the store, Sarah will see if there are any other unusual fruits!

Once upon a time, there was a dish. It was lively and colorful, with yellow, green and red. One day, a little bug wanted to make the dish its home. Carefully, it settled onto the curved surface of the dish.

The little bug watched as the dish was lifted and placed onto the big, wooden table. As it surveyed the room, it was filled with lots of fun things to do - like a big pile of colorful blocks and a soft, furry toy.

The little bug felt content and enjoyed watching the lively family. The children ran around the room and the mom and dad laughed and talked.

The little bug was happy to have found a nice place to settle. He stayed there for a long time and would keep watch over the family every day, happily living in its dish.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot liked to jump and play in the park with his friends. One day, Spot saw a shiny collar on the ground. He picked it up and put it on. The collar was too tight, but Spot didn't mind.

Spot's owner didn't see the new collar and took him for a walk. Suddenly, Spot saw a squirrel and ran after it. He tried to jump over a fence, but the collar got stuck. Spot couldn't breathe and fell down. His owner tried to help him, but it was too late. Spot was dead.

Everyone was very sad. They buried Spot in the park and put flowers on his grave. His owner cried and wished he had never put the collar on Spot. From that day on, everyone remembered Spot as a happy dog who loved to jump and play.

Once, there was a little girl who saw a purple creature. The creature was very dangerous. She wanted to introduce herself and asked it what its name was. But when she tried to do this, the creature got angry. It tried to attack the girl. She was so scared that she ran away as fast as she could.

The little girl never saw the purple creature again. She was so lucky that she had escaped from it. The creature was too dangerous for her and she thought it was best to stay away from it. But she always remembered the day she tried to introduce herself to the purple creature. She never forgot how dangerous it was.

Mama and Baby Bear were walking through the forest one day. Mama Bear was pointing to all the different animals. "Look Baby Bear," she said, "here is a rabbit. And there is a squirrel. Do you see the young fawn in the meadow?". 

Baby Bear was so excited! He pointed to the meadow and said, "See, Mama. Good fawn!"

Mama Bear laughed and said, "That's right, Baby Bear. You are very smart. Good job!" 

They continued on their walk and eventually stopped to rest. Mama Bear pointed up at the trees and said, "See the birds in the sky? They are so tiny and can fly very high. Isn't that good, Baby Bear?" 

Baby Bear smiled and said, "Yes, Mama. Good birds!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to read. He had a big book with lots of pictures and words. One day, he went outside to play and saw a pile of leaves. He wanted to jump in them, but they were too messy. 

Timmy's mom came outside and saw the leaves. "We need to rake these leaves," she said. "Can you help me, Timmy?" Timmy was brave and said yes. They worked together and raked all the leaves into a big pile. 

Then, Timmy's little sister came outside and wanted to jump in the pile. But Timmy said no because they worked hard to make it neat. His sister got upset and started to cry. Timmy felt bad, so he read her a story from his book. She stopped crying and they all played together in the leaves. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a computer. Its job was to protect the family's secrets. One day, the computer was very nervous. It was scared that someone would steal the secrets. So it decided to hide them. 

The computer started looking for a place to hide. First, it looked in the closet. But the closet was too small. Then it looked under the bed. But there were too many stuffed animals there. The computer kept searching until it found the perfect place. 

The computer hid the secrets in a toy box. It told the secrets to stay safe and to never leave the box. Then it ran to the kitchen and told the family. 

The family was very happy to know the secrets were safe. From then on, the computer made sure the secrets stayed safe. It even decorated the box with stickers so that everyone knew it was an important box. 

The computer was happy it was able to protect the family's secrets. It was proud that it did a good job.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Betty. They were playing in the park together. Bob had a kite and Betty was running around chasing it. Suddenly Bob's kite flew out of reach and they both stopped to take a break.

Betty lay down in the grass and closed her eyes. She put her sweet hand on her forehead and breathed deeply. She began to relax.

Bob watched her for a moment and then lay down next to her. He felt himself start to relax too. The day was warm and the sun felt nice on his face.

Soon enough, the two friends felt so relaxed that they fell asleep in the park. They both had a sweet nap and when they woke up, they felt refreshed and happy.  They hugged each other and jumped up ready to play again.

Sam had a wonderful idea. He wanted to explore someplace new and exciting. So Sam asked his mom if he could explore the beach. She thought it was a creative idea and she gave him permission.

Sam set off with his bucket and his net. He wanted to explore and have fun.

When he reached the beach, Sam started looking around. He soon saw some small crabs scuttling around in the sand. His eyes lit up and he exclaimed, "I found some crabs!"

He tried to catch one with his net. He was a little too slow and the crab scuttled away. After a few minutes, he had managed to catch one. "Wow, look how fast it is!" He said proudly.

Sam put the crab carefully in his bucket and watched it for a while. It seemed so strong and brave. He liked it a lot! Sam's mom saw Sam happily playing and gave him a big hug. She was proud that he was so creative and brave. 

The two of them had a great day at the beach. Sam was so happy he had permission to explore and find something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pink dress that she loved to wear every day. One day, Lily went for a walk in the dark forest. She was scared because she couldn't see anything. Suddenly, she heard a noise and saw a little bunny suffering. She picked up the bunny and took it home with her. 

Lily took care of the bunny and gave it some carrots to eat. The bunny was very happy and started to feel better. Lily was happy too because she loved animals. She decided to keep the bunny as her pet and named it Pinky. From that day on, Pinky and Lily were best friends and they went on many adventures together in the forest.

Once there was a little girl named Sally. Sally wanted to drive her dad's car. Her dad said she was too young to drive, and she had to wait until she was older.

Sally was very sad. She wanted to be able to drive and show off her driving skills.

One day, her dad got an amazing trophy at work. The trophy was shaped like a car with gold wheels and a bright blue finish. Sally knew right away that this was the perfect trophy for her.

Her dad was a bit harsh, and he said no. But little Sally was not going to give up that easily. She reminded her dad of all the hard work she had done, and after a few minutes of arguing, her dad gave in.

Sally was so happy. She grabbed the car-shaped trophy and sat behind the wheel for the first time. She pretended to drive, turning the wheel and pushing the pedals with her little feet.

Sally loved her new driving trophy and spent lots of time honing her driving skills. She eventually became a great driver, and all because of her dad's special trophy.

Ben and Mia have a pet parrot. His name is Coco. Coco can say many words. He likes to say hello, bye, and his own name. He also likes to copy what Ben and Mia say.

One day, Ben and Mia are playing with Coco. They teach him some new words. They say "calm", "happy", and "love". Coco repeats them. He says "calm, calm, happy, happy, love, love". Ben and Mia clap and hug Coco. They are proud of him.

But then, Coco sees a big dog outside the window. The dog is barking loud. Coco gets scared. He forgets the new words. He says "woof, woof, help, help, Coco, Coco". He flaps his wings and squawks. Ben and Mia try to calm him down. They say "shh, shh, it's okay, Coco, it's okay. The dog can't hurt you. You are safe with us. We are calm, happy, and love you".

Coco listens to Ben and Mia. He sees that they are not afraid. He feels their hugs. He calms down. He stops saying "woof, woof, help, help". He says "calm, calm, happy, happy, love, love". He smiles and nuzzles Ben and Mia. They smile and nuzzle him back. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a brave robot called Sparky. Every day, he would go out and fix broken things. 

One day, Sparky saw a huge wreck in the middle of the road. He wanted to help, so he decided to go and fix it. When he arrived, he saw it was a bus. 

"Oh no!" Sparky said. "That needs to be fixed!" He worked hard and fixed the bus. 

Just then, a driver appeared from nowhere. "Thank you for fixing my bus," he said. "I was worried it could never be fixed, but you made it work again. You are so loyal." 

Sparky smiled. "You're welcome," he said. 

And that was how Sparky fixed the bus and made the driver very happy.

Once there was a little girl who wanted to go to a party. She asked her mom for an invitation. When the invitation came, it was very colorful. It had all sorts of happy designs on it, like stars and stripes and swirls. The little girl was so excited! She cheered and jumped around. She was ready to go to the party.

The little girl and her mom went to the party. It was in a big park and there were lots of people and all sorts of fun things to do. There were bounce houses and a water slide and games and food. Everything was so colorful!

The little girl had a great time at the party. She wanted to stay all day and play with her friends. But all too soon it was time to go. The little girl was sad but she had lots of great memories from the party, and a ton of colorful pictures to look back on.

Once upon a time, there lived two boys who were best friends. They always played together and had so much fun.

One day, the boys went outside to play and they decided to explore a cave. When they went inside, they saw a bright spirit. It was buzzing with energy and looked very special.

The boys were very curious and wanted to touch it, but the spirit said to them, "You must not touch me! I am too important and must stay here."

The boys were disappointed, but they said, "Ok, we understand. We will not touch you."

But then one of the boys had an idea. He suggested that if they asked nicely, the spirit would allow them to touch it. The other boy thought this was a great idea and so they asked the spirit nicely if they could touch it.

The spirit allowed them to touch it and the boys felt a great joy that they had never felt before. The spirit was so important that it made them feel special. They thanked the spirit and continued to explore the cave. From that day on, they would often come back to the cave and talk to the spirit.

Once upon a time, there was a bookcase. It was made of wood and it was tall and strong. All day long, it stood alone in the room.

But one night, the bookcase started to sing a sleepy song. It said, "I want to sleep, I want to rest."

The bookcase asked all around, "Is there a place where I can sleep?" But no one was available. So the bookcase had to find a place to sleep by itself.

Finally, the bookcase sighed and lay down on the floor. It was cozy and it was warm, so the bookcase went to sleep.

It dreamed of the days when it was available, when it was filled with books and when it was standing in the room.

The bookcase slept all night long, until the morning light came shining through the window. Then the bookcase woke up and stood up tall again. It was happy to be available and ready for another day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but she always made a big mess. One day, her mom came in and said, "Lily, you need to clean up your toys. It's not safe to leave them all over the floor."

Lily replied, "But mom, I don't know how to balance them all!"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's okay, we can work on it together."

So, they started to clean up the toys and Lily's mom showed her how to balance them on top of each other. Lily thought it was charming how they could all stay together without falling.

After they finished cleaning, Lily's mom said, "Remember, it's important to take care of our earth too. Just like we balance our toys, we need to balance the things we do to keep our planet healthy."

Lily nodded and said, "I will try my best to keep the earth clean and balanced too!"

Once upon a time there was a huge book. The book was loved by a little girl named Sue. Every day she would give the book a huge hug.

One day, Sueâ€™s mommy gave her a pair of scissors. â€œYou can use these to cut,â€ her mom said.

Sue was so excited. She grabbed the scissors and ran straight to the huge book. Sue started cutting and cutting. She trimmed the pages into shapes, drew lines and designs. She was so proud of all the new shapes she made.

Suddenly, Sue heard someone calling her name. It was her mommy. â€œSue, why did you cut the book?â€ Mommy asked. She looked really mad.

Sue was scared, but she was brave to admit her mistake. â€œI wanted to make it look pretty,â€ she said. 

Mommy gave Sue a hug. â€œI know you meant well, but next time, you must ask permission before you cut anything, okay?â€ 

Sue nodded her head, and she and her mommy hugged the huge book together.

Once upon a time there was a stick. It was a gentle stick. Every day the stick enjoyed sitting in the sunshine in the park.

One day, the stick was sitting by the lake. Suddenly, a big, mean puff of wind came, and it picked up the stick! The stick tried to hold on, but it couldn't keep a grip. The wind carried the poor stick way away, up high into the sky. The stick was scared of all the heights, but it kept flying, and soon it was out at sea.

The wind tossed the stick around for a long time. The stick was so very far from home and so very scared. Finally, the wind got tired and let the stick fall into the deep, dark water.

The poor stick was never seen again. It never enjoyed the sunshine, never saw its friends. The gentle stick was gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a colorful bird. The bird liked to fly high in the sky. The bird had many friends.

One day, a big wind came. The wind was a hurricane. The bird and its friends were scared. They needed to find a safe place.

The colorful bird had an idea. It started to ring a bell. The bell sound was loud. All the friends heard the bell and came together. They found a safe place to hide from the hurricane. The bird and its friends were happy and safe.

Once there was a little girl named Bella who loved to clean. Every day she would grab her cloth and bucket and go around cleaning everything in sight.

One day, Bella wanted to clean her big space. It was pretty big, so she was really excited to get it cleaned up. She put her cloth and bucket away and got to work.

She scrubbed the floors, dusted the walls and was careful to get into all of the corners. Soon the space looked beautiful! It was so impressive that she couldn't help but smile.

When Bella finished, her space looked so clean and tidy. She was so proud of what she had done and couldn't wait to show her mom. 

"Mom, look how clean my space is!" she shouted. Her mom smiled and said, "That looks amazing, Bella. You did an impressive job!" 

Bella was so happy and couldn't wait to show off her cleaned space to her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jake. Jake loved to play outside and explore the world.

One day, Jake was playing near a pond and he saw a mask in the water. He wanted to get the mask so he started to struggle to get it. The water was deep, but he was determined to get the mask.

He finally managed to get it and looked at it with admiration. It was clean and sparkled in the sun.

"What a beautiful mask!" he said.

Then he heard a voice behind him. "That's my mask!" said an old man. 

The old man thanked Jake for getting his mask from the pond. Jake was happy that he was able to help the old man, and they both went their separate ways.

The sun was shining brightly one morning when Max decided to explore the creek near his house. He grabbed his bucket and waded into the cool water. Max was having so much fun, splashing and playing.

Suddenly, Max saw something in the water ahead of him. It was a sign. He floated closer and read the sign. It said 'Danger - Do Not Enter'. Max had learned about dangers, and so he backed away from the creek.

Max was sad but he knew it was better to be safe than sorry. He thought of a plan. Max decided to go home, get his binoculars and then he could watch the creek from a safe distance.

Max eventually made it back home but he was careful to keep his distance from the creek. He set up his binoculars and zoomed in on the creek. Through the binoculars he could see the dangerous things that might be lurking in the water.

He was glad he didn't try to go closer. For now, Max will just have to keep watching the creek from a safe spot.

Once upon a time, there was a playful puppy named Max. Max loved to run and jump and play all day long. One day, Max's family decided to take him to a restaurant. Max was very excited to go to the restaurant and try some new food.

When they arrived at the restaurant, Max was so happy that he started to jump around and wag his tail. But then, Max saw a big bowl of water on the floor. He ran over to it and started to play in the water. He splashed and splashed until he was soaking wet.

Max's family was very embarrassed and they had to take him home early. Max was sad that he couldn't stay and play anymore. When they got home, Max's family gave him a bath and put him to bed. Max was very tired and sad that he couldn't go back to the restaurant.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They both loved to play the trumpet and they were very good at it. They practiced every day and they loved to compete with each other to see who was the best.

One day, they got into a big fight because they both wanted to play the trumpet at the same time. They were so competitive that they didn't want to share the trumpet. They were both very angry and they didn't talk to each other for a long time.

But then, they realized that it was better to share the trumpet and play together than to fight and be separate. They learned that being friends was more important than being competitive. From that day on, they played the trumpet together and they were very happy. The moral of the story is that it's better to share and be friends than to be competitive and separate.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a lot of toys, but he was always asking for more. His mommy and daddy always gave him what he wanted, but they noticed that Timmy was becoming spoiled.

One day, Timmy's mommy and daddy decided to take away some of his toys. Timmy was sad at first, but then he realized that he didn't need so many toys to be happy. He started to play with the toys he still had and he had even more fun than before.

Timmy's mommy and daddy were very happy to see him improve and learn that success doesn't come from having a lot of toys. They were proud of their little boy and happy to see him grow up to be a kind and happy person.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man named Jim. Jim had a huge house and lots of money, but he didn't know what to do with it. One day, while he was walking around town, he met a small boy. His name was Sam.

When Jim asked Sam what he was doing, Sam said he was playing in the sand. Jim loved watching Sam play, and decided to join him. For hours, they played together in the sand.

Soon, Sam asked Jim why he had so much money, and Jim replied that he was looking for a way to use it. Sam told Jim that he should build a big jungle in his backyard. Jim liked the idea and thanked Sam for the suggestion.

Little did they know that this was just the beginning of their adventure together! Jim used his money to build the jungle and he and Sam spent their days playing in it. As years went on, Jim became even richer. Not just richer in money, but richer in life as well!

Once upon a time there was a wide and adventurous forest. In the middle of the forest lived a little bear called Bob. Bob was always looking for new and exciting things to do. One day Bob heard a sound in the forest, it was a peculiar sound like something he had never heard before - it was the sound of music.

Bob tiptoed towards the music and saw a group of animals dancing in a big circle. He was curious so he asked one of them, "What are you doing?"

The animal answered, "We are dancing! Would you like to join us?"

Bob was excited and he jumped in the circle and began to dance too. They danced around in the magical forest and it made them feel so happy and adventurous!

That night Bob went to sleep with a big smile on his face. He knew that dancing was a wonderful way to spend his days and he was very happy that he was brave and adventurous enough to join the dance.

Bee and Ant were friends. They liked to play and help each other. One day, they saw a big hive on a tree. The hive had many bees and honey.

"Bee, is that your home?" Ant asked.

"Yes, it is. Do you want to see it?" Bee said.

"Can I? Is it safe?" Ant said.

"Of course, it is safe. You are my friend. Come with me. I will show you around." Bee said.

They flew and crawled to the hive. Bee introduced Ant to her family and friends. They were very nice and gave Ant some honey to taste. Ant liked the honey. It was sweet and sticky.

"Wow, your home is amazing. You have so much honey and so many bees. How do you make it?" Ant asked.

"We work hard and cooperate. We collect nectar from flowers and make honey. We also build and improve our hive. We make it bigger and stronger. We have a queen who leads us and cares for us." Bee explained.

"That is very impressive. You are very smart and organized. I admire you." Ant said.

"Thank you, Ant. You are very kind and brave. I admire you too. You can carry many times your weight and you live in a big colony. How do you do it?" Bee asked.

"We also work hard and cooperate. We gather food and store it. We also dig and improve our nest. We make it deeper and wider. We have a queen who lays eggs and makes more ants." Ant explained.

"That is very amazing. You are very strong and loyal. We have a lot in common." Bee said.

"Yes, we do. We are both insects and we both live in groups. We both have queens and we both make food. We are both friends and we both like to learn." Ant said.

They smiled and hugged. They decided to visit each other more often and share their knowledge and skills. They also invited their families and friends to join them. They had a lot of fun and made more friends. They improved their hive and their nest. They also improved their friendship. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to bounce around in the grass and play with his friends. One day, Benny fell and hurt his paw. His mommy called an ambulance to take him to the hospital. Benny was scared, but the ambulance came quickly and the nice paramedics took good care of him. Benny was impatient to get better so he could go back to playing with his friends. After a few days, Benny's paw felt much better and he could bounce around again. He was so happy to be back with his friends and have fun in the sunshine.

One day, a little girl was walking outside in her mild weather. She was wearing her new hat that her mom had bought for her. As she was walking, she noticed a man on the corner. The man was trying to steal hats from the people that were passing by. The little girl was scared, but she didn't want to lose her new hat. She quickly ran away and hid behind a tree.

The man didn't notice the little girl. He just kept stealing hats from the people. But then, he tried to steal the hat off of the little girl's head. He reached for her hat, but the little girl was too fast. She ran away from the man and back to her family's home. 

The little girl was never scared again. She kept her hat safe, and she never forgot to watch out for the bad man trying to steal hats. The little girl loved her hat, and she never let anyone take it away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go to the park with her mommy and daddy, but they didn't have enough seats in the car. Lily insisted that she could sit on the floor, but her parents said it wasn't safe. 

Finally, her daddy had an idea. He said, "Lily, why don't you sit in my lap? That way we can all go to the park together!" Lily thought this was a great idea and climbed into her daddy's lap. 

When they got to the park, Lily wanted to play on the swings. But she was a little scared because they looked hard. Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. The swings are easy to use. I'll show you how!" And sure enough, after a few tries, Lily was swinging higher than anyone else in the park. 

Lily had so much fun at the park that day, and she was so happy that her parents found an easy way to bring her along. She insisted that they come back again soon, and they all agreed it was a great idea. The end.

One day, there was a girl who was feeling very sad. She was standing with her shoulder slumped, looking around for something to make her happy. Suddenly, a magical butterfly flew over her shoulder. She felt so grateful for it's beauty, that her sadness disappeared! She watched as the butterfly flew off into the sky, and she smiled.

The next day, the girl returned to the same spot. But unfortunately, the butterfly was not there. Her sadness returned, but she remembered how great it had felt the previous day. She lifted her shoulder and thanked the butterfly.

The following day, the girl visited the spot again. To her surprise, the butterfly had returned! She was so grateful and thanked it with a big smile. She watched as the butterfly flew away, still feeling very grateful.

This pattern happened several more times. Whenever the girl was feeling down, the butterfly would magically appear. She learned that if she was grateful, the butterfly would come and make her happy. She thanked it each time it disappeared into the sky, feeling happier and more grateful each time.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl named Alice. She was very curious and loved to create things. One day, she got a special idea. She decided to make some special candy! She gathered all of the ingredients she needed, plus a little extra special something. 

Alice worked very hard to make her candy. She mixed and stirred, and watched carefully as her candy started to take shape. When it was finally ready, she was very proud of her creation. 

Alice took a bite of the candy. It was delicious! She wanted to share her candy with the world, so she decided to give it away. She bravely set out to tell her friends what she had made. 

Everyone was so amazed that Alice had created such delicious candy. They couldn't believe how brave she had been to make and share it. From then on, every time Alice had a special idea, her friends knew it was going to be something special and delicious!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys and his friends. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play. Timmy saw his friends and ran to play with them. 

Timmy's friends were playing a game and they asked Timmy to join. Timmy was very excited and started to play. Suddenly, Timmy fell down and his pants ripped. Timmy was embarrassed and ran away crying. 

Timmy's mom saw him and tried to make him feel better. She told him that accidents happen and it's okay to make mistakes. Timmy felt a little better and they went to get ice cream. 

On the way home, Timmy saw a man shouting and fighting with another man. Timmy was scared and asked his mom why they were fighting. His mom said that sometimes people don't get along and it's important to try and make peace. 

When they got home, Timmy's mom opened the door and they saw that their house had been robbed. Timmy was very scared and didn't understand why someone would do that. His mom called the police and they came to investigate. Timmy felt sad and scared because he lost his favorite toy. 

In the end, the police caught the robbers but Timmy still felt sad because he lost his toy. His mom hugged him and told him that they can always get a new toy but they can't replace the peace of mind that they lost.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a frog jumping around in the grass. The frog was green and had big eyes. Lily thought the frog was cute.

Lily went inside to get some cookies. She accidentally dropped some crumbs on the ground. The crumbs made a messy pile. Lily didn't clean it up because she was in a hurry to go back outside.

When Lily came back outside, she saw that the frog had hopped over to the messy pile of crumbs. The frog was eating the cookies! Lily was happy to see the frog enjoying the cookies. She decided to repeat this every day and share her cookies with the frog. From that day on, Lily and the frog became good friends.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a restless boy who loved to run and play all day. One day, as he was playing, he found a big tree with a small bird on a branch.

The small bird said, "Tim, I want to warn you. There is a big dog near the tree. Please be careful!" Tim looked around, but he could not see the big dog. The bird said, "Listen to my words and be safe."

Tim listened to the bird and walked away from the tree. As he walked, he saw the big dog coming. The dog barked loudly, but Tim was safe because he had listened to the bird's words. Tim thanked the bird and went home, feeling happy and safe.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Amy. They were both playing around in an elevator. They were very excited and kept pushing all the buttons. 

Suddenly, the elevator started to move very fast! Amy and Bob were scared, but then Bob said, "Let's try to catch the buttons!"

They both tried to catch the buttons, but the elevator was going too fast. Amy said, "It's too hard to catch the buttons. What should we do?" Bob said, "Let's just make this elevator go the other way!"

So, Amy and Bob worked together and quickly grabbed the buttons. The elevator stopped and they were so happy. They ran out and started playing again. 

"That was a fast ride!" said Bob. Amy said, "Yes, but don't do it again without a grown-up, ok?" Bob said, "Yes, ok." And they laughed together until the sun went down.

Anna and Ben were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They liked to look at the water and the fish and the birds. One day, the boat stopped near a small island. Mom and dad said they could go and play on the sand and look for shells.

Anna and Ben were happy and ran to the shore. They found many pretty shells and some rocks and sticks. They made a castle with the sand and decorated it with the shells. They had so much fun that they did not see the boat leave.

"Anna, look!" Ben said. "The boat is gone!"

Anna looked and saw that the boat was far away. She felt scared and sad. She did not know how to get back to mom and dad.

"Ben, what do we do?" she asked.

Ben did not know either. He felt scared and sad too. He hugged Anna and said, "Don't worry, Anna. Maybe they will come back soon. Maybe they just forgot us."

They sat on the sand and waited. They hoped that mom and dad would see them and come back. They felt hungry and thirsty and cold. They started to panic.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "We are here! We are on the island!"

But no one heard them. The boat was too far and the water was too loud.

They cried and cried. They wished they were back on the boat, where it was warm and comfortable and safe. They wished they were with mom and dad, who loved them and took care of them. They wished they never left the boat.

It was summer and the sun was shining brightly. Gina and her mom took a boat ride to the harbor.

When they arrived at the harbor, Gina was amazed. She had never seen so many big boats before. 

"Mom, why are there so many boats?" asked Gina.

"These boats sail to many different places. But we must be careful. Some waters can be dangerous," her mom said.

Gina knew what her mom meant. She could see the whitecaps on the horizon and knew they could not be too confident.

The pair returned back to shore with happy memories. Gina had learned something: there can be beauty in certain places, but you must also be aware of the dangerous waters.

Once there was a boy named Tim. Tim was sad and miserable. He did not have any friends. He liked to keep his toys on a bookshelf in his room. The bookshelf was big and had many toys.

One day, Tim saw a cat outside his window. The cat was lost and looked sad too. Tim wanted to be friends with the cat. He took the cat inside his house and gave it some food. The cat was happy and Tim was happy too.

But the cat liked to play with Tim's toys on the bookshelf. The cat knocked over the toys and broke them. Tim was very sad and angry. He took the cat back outside and said, "You cannot be my friend." Tim was alone again, and the cat was sad too.

Once upon a time, two friends were out walking together. One of them, Tess, had an umbrella. 

Suddenly, the sky grew dark and rain started to fall. Tess pulled out her umbrella and opened it up. "Be careful," she said to her friend. "We need to take it slow so we don't fall."

But it was too late! Her friend started running, and she stumbled and fell. Tess stepped in and closed the umbrella. She held it over her friend's head to protect them from the pouring rain.

Her friend blinked away the rain from their eyes and looked up at Tess gratefully. "Thank you," they said. 

Tess smiled. "You're welcome!" she said. "That's what friends are for!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her pink teddy bear more than anything in the world. One day, Lily was playing with her teddy bear when she accidentally dropped it behind the couch. She tried to reach for it, but it was hidden too far away.

Lily started to cry and her mommy came to see what was wrong. "What happened, sweetie?" her mommy asked. "I dropped my teddy bear and it's hidden behind the couch," Lily replied between sobs.

Her mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, we'll find it together." They moved the couch and found the pink teddy bear. Lily was so happy and hugged her mommy tightly.

The moral of the story is that it's okay to make mistakes and ask for help. Sometimes things get hidden or lost, but with a little help, they can be found again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a white teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, Lily was playing outside when she accidentally dropped her teddy bear into a muddy puddle. She was very sad because her teddy bear was now dirty and not white anymore.

Her friend, Tom, saw her crying and asked her what was wrong. Lily told Tom what happened and how sad she was. Tom said, "Don't worry, Lily. I have a dependable washing machine at home. We can wash your teddy bear and make it white again." Lily was very happy and accepted Tom's offer.

Tom took the teddy bear home and put it in the washing machine. After a few minutes, he took it out and it was as good as new! Lily was so happy and thanked Tom for being such a good friend. From that day on, Lily and Tom were the best of friends and they always helped each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and put on different outfits. One day, she found a pretty bow and wanted to wear it in her hair. But the bow kept falling out.

Lily's mom came in and saw her struggling. "Let me help you," she said. She took the bow and attached it to a clip. "Now it will stay in your hair," she said.

Lily was so happy and said, "Mommy, you're so good at fashion!" Her mom smiled and said, "I just know how to make things regular so they work properly." From that day on, Lily wore her bow every day and it never fell out again.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful bug. He lived in a big garden and he loved to sing songs. Every day, he would sing the same song - even when it was raining.

The bug wanted to help the other creatures in the garden so he came up with a plan. He decided to remain in the same spot so others could find him. He sang his song really loudly, so that everybody could hear him. 

One day, a baby bird in the garden heard the bugâ€™s song and became very happy, because she remembered that song. She called all her friends and they flew towards the bug because they wanted to meet him. 

The bug was so helpful and was really happy that his song was useful and he made many new friends. The bug, the baby bird and all their friends had so much fun together and sang the same song all day long!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the sunshine, but one day the sky turned gloomy and dark. Suddenly, a big tornado came and started to lift everything up in the air! Lily was scared, but her mom picked her up and carried her to the basement. They stayed there until the tornado went away. When they came back outside, everything was a mess, but they were safe. From that day on, Lily was always careful when the sky looked gloomy and knew to go to the basement if a tornado came.

Once upon a time, there was a very gloomy frog. He was so lonely, he just wanted to have a friend. So, one day, he decided to lie on his back in the sun. As he was basking in the glorious heat, a little girl, who was only three, came along. She saw the frog lying there, and said hello. The frog was so happy he jumped up and said hello back. 

The little girl was so delighted! She asked the frog if he would like to be her friend, and he said yes. From that day on, the frog and the little girl became the best of friends. Every morning the frog would jump out of his pond and give the little girl a big hug. 

The frog and the little girl even started having tea parties with mud pies! They had the best time together. Even on the gloomiest days, their friendship brought joy to their hearts. 

The frog and the little girl became inseparable. And their friendship never stopped blooming, from then until eternity.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the forest near her house. One day, she went on a trail and found a big puddle. 

Lily said, "I want to jump in the puddle, but I don't want to get wet!"

Her friend, a talking squirrel, said, "Why don't you soak your feet in the puddle? That way, you won't get too wet!"

Lily thought that was a great idea. She took off her shoes and socks and soaked her feet in the puddle. It felt cold and squishy, but also fun! 

From that day on, Lily and her squirrel friend would go on many adventures together. They would always find new trails to explore and new puddles to soak their feet in.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to ride their bikes. One day, they rode to the pond near their house. They saw some ducks and fish in the water.

"Look, Ben, the ducks are hungry. Let's give them some bread," Lily said.

"OK, Lily, but we only have a little bread. We need some for ourselves too," Ben said.
