They broke the bread into small pieces and threw them to the ducks. The ducks quacked and ate the bread. Lily and Ben smiled and watched them.

But then, a big goose came and chased the ducks away. It ate all the bread and honked loudly. Lily and Ben were scared and angry.

"Hey, goose, that's not nice. You should share with the ducks. They were here first," Lily shouted.

The goose ignored her and looked for more bread. It saw Lily and Ben's bikes and thought they were food. It bit the tires and the seats and made holes in them.

Lily and Ben ran to their bikes and tried to stop the goose. But it was too strong and mean. It pecked at them and made them cry.

"Help, help, someone help us," they screamed.

A man who was walking his dog heard them and came to help. He shooed the goose away and checked their bikes. He saw that they were ruined.

"I'm sorry, kids, your bikes are broken. You can't ride them anymore. What were you doing here?" he asked.

"We were feeding the ducks, but the goose came and took everything. It was greedy and nasty," Lily said.

The man nodded and said, "I see. Well, you were kind and generous to the ducks, but you should also be careful and wise. The pond is not a safe place for kids and bikes. There are many animals and things that can hurt you. Next time, you should ride somewhere else, or ask your parents to come with you."

Lily and Ben thanked the man and his dog. They learned their lesson and never rode to the pond again. They also learned to be more grateful for what they had and to respect other living things.

Once upon a time, there were two friends living in a forest. One day, they wanted to pick some fruit for breakfast. They started to quarrel about which kind to pick.

"I want to pick the big, juicy red berries," said the one.

"No, I want to get the small, green apples," the other exclaimed.

They argued and argued, until eventually they both said, "Let's just get both kinds of fruit!"

So, the two friends picked a big, juicy red berry for one friend and a small, green apple for the other. They were so happy to finally agree on something.

They ate the fruit together and had a great breakfast. Since then, they always agreed to share and picked different kinds of fruit. 

The End.

One night, Sarah went outside to look up at the sky. She noticed something special. At the top of the tall house, a chimney was wearing a hat of smoke. Sarah smiled. She thought it was very cool.

Sarah was tired, so she decided to go back inside for bedtime. As she stepped in through the door, she looked back up at the chimney one last time. It was still wearing its hat of smoke.

In the morning, Sarah went outside again to see if the chimney was still wearing its hat. Sure enough, there it was, wearing its smoke hat high up on the tall house.

Sarah thought the chimney was very special. She also thought it was very cool that the chimney was always wearing a hat of smoke at night. Sarah was tired again, but this time, she was tired from smiling so much.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Ben. Ben was three years old and loved to store his toys in his bedroom. He even had a special place where he stored his favorite toy.

One day Ben felt a strong urge to open his special toy box, but the lid was broken. He tried again and again but it wouldn't open. He started to feel sad and didn't know what to do.

Then his mom came into the room. When she saw Ben struggling with the toy box she said, â€œWhy don't you let me help you, Ben?â€

Ben was happy to accept the help. His mom used a screwdriver to carefully open the lid, and Ben gasped with wonder. Inside the box he found a lovely surprise-- a toy truck!

Ben clapped with joy and gave his mom a big hug. His urge to open the box had been worth it. From now on, Ben promised himself he'd always store his favorite toy safely in the box.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play in the garden and eat carrots. One day, while Fluffy was playing, he saw a big hole in the fence. Fluffy wanted to escape and explore the world outside the garden.

Fluffy went to his friend, a little bird named Tweety. "Tweety, I want to escape and see the world outside the garden. Do you want to come with me?" asked Fluffy. "Yes, I want to come with you," replied Tweety.

Fluffy and Tweety went through the hole in the fence and started to explore. They saw a big tree and decided to climb it. While they were climbing, Fluffy's nail got stuck in the tree. "Oh no, my nail is stuck!" cried Fluffy. Tweety helped Fluffy free his nail.

After a while, they saw a cheap ice cream truck. They went to the truck and bought some ice cream. Fluffy and Tweety had a great adventure and couldn't wait to explore more of the world outside the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play near the old creek. It was fun to throw rocks and watch the water splash.

One day, Tim saw a big, sharp stick near the creek. He wanted to play with it. But his mom said, "No, Tim! That stick is too sharp. It can hurt you."

Tim was sad, but he knew his mom was right. He left the sharp stick and went back to throwing rocks in the creek. And he had lots of fun playing safely by the water.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big fountain with water that went up and down. They ran to the fountain and put their hands in the water. It was cold and wet.

"Look, Lily, look!" Tom said. "The water makes mist. Can you see the mist?"

Lily looked up and saw the mist. It was like a thin cloud that floated in the air. She smiled and said, "Yes, I see the mist. It is pretty. Can we touch the mist?"

They tried to touch the mist, but it was too high. They jumped and stretched, but they could not reach the mist. They laughed and said, "The mist is too fast. We cannot catch the mist."

A man was watching them from a bench. He had a big hat and a big coat. He liked to see the children play. He clapped his hands and said, "Bravo, bravo! You are very good at jumping. You make me happy."

Lily and Tom heard the man and turned around. They saw him applaud. They did not know what applaud meant, but they saw he was happy. They smiled and said, "Thank you, thank you! You are very nice. Do you want to play with us?"

The man nodded and said, "Yes, I want to play with you. But first, let me give you something. I have a surprise for you in my coat."

He reached into his coat and pulled out two balloons. One was red and one was blue. He gave the red balloon to Lily and the blue balloon to Tom. They were very happy and said, "Wow, wow! Balloons! We love balloons!"

They took the balloons and ran to the fountain. They held the balloons high and tried to touch the mist. The mist made the balloons shiny and wet. They laughed and said, "Look, look! The mist likes the balloons. The balloons like the mist."

The man watched them and smiled. He was glad he gave them the balloons. He thought they were very good children. He did not see the bad dog that was coming from behind. The bad dog saw the balloons and wanted to pop them. He ran to the children and barked. He jumped and bit the balloons. The balloons popped and made a loud noise. The children screamed and cried. The man shouted and ran to the children. He scared the bad dog away. He hugged the children and said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. The bad dog was very mean. He popped your balloons. Are you okay?"

Lily and Tom were very sad. They lost their balloons. They said, "No, no. We are not okay. The bad dog was very bad. He popped our balloons. We liked our balloons. We want our balloons back."

The man felt very sorry. He said, "I know, I know. The bad dog was very bad. He popped your balloons. You liked your balloons. But I cannot give you your balloons back. They are gone. But I can give you something else. I have another surprise for you in my hat."

He took off his hat and showed them what was inside. It was a big cake with frosting and candles. He said, "Look, look! A cake! A cake for you! I made it for you. It is your special day. Happy birthday, Lily and Tom!"

Lily and Tom were very surprised. They did not know it was their birthday. They said, "A cake? A cake for us? You made it for us? It is our birthday? Happy birthday, Lily and Tom!"

They forgot about the bad dog and the balloons. They saw the cake and smiled. They said, "Wow, wow! A cake! A cake for us! You made it for us! It is our birthday! Thank you, thank you! You are very nice. You are our friend."

They blew the candles and made a wish. They wished for more balloons and more mist and more fun. They ate the cake and shared it with the man. They said, "The cake is very good. You are very good. We are very happy."

The man was very happy too. He said, "You are very welcome. You are very good. I am very happy."

They hugged and kissed and said, "We love you. You love us. We are a happy family."

They played and sang and danced. They saw the mist and the fountain and the sun. They did not see the bad dog that was hiding behind a tree. He was very angry and jealous. He said, "Grrr, grrr. I hate them. I hate them. They have a cake. They have a friend. They are happy. I want to make them sad

Once upon a time there was a bright lady. She loved to read books. Every day she would go to the library and pick out a different book. She would sit in the sunshine and read the stories with the pages turning. 

Sometimes other children would come to the library too. They liked to listen to the bright lady read stories to them. They would all sit around in a circle and listen to the beautiful stories together. 

The bright lady had a favorite story that she would read over and over. She would read it in the sunshine and the children loved to listen. 

The bright lady always had a smile on her face as she read the stories. The children were happy to hear her read and would always come back for more stories. 

Reading was so much fun for everyone!

Once upon a time, there was a big truck. The truck was very large and it could go very fast. It had big wheels that turned quickly and made a loud noise. The driver of the truck liked to whistle while he drove. 

One day, the driver saw a bird on the road. The bird was very small and it couldn't fly. The driver stopped the truck and got out to help the bird. He picked it up gently and put it in the back of the truck. 

As the truck drove down the road, the bird started to feel better. It looked around and saw how fast the truck was going. It felt like it was flying! The bird started to whistle too, and the driver smiled. They both enjoyed the speed of the big truck.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cold and her nose was very runny. Her mom gave her some medicine to make her feel better. 

Lily didn't like taking medicine because it tasted yucky. She sighed and said, "I don't want to take it, Mommy." 

Her mom smiled and said, "I know it doesn't taste good, but it will help you feel better. Just take it like a big girl." 

Lily took the medicine and made a funny face. Her little brother, who was always nosy, asked, "What's wrong, Lily?" 

Lily replied, "I had to take medicine, and it tasted yucky." Her brother laughed and said, "Silly Lily, medicine is supposed to help you feel better!"

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Anna has a colorful puzzle with many pieces. Ben has a big truck that can make noises. Anna likes to fit the pieces together and recognize the pictures. Ben likes to drive the truck around and make it honk.

"Look, Anna, I have a truck!" Ben says, showing his toy to Anna. "It can open and close and carry things. It is very fun!"

"That is nice, Ben, but I like my puzzle more," Anna says, holding up a piece. "It has many colors and shapes. It is very pretty!"

Ben wants to play with the puzzle too. He grabs a piece from Anna and tries to fit it in his truck. Anna gets angry and pulls the piece back.

"Hey, Ben, that is my puzzle! You have your own toy. Give it back!" Anna shouts.

"No, Anna, I want to play with the puzzle too! It is also fun!" Ben shouts back.

They start to tug and pull on the piece, making it bend and tear. They both cry and drop the piece on the floor. Their mom hears the noise and comes to the living room.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks, looking at the broken piece and the sad children. "Why are you fighting over a puzzle?"

"Ben took my puzzle and tried to put it in his truck. He ruined it!" Anna says, pointing at Ben.

"Anna did not let me play with the puzzle. She was mean!" Ben says, pointing at Anna.

Mom sighs and picks up the piece. She shows it to Anna and Ben.

"Look, this is a piece of a flower. It is very colorful and beautiful. But now it is broken and ugly. Do you think the flower is happy?" Mom asks.

Anna and Ben shake their heads. They feel sorry for the flower.

"Playing with toys is fun, but sharing them is even more fun. If you share your toys, you can make more friends and have more fun. Do you understand?" Mom asks.

Anna and Ben nod. They look at each other and say sorry.

"I am sorry, Ben. You can play with my puzzle if you want. But please be careful and do not break it," Anna says.

"I am sorry, Anna. You can play with my truck if you want. But please be careful and do not make it dirty," Ben says.

They hug and smile. They decide to play together and share their toys. They fit the puzzle pieces and recognize the pictures. They drive the truck and make it honk. They have a lot of fun. Mom is happy and proud of them. She gives them a kiss and a cookie. They say thank you and enjoy their snack. They are good friends. The end.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a small rabbit. The rabbit was white and had big ears. The rabbit's name was Fluffy. Fluffy liked to play with his friends. One day, Fluffy found an amazing pebble. The pebble was shiny and smooth.

Fluffy showed the pebble to his friend, a little bird named Chirpy. Chirpy said, "Wow, Fluffy! That is an amazing pebble! Where did you find it?" Fluffy told Chirpy that he found it near the big tree.

As they were talking, a big loud sound came from the sky. It made Fluffy and Chirpy tremble. They were scared. They hid behind the big tree and held the amazing pebble tight.

After a while, the loud sound went away. Fluffy and Chirpy came out from behind the tree. They were not scared anymore. They laughed and played with the amazing pebble. They knew that as long as they were together, they would be brave.

From that day on, Fluffy and Chirpy were the best of friends. They played in the big forest every day. And they always kept the amazing pebble with them, to remind them of their brave adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a competitive knob. It was a shiny knob and it could do so many things.

One day, the knob heard a whisper. The whisper said "You are the special knob." The knob was so excited!

So the knob started to try out some of the things it could do, like unlocking doors and turning things on and off. But the knob was getting tired of always being the same.

So the knob decided to go on an adventure. It was so much fun! The knob did all kinds of things and became more competitive with each new thing it tried.

At the end of the day, the knob was feeling very proud of itself and it went back home, whispering to itself "I am a very special knob!"

Susie was happy. She went to the cold field with her mom. The sun was shining, the wind was whispers around them.

"What are we going to do here mom?" asked Susie.

"We are going to use this field. We will pick some flowers," her mom said.

Susie looked around and saw that there were no flowers in the field. "Where are the flowers mom?"

"The flowers might not bloom yet, it's still too cold. We just have to wait," said her mom.

Susie was disappointed. She wanted to find some flowers now. But she saw her mom was sad too.

Susie had an idea. She gave her mom a hug and said, "Let's pick some grass. We can use it for something later."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea! We can make a little basket out of it."

So the two of them picked the grass. They made their basket and took it home. It was a happy ending for both of them.

Lily was sad. She had a big cut on her knee from falling down. It hurt a lot and it was red and wet. Mommy put a band-aid on it and gave her a hug. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. Your cut will heal soon. You are very brave."

Lily wanted to feel better. She liked to sing and dance. She had a stage in her room, made of boxes and blankets. She had a microphone and a dress and a hat. She wanted to put on a show for Mommy and Daddy and her teddy bear.

She asked Mommy, "Can I sing and dance on my stage? Will it make my cut heal faster?" Mommy smiled and said, "Sure, Lily. You can sing and dance on your stage. It might not make your cut heal faster, but it will make you happy. And being happy is good for healing."

Lily was happy. She put on her dress and her hat and grabbed her microphone. She went to her stage and turned on the music. She sang her favorite song and danced with her teddy bear. She felt the pain in her knee go away. She looked at Mommy and Daddy and saw them clapping and cheering. She said, "Thank you for watching my show. I love you very much."

Mommy and Daddy hugged her and said, "We love you too, Lily. You are a wonderful singer and dancer. And your cut is looking much better. It is not so red and wet anymore. It is clear and dry. You are healing very well." Lily was proud and happy. She kissed her cut and said, "Goodbye, cut. Hello, stage."

Once there was a big, blue ocean. In the ocean, there was so many things. One of the things was jellyfish. The jellyfish were so thick and many.

One day, the jellyfish wanted to separate. They wanted to find different parts of the ocean. So, they decided to take two paths. One path was big, the other path was small.

The small jellyfish went one way and the big jellyfish went the other. After separating, the jellyfish couldn't see each other any more. But, the jellyfish felt happy because they could explore the ocean. 

The jellyfish had so much fun in the ocean. And the jellyfish were still friends, even when they couldn't see each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to wear red clothes. She thought red was the best color in the world. Her mommy said that Lily had a great fashion sense.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. She wore her favorite red dress and red shoes. While playing, she saw a big bush with pretty flowers. Lily wanted to see what was behind the bush, so she decided to peek.

As she peeked behind the bush, she saw a cute, little red bird. The bird was singing a happy song. Lily smiled and said hello to the bird. The bird flew away, and Lily went back to playing. She was glad she peeked behind the bush and made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was an old black bird. He liked to fly around in the sky for fun. He flew so high in the sky, sometimes he couldn't see the ground below. One day, the old black bird was flying over a big mountain. He liked to fly around the mountain, so he flew around it again and again. But then something strange happened. As the old black bird flew higher and higher around the mountain, the air began to feel different. Suddenly, it felt like he was flying in a wind tunnel. Flying became easier and easier, and the old black bird flew higher and higher. He kept going until he couldn't see the mountain any more. He had discovered he could fly so high that he could look down from way up in the sky! The old black bird was so happy, he flew all around until nighttime came. He flew back home, ready to fly even higher the next day.

The three bears were walking through the forest. Mama Bear said, "I think I know where we should go!" 

Little Bear guessed, "Is it the lake? Is it the woods? Is it the meadow?"

Mama Bear smiled and said, "Guess again!" 

Big Bear said, "I think it's Grandma's house!"

Mama Bear said, "That's right! Let's go!"

They arrived at Grandma's house and she was very happy to see them. Grandma was bossy and said, "Let's go inside, I have something special for you all." They walked into the kitchen, and Grandma handed each of them a teaspoon. 

Little Bear asked, "What is this for?"

Grandma answered, "You can use it to eat your soup!"

Big Bear grinned and said, "Yay! Soup!"

Mama Bear said, "Let's eat!"

And they all sat down to enjoy Grandma's special soup.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet was very cheerful and loved to sing. One day, Tweet saw a flame in the forest. Tweet knew it was dangerous, so he flew to tell his friends. 

Tweet found his friends, Bunny and Squirrel, and told them about the flame. Bunny said, "Let's go put out the flame!" Squirrel said, "No, let's fight the flame!" 

Tweet knew they needed to work together, so they went to the flame. Bunny used her strong legs to stomp on the flame, and Squirrel used his bushy tail to smother it. Together, they put out the flame. 

The moral of the story is that when we work together, we can do great things. Even though Bunny and Squirrel wanted to fight the flame, they needed to work together to put it out. Tweet was happy that his friends helped him, and they all sang a cheerful song together.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys and make noise. But they do not like to eat their meal. They think it is boring and yucky.

One day, Mom makes a big meal for them. She says, "Come on, Sara and Tom, it is time to eat. You need to grow strong and healthy. This meal is good for you."

But Sara and Tom do not want to eat. They say, "No, Mom, we do not like this meal. We want to play more. Can we have candy instead?"

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, you cannot have candy. Candy is not a meal. It is a treat. You can have candy later, after you eat your meal."

Sara and Tom are sad. They do not want to eat their meal. They want to prevent Mom from making them eat. They have an idea. They say, "Mom, can we help you with the dishes? We want to be helpful."

Mom smiles. She says, "That is very nice of you, Sara and Tom. But you need to eat your meal first. Then you can help me with the dishes."

Sara and Tom are not happy. They do not like Mom's answer. They think of another idea. They say, "Mom, can we tell you a story? We have a very funny story. You will laugh a lot."

Mom laughs. She says, "That is very sweet of you, Sara and Tom. But you need to eat your meal first. Then you can tell me your story."

Sara and Tom are frustrated. They do not like Mom's answer. They think of another idea. They say, "Mom, can we sing you a song? We have a very beautiful song. You will like it a lot."

Mom claps. She says, "That is very lovely of you, Sara and Tom. But you need to eat your meal first. Then you can sing me your song."

Sara and Tom are out of ideas. They do not know how to prevent Mom from making them eat. They look at their meal. They look at Mom. They look at each other. They sigh. They say, "Okay, Mom, we will eat our meal. But we do not like it."

Mom hugs them. She says, "Thank you, Sara and Tom, for being good children. I know you do not like this meal, but it is good for you. I love you very much. And I am proud of you for trying something new."

Sara and Tom eat their meal. They do not like it, but they eat it. They want to make Mom happy. They want to be strong and healthy. They want to have candy later. They want to help Mom with the dishes. They want to tell Mom their story. They want to sing Mom their song.

Mom is happy. She says, "You did it, Sara and Tom. You ate your meal. You are very successful. I am very happy. Now you can have candy. And you can help me with the dishes. And you can tell me your story. And you can sing me your song."

Sara and Tom are happy. They say, "Yay, Mom, we did it. We ate our meal. We are very successful. We are very happy. Now we can have candy. And we can help you with the dishes. And we can tell you our story. And we can sing you our song."

They have candy. They help Mom with the dishes. They tell Mom their story. They sing Mom their song. They have fun. They love Mom. Mom loves them. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, comfy couch in her living room where she loved to sit and watch her favorite cartoons. One day, her mom brought home a new toy for her to play with. It was a toy train that Lily loved very much.

Lily decided to attach the train to the couch with some tape. She wanted to make sure it wouldn't fall off. Her mom saw what she was doing and said, "Wow, Lily! You're very clever. You attached the train to the couch so it won't move."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I did! I love my new train. It's so pretty." Her mom replied, "Yes, it is. You're lucky to have such a wealthy imagination." Lily didn't know what "wealthy" meant, but she knew it was a good thing because her mom sounded happy. She hugged her mom and said, "I love you, Mommy." Her mom hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily."

Mum and her little girl were making ice cream. The girl watched as Mum filled the bowl with cream and sugar. She smiled as Mum put it in the big box that shook and turned it around.

"What's that called, Mum?" the little girl asked.

"It's an ice cream maker," said Mum. "And do you know what it does?"

The little girl shook her head.

"It melts the cream and sugar together to make ice cream," said Mum.

The little girl watched as the box made the cream and sugar mix together. After some time, Mum opened the lid and the little girl peered inside. There was nothing there except an empty bowl.

"Where's the ice cream, Mum?" the little girl asked.

"It's finished melting, so now it needs to go in the freezer," said Mum.

The little girl watched as Mum put the empty bowl in the freezer. After a short while, Mum returned with a delicious bowl of ice cream.

The little girl smiled as she dug in with her spoon. Delicious!

Tommy was a smart 3 year old, much smarter than other children his age. He saw the world in his own special way. When his parents asked him to come with them to the park, he said yes. 

As they drove up to the park, Tommy noticed a big camera up in a tree. He asked his parents what it was and why it was there. His dad said, "It's a camera, Tommy. It was put there to take pictures of people in the park." 

When Tommy and his parents reached the park, Tommy spotted the camera again. But this time, he noticed something different. He saw people suffering, carrying heavy bags and struggling up the path. 

Tommy asked his dad what was going on. His dad smiled sadly and explained, "Those people are suffering because they have to carry heavy things. That camera is here to make sure they're following the rules." 

Tommy's dad gave him a hug and said, "You're so smart for understanding this." Tommy realized that the camera was there to help the people in the park, not to make them suffer.

Once upon a time, a little girl felt very anxious. She wanted to go to the city, but she was too scared. Then, she had a thought â€“ what if she could jump to the city?

So she tried. She jumped really really high, stretching into the sky and reaching for the clouds. Slowly, she flew through the air and landed in the city.

She was so excited to see the city up close! Everywhere she looked, there were bright buildings, lots of people and cars zooming around.

She looked up and saw the sun, beginning to set and all the lights of the city were beginning to turn on. It was so beautiful she couldn't help but smile.

The little girl was very happy that she had jumped to the city. She was no longer anxious, but brave and strong.

Anna was restless. She did not want to nap. She wanted to play with her toys and run around the house. But Mommy said she had to nap or she would be grumpy later.

"Please, Mommy, no nap!" Anna said, trying to resist Mommy's arms.

"Sorry, Anna, you need to nap. It's good for you. You can play after you wake up," Mommy said, carrying Anna to her bed.

Anna pouted and kicked. She did not like her bed. It was boring and soft. She wanted to be awake and loud. She saw a pear on the nightstand. She liked pears. They were sweet and juicy.

"Can I have the pear, Mommy?" Anna asked, hoping to get out of napping.

"No, Anna, the pear is for later. You can have it after you nap. Now close your eyes and sleep," Mommy said, tucking Anna in.

Anna frowned. She did not want to sleep. She wanted the pear. She reached for the pear when Mommy left the room. She grabbed it and bit into it. It was yummy. She smiled and ate more.

But then she heard Mommy coming back. She hid the pear under her pillow. She pretended to sleep. She hoped Mommy would not see the pear.

Mommy opened the door and looked at Anna. She saw the juice on Anna's mouth and the lump under her pillow. She knew Anna had the pear.

"Anna, did you eat the pear?" Mommy asked, lifting the pillow.

Anna opened her eyes and saw Mommy holding the pear. She felt guilty. She knew she was naughty.

"Sorry, Mommy," Anna said, looking down.

Mommy sighed. She was not happy. She took the pear and put it in the trash.

"Anna, you should not eat the pear. You should nap. Now you have no pear and no nap. How do you feel?" Mommy asked.

Anna felt bad. She felt tired and hungry. She wished she had napped and saved the pear.

"Sad, Mommy," Anna said, sniffling.

Mommy hugged Anna. She was not angry. She loved Anna.

"It's okay, Anna. I forgive you. But next time, listen to Mommy, okay? Napping and eating at the right time are important. They make you healthy and happy. Do you understand?" Mommy asked.

Anna nodded. She understood. She wanted to be healthy and happy.

"Okay, Mommy. I will listen to you. I will nap and eat at the right time. I love you, Mommy," Anna said.

"I love you too, Anna. Now let's try to nap again. Maybe you will have a nice dream about pears," Mommy said, kissing Anna's forehead.

Anna closed her eyes and cuddled with Mommy. She felt sleepy and calm. She napped and dreamed about pears.

One day, a big bus went down the road. The bus was very fair and nice. It had many colors and a happy face. The bus liked to take kids to fun places like the park and the zoo.

At the park, the kids saw a man balance on a long rope. He was very good at it. The kids clapped and laughed. They wanted to try to balance too. So, the man let them try, but he held their hands so they would not fall.

After playing at the park, the bus took the kids to the zoo. They saw many animals like big lions, tall giraffes, and funny monkeys. The kids were very happy. At the end of the day, the fair bus took them home. They waved goodbye to the bus and thanked it for the fun day.

One day, a little girl went to the beach. She wanted to build a sandcastle. She had a box with sand toys and batteries.

The little girl said, "Let's unpack the sand toys!" She took out the toys, a bucket and some shells. She started to dig and make towers.

Suddenly, the little girl stepped on something rough. It was a battery! The battery had broken and leaked all over the sand. The little girl started to cry.

The little girl's mom said, "It's okay, sweetheart. We have another box with batteries back at home."

The little girl was sad but they packed up their sand toys and left the beach. The sandcastle was never finished.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who went on a great big adventure. He was looking for something special, something he had never seen before. He looked and looked, but he couldn't find it. Finally, one day, he saw something hidden under the leaves. He bent down and picked it up. It was a peanut! He knew it had been hidden there all along. He was so excited and ran home to show his mom what he had found. He showed her the peanut and told her all about his adventure.She was so proud of him and they both enjoyed a big hug. The little boy was happy because he had found something special and enjoyed sharing it with his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who always forgot to wake up on time. His mummy decided it was time to get him an alarm. 

So they went to the shop together. There was a special alarm with a funny sound and it was perfect for him. But the boy was impatient and didn't want to wait until they got home to set it up.

Mummy explained that the alarm was for when it was time for him to wake up. Every morning when it went off, he had to get up and get ready for the day. The boy smiled as he liked the idea.

The next morning, the alarm made the funny sound and the boy was so excited. He grabbed his clothes and ran to the bathroom. 

Mummy was so proud of the boy for understanding what the alarm was for and getting ready so quickly! 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a treasure map on the ground. She followed the map and finally found the treasure. But when she opened it, she realized it was fake. 

Lily was very sad and angry. She screamed loudly and her friends came running to see what was wrong. Lily showed them the fake treasure and they all agreed to help her find the real treasure. They searched everywhere and finally found a real treasure chest. 

Lily was very happy and thanked her friends for helping her. She learned that sometimes things may not be what they seem, but if you keep trying, you can find something even better.

Once there was a bear who was very healthy. He was walking through the forest one day, looking for something to eat. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise behind him. The bear turned around to see a lion on his tail. The lion had a big, scary face and roared like a thunder. The bear was scared, so he started to run. 

The lion followed the bear through the trees and across the fields. The bear was so scared, he didn't know what to do. He knew the lion wasn't being friendly and was a threat to him.

The bear ran as fast as his legs could carry him and kept on running for a long time. Suddenly, he came upon a cave. Without thinking twice, the bear ran inside. The cave was dark and damp, but it was perfect for the bear to hide from the lion. 

The bear stayed in the cave for sometime until he was sure the lion had gone away. After an hour or so he came out. It was then that the bear realised how lucky he had been. He was safe and he had been kept away from the threat of the lion. 

The bear continued his journey through the forest, but this time he was more careful. He was determined to stay healthy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she pretended to be a princess in a castle made of blocks. She built a triangle-shaped tower and pretended to be trapped inside.

Suddenly, a big, strong dragon came and tried to break the tower. But Lily was weak and couldn't stop the dragon. She tried to run away, but the dragon caught her and took her away.

Lily's mom came to play with her toys later that day and found the broken tower and Lily's favorite toy missing. She knew something was wrong and called the police. They searched for Lily and found her in the park, scared and alone.

The bad dragon was caught and Lily was safe, but she never played pretend with that triangle tower again. She knew it was too dangerous.

Once upon a time there was a girl, called Jane. She was very stubborn. Every day she would skip all the way to school, carrying her bag. But one day something happened! There was an earthquake which made the ground shake. Jane was so scared that she refused to move. She was much too stubborn to skip anymore. She stayed still, even when the tremor stopped, until it was too late for her to get to school. The teachers were so angry with her for being late. Jane never went to school on time again.

Timmy was a chubby boy who loved jam. He ate jam on toast, jam on crackers, jam on pancakes. He had a big jar of jam in his room that he hid from his mom. He did not like to share his jam with anyone.

One day, Timmy went to the park with his mom and his little sister, Lily. Lily was a thin girl who did not like jam. She liked carrots and apples and cheese. She had a small bag of snacks in her mom's purse. She did not mind to share her snacks with anyone.

At the park, Timmy saw a big dog. The dog was brown and fluffy and had a red bow on its neck. The dog looked friendly and wagged its tail. Timmy wanted to pet the dog, but he was afraid. He hid behind his mom and watched the dog.

Lily saw the dog too. She was not afraid. She ran to the dog and said, "Hello, doggy! You are so cute! Can I pet you?" The dog licked her face and let her pet its fur. Lily giggled and said, "You are so soft and warm! Do you want a snack?" She took out a carrot from her bag and offered it to the dog. The dog sniffed the carrot and ate it. Lily smiled and said, "You like carrots? Me too! Do you want another one?" She gave the dog another carrot and the dog wagged its tail.

Timmy watched Lily and the dog. He felt angry and jealous. He wanted to pet the dog too, but he did not have any snacks to give. He thought of his jam in his room. He wished he had brought some jam with him. He thought the dog would like jam more than carrots. He thought he could make the dog like him more than Lily. He decided to go back to his room and get some jam.

He told his mom, "Mom, I need to go to the bathroom. Can I go back to the room?" His mom said, "Okay, but hurry back. Don't be long." Timmy nodded and ran to the room. He did not go to the bathroom. He went to his closet and took out his jar of jam. He opened it and smelled it. It was sweet and sticky. He licked his lips and said, "This is the best jam ever. The dog will love it. Then the dog will be my friend and not Lily's." He took a spoon and scooped some jam. He put it in his pocket and ran back to the park.

He saw Lily and the dog still playing. He walked up to them and said, "Hi, Lily. Hi, doggy. Can I play with you?" Lily said, "Sure, Timmy. This is a nice doggy. He likes carrots. Do you have any carrots?" Timmy said, "No, I don't have any carrots. But I have something better. I have jam. Do you want some jam, doggy?" He took out the spoon with jam and showed it to the dog. The dog sniffed the jam and barked. He did not like jam. He liked carrots. He thought the jam was yucky and bad. He growled at Timmy and bit his hand. Timmy screamed and dropped the spoon. The jam spilled on the ground and on his clothes. He cried and said, "Ow, ow, ow! The dog bit me! The dog bit me!" His mom heard him and ran to him. She saw the blood and the jam and the dog. She said, "Oh, Timmy, what did you do? Why did you bring jam to the park? Why did you try to feed the dog jam? You know dogs don't like jam. You know jam is for people, not for dogs. You were naughty and foolish. Now you are hurt and messy. Come on, let's go to the nurse and clean you up." She took Timmy by the hand and led him away. Lily followed them and said, "Bye, doggy. Thank you for playing with me. You are a good doggy. I hope you are not in trouble. I hope you find more carrots." The dog barked and wagged its tail. He licked Lily's face and bowed his head. He was sorry for biting Timmy, but he was glad for meeting Lily. He liked Lily. She was a nice girl. She liked carrots. He liked carrots. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny was very cute and adorable. One day, Benny went on a tour of the forest. He hopped from tree to tree and saw many animals along the way. 

Suddenly, Benny saw a big carrot patch. He hopped over to it and started eating the carrots. They were so yummy! But then he heard a loud noise. It was the farmer who owned the carrot patch. 

Benny quickly hopped away and continued his tour of the forest. He saw birds flying and squirrels playing. It was a fun adventure for Benny. When he got back home, he was tired but happy. Benny fell asleep dreaming of all the fun he had on his tour.

Jenny and John were walking in the park one day. They saw a machine and Jenny became excited. "Let's play on it," said Jenny.
John saw how competitive the machine was and said, "Do you think you can beat it?"
Jenny smiled and said confidently, "Yes, I can beat it. Watch me!"
But as soon as Jenny started playing, the machine started to make loud noises and lights flashed on it. As it got louder, Jenny got scared and ran away. 
John laughed and went to the machine. He played and beat it easily. Jenny was surprised and said, "You really scared the machine!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy sailboat in the pond near her house. One day, Lily's friend Billy came over to play. 

"Can I borrow your sailboat, Lily?" asked Billy.

"Sure, but be careful with it," replied Lily.

Billy took the sailboat and started playing with it. Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew the boat away. Billy tried to catch it, but it was too far. 

"Oh no, Lily's sailboat is gone!" cried Billy.

"Don't worry, we can find it together," said Lily. They searched and searched, but they couldn't find the sailboat anywhere. 

Just when they were about to give up, they saw something funny in the pond. It was Lily's sailboat, stuck in some weeds. They were so happy to find it, and they sailed it back to shore together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to eat cherries. She thought they were very delicious. One day, her mom gave her a big bowl of cherries to eat.

Sue was so happy. She sat down and started to eat the cherries one by one. She liked how they were red and sweet. She ate and ate until there was just one cherry left.

Sue wanted to finish all the cherries in the bowl. She picked up the last cherry and ate it. It was the most delicious cherry of all. Sue was very full and happy. She thanked her mom for the yummy cherries and went to play outside.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play together. They have a big toy mountain. They put cars and animals on the mountain.

One day, Sara and Tom have a fight. Sara wants the red car. Tom wants the red car too. They pull the car. The car breaks. Sara and Tom are sad and angry. They separate the mountain. Sara takes one half. Tom takes the other half. They do not talk to each other.

Mama sees Sara and Tom. She asks them what is wrong. Sara and Tom tell her about the car and the mountain. Mama says, "I am sorry the car broke. But you can still share the mountain. The mountain is big enough for both of you. You can have fun together. You are nice friends."

Sara and Tom think about what Mama says. They feel sorry for the fight. They miss each other. They say sorry to each other. They hug. They put the mountain together again. They play with the cars and the animals. They are happy. Mama smiles. She is proud of Sara and Tom.
